words.en: The severity of something is the degree to which it is serious or severe.

words.tr:
adj. 起改革作用的；感化的
n. 少年犯管教所；青少年教养院
words.ex: The new law is a reformatory step toward justice.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律是迈向正义的改革性举措。
words.en: A reformatory is a type of prison where young people who have committed crimes are sent to be reformed.

words.ex: His calm temperament helps him stay peaceful in stress.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的性情让他在压力下保持平和。
words.en: Your temperament is your basic nature, especially as it is shown in the way that you react to situations or to other people.

words.tr:
adj. 失职的；违法的；拖欠债务的
n. 违犯者；少年罪犯；违法者
words.ex: The delinquent worker ignored his duties.
words.ex_cn: 这位失职的员工忽视了他的职责。
words.en: A delinquent is someone, especially a young person, who commits a crime or breaks the law.

words.ex: He escaped from servitude and found freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他逃离了奴役，获得了自由。
words.en: The state of being a slave or completely subject to someone more powerful.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.tr: n. 强迫；强制；难以抗拒的冲动
words.ex: He felt a compulsion to check the door again.
words.ex_cn: 他感到一种必须再次检查门的强迫感。
words.en: A compulsion is a very strong desire to do something, which you find difficult to control.

words.ex: He is stubborn and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很顽固，不肯改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is stubborn is determined to do what they want and is very unwilling to change their mind.

words.ex: He tries to procure food for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他努力为家人获取食物。
words.en: To obtain something, especially with care or effort.

words.ex: He didn't flinch when the needle touched his skin.
words.ex_cn: 当针碰到他的皮肤时，他没有退缩。
words.en: If you flinch, you make a small sudden movement, especially when something surprises you or hurts you.

words.tr:
adj. 偏执狂的；患妄想狂的；过分猜疑的
n. 偏执狂患者；妄想症患者
words.ex: He is paranoid that someone is watching him.
words.ex_cn: 他总觉得有人在监视他。
words.en: If you say that someone is paranoid, you mean that they are extremely suspicious and afraid of other people.

words.ex: The hull of the boat was damaged by the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 船的船体被岩石损坏了。
words.en: The main body of a ship or other vessel, including the bottom, sides, and deck but not the masts, superstructure, rigging, engines, and other fittings.

words.ex: The rooster crows every morning.
words.ex_cn: 公鸡每天早上打鸣。
words.en: A rooster is an adult male chicken.

words.tr:
n. 导管；管道；管子
v. 通过管道输送
words.ex: The air flows through the duct.
words.ex_cn: 空气通过管道流动。
words.en: A duct is a pipe or tube through which liquid or gas flows.

words.ex: The farmer tried to exterminate the rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫试图消灭老鼠。
words.en: To exterminate means to kill all the members of a group of people or animals, or to destroy something completely.

words.tr:
v. 刺；戳；捅；用拳猛击
n. 刺；戳；捅；猛击
words.ex: He gave a quick jab to his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他给了对手一记快速的刺拳。
words.en: To poke or thrust sharply; to make a quick, sharp punch.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄
n. 嘲笑；讥笑的言语
words.ex: The crowd began to jeer at the losing team.
words.ex_cn: 观众开始对落败的队伍嘘声四起。
words.en: To jeer means to laugh at someone or shout rude remarks at them in order to show that you do not respect them.

words.ex: He unraveled the knotted string.
words.ex_cn: 他把打结的绳子拆散了。
words.en: To unravel means to separate or disentangle the threads of a fabric or a rope, or to solve or explain something that is complicated or mysterious.

words.tr:
n. 保险业；证券包销
v. 承担经济责任；承保；承销；“underwrite”的现在分词
words.ex: The bank's underwriting department approved the loan.
words.ex_cn: 银行的承保部门批准了这笔贷款。
words.en: The activity of guaranteeing to buy all the new shares that a company is issuing if no one else buys them, or the activity of providing insurance.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说
words.ex: He understated the cost of the repair.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写了维修的费用。
words.en: If you understate something, you describe it in a way that suggests it is less important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: He read an anthology of short stories last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚读了一本短篇故事选集。
words.en: An anthology is a collection of writings, such as poems or stories, that have been chosen by someone because they are considered to be the best or most interesting examples of their kind.

words.ex: He is studying anthropology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学里学习人类学。
words.en: Anthropology is the study of human societies and cultures and their development.

words.ex: The doctor gave him an antidote for the poison.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一种解毒剂来对抗毒药。
words.en: An antidote is a substance that counteracts the effects of poison or something harmful.

words.tr: n. 装饰船头的人像；傀儡领袖；有名无实的首脑；
words.ex: The old ship had a wooden figurehead of a lion.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船的船头有一个木制的狮子像。
words.en: A figurehead is a person who is the head of an organization or country in name only, without any real power or authority.

words.ex: The actors stood in front of the backdrop with a mountain scene.
words.ex_cn: 演员们站在有山景的背景幕布前。
words.en: A backdrop is a large piece of cloth, often with scenery or buildings painted on it, that is hung at the back of a stage in a theatre.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.tr: v. 使士气低落；使失去斗志
words.ex: The bad news demoralized the team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息使团队士气低落。
words.en: If something demoralizes someone, it makes them lose so much confidence in what they are doing that they want to give up.

words.ex: The car depreciates every year.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车每年都会贬值。
words.en: If something such as a currency depreciates or if something depreciates it, it loses some of its original value.

words.tr:
n. 门闩；碰锁；弹簧锁
v. 用闩闩上；用碰锁锁上
words.ex: The door has a simple latch to keep it closed.
words.ex_cn: 这扇门有一个简单的门闩来保持关闭。
words.en: A latch is a fastening for a door or gate, consisting of a bar that is lifted from its catch, groove, or hole by a lever, or that slides or is pushed into place.

words.tr: n. 露天历史剧；盛装游行（或庆典）；选美比赛
words.ex: The town held a pageant to show the history of the old kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇举办了一场露天历史剧，以展示古老王国的历史。
words.en: A pageant is a public entertainment consisting of a procession of people in elaborate, colorful costumes, or an outdoor performance of a historical scene.

words.ex: He wavers when choosing between two jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他在两个工作之间摇摆不定。
words.en: If you waver, you cannot decide about something or you are uncertain about what you should do.

words.ex: The candle's flicker lit up the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛的闪现照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: If a light or flame flickers, it shines unsteadily.

words.tr: v. 消灭；歼灭；彻底击败
words.ex: The bomb will annihilate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To annihilate something means to destroy it completely.

words.ex: They paid five dollars apiece for the tickets.
words.ex_cn: 他们每人五美元买了票。
words.en: If something is given or sold apiece, each person is given or sold one, or each thing is sold for a particular amount.

words.ex: He is bashful when he speaks in front of people.
words.ex_cn: 当他当着大家说话时，他很害羞。
words.en: If someone is bashful, they are shy and easily embarrassed.

words.ex: She replenished the water bottle after the hike.
words.ex_cn: 她在徒步后补充了水瓶里的水。
words.en: If you replenish something, you make it full or complete again.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

words.tr: adj. 令人不安的；令人慌张的；令人窘迫的； v. “disconcert”的现在分词；
words.ex: The loud noise was disconcerting.
words.ex_cn: 那阵响声令人不安。
words.en: If you say that something is disconcerting, you mean that it makes you feel anxious, confused, or embarrassed.

words.tr:
n. 有志者；立志…的人
adj. 有野心的；有抱负的
words.ex: He is an aspirant for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他是这份工作的求职者。
words.en: An aspirant is someone who is ambitious and eager to achieve a particular goal or position.

words.ex: The pastoral man tends his sheep on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧人在山上照看他的羊。
words.en: Relating to the countryside or to the work of a shepherd; idyllically rural.

words.tr:
adj. 起作用的；运作中的
n. 技工；密探；特工
words.ex: The operative plan is to start tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 实施的计划是明天开始。
words.en: An operative system or plan is one that is in use or being used. An operative is someone who works for a government agency or a private company, often doing secret or confidential work.

words.ex: Each participant must sign the form.
words.ex_cn: 每个参与者都必须签署表格。
words.en: A participant is someone who takes part in an activity or event.

words.tr: adj. 不熟练的，不内行的
words.ex: He is inexpert at fixing cars.
words.ex_cn: 他修车不太在行。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as inexpert, you mean that they show a lack of skill.

words.ex: He wants to circumnavigate the world by boat.
words.ex_cn: 他想乘船环游世界。
words.en: To circumnavigate means to travel all the way around the entire Earth or an island.

words.ex: He showed his portfolio to the art teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向美术老师展示了他作品集。
words.en: A portfolio is a set of pictures by someone, or photographs of examples of their work, which they use when entering competitions or applying for work.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.ex: They parked the caravan by the lake for the weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他们把旅行拖车停在湖边过周末。
words.en: A caravan is a group of people, especially traders or pilgrims, traveling together across a desert in Asia or North Africa.

words.ex: He is facing litigation over the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他因合同问题面临诉讼。
words.en: Litigation is the process of taking legal action or bringing a lawsuit in a court of law.

words.tr: n. 地方法官；治安官；行政官；
words.ex: The magistrate decided the small case quickly.
words.ex_cn: 地方法官迅速裁决了这起小案件。
words.en: A magistrate is an official who acts as a judge in law courts that deal with minor crimes or disputes.

words.ex: He signed the affidavit before the lawyer.
words.ex_cn: 他在律师面前签署了宣誓书。
words.en: A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation, for use as evidence in court.

words.tr: n. 植物区系；植物群（flora 的变形）
words.ex: The florae in the rainforest are very diverse.
words.ex_cn: 雨林中的植物群非常多样。
words.en: The plants of a particular region, habitat, or geological period.

words.tr:
n. 泡菜；腌菜；腌汁；腌制品；困境
v. 腌制（泡菜等）
words.ex: He put a pickle on his sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他在三明治上放了一颗酸黄瓜。
words.en: A pickle is a vegetable or fruit that has been preserved in vinegar or salt water, or a difficult situation.

words.tr: n. 好友；密友；任人唯亲
words.ex: He went to lunch with his crony after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后和好友一起去吃午饭。
words.en: A crony is a close friend or companion.

words.ex: He gave a quick answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对问题给出了一个快速的回答。
words.en: Moving fast or doing something in a short time.

words.ex: He planted carrots in a small patch.
words.ex_cn: 他在一小块地上种了胡萝卜。
words.en: A patch is a piece of material used to mend a hole or a weak spot in something, or a small area that is different from the area around it.

words.tr: adj. 无法解释的；费解的
words.ex: His sudden silence was inexplicable.
words.ex_cn: 他突然的沉默无法解释。
words.en: If something is inexplicable, you cannot explain why it happens or why it is true.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.ex: The preamble explains the purpose of the law.
words.ex_cn: 序言解释了法律的目的。
words.en: A preamble is an introduction to a speech or piece of writing, especially one that explains what follows.

words.ex: He tried to dissuade her from quitting her job.
words.ex_cn: 他试图劝她不要辞掉工作。
words.en: If you dissuade someone from doing something, you persuade them not to do it.

words.ex: He was accused of poaching ideas from his colleague.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控盗用同事的想法。
words.en: To poach means to illegally hunt or catch animals or fish, or to cook something such as an egg without its shell in or over boiling water.

words.ex: They crossed the river on a wooden raft.
words.ex_cn: 他们乘着木筏渡过了河。
words.en: A raft is a flat structure made of pieces of wood tied together, which is used as a boat or floating platform.

words.ex: The ram broke down the wooden door.
words.ex_cn: 撞击装置撞碎了木门。
words.en: A ram is an adult male sheep. As a verb, it means to force something into a place or to hit something with great force.

words.tr: n. 护林员；公园看管人；突击队员；
words.ex: The ranger walked through the forest to check for fires.
words.ex_cn: 护林员在森林里巡逻，检查是否有火灾。
words.en: A ranger is someone whose job is to look after a forest or a large park.

words.tr:
n. 抽奖售物
v. 抽奖赠送（货品）
words.ex: He bought a ticket for the raffle.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一张抽奖票。
words.en: A raffle is a type of lottery in which people buy tickets for a chance to win a prize.

words.ex: The vacuum cleaner uses suction to pick up dust.
words.ex_cn: 吸尘器利用吸力来吸走灰尘。
words.en: Suction is the process by which liquids, gases, or small particles are drawn into a space or device because the pressure inside is lower than the pressure outside.

words.ex: The subtlety of her smile made everyone curious.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的微妙之处让所有人都感到好奇。
words.en: The quality of being subtle, especially in a way that is difficult to notice or understand.

words.tr:
n. 施舍品；失业救济金
v. 发放救济
words.ex: The government gives dole to the unemployed.
words.ex_cn: 政府向失业者提供救济金。
words.en: Money or food given by a government to people who are poor and have no other way of getting money or food.

words.ex: The submarine uses sonar to find objects underwater.
words.ex_cn: 潜艇使用声呐来发现水下的物体。
words.en: Sonar is a system for detecting objects under water by emitting sound pulses and detecting or measuring their return after being reflected.

words.ex: The storm caused great scathe to the crops.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对庄稼造成了严重危害。
words.en: To scathe means to harm or damage something or someone, either physically or emotionally.

words.ex: The church runs an outreach to help homeless people.
words.ex_cn: 这家教堂开展外展服务来帮助无家可归者。
words.en: Outreach refers to the activity of an organization that provides a service or advice to people in the community, especially those who cannot or are unlikely to come to an office, a hospital, etc. for help.

words.ex: The farmers work in the paddy every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农民每天早上都在稻田里劳作。
words.en: A paddy is a field in which rice is grown. It is typically flooded with water.

words.tr:
n. 异教徒；无宗教信仰者
adj. 异教的；异教徒的；无宗教信仰的
words.ex: He lived in a pagan village long ago.
words.ex_cn: 他很久以前住在一个异教村庄里。
words.en: A pagan is someone who worships many gods or no god, especially one who belongs to a religion that existed before Christianity.

words.ex: The statue has a strong torso.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像有一个强壮的躯干。
words.en: The main part of the human body, not including the head, arms, or legs.

words.ex: He sings gospel music every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日唱福音音乐。
words.en: The teachings of Jesus and the apostles, especially as contained in the first four books of the New Testament, known as the Gospels.

words.ex: He gave his mother a massage after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后给妈妈做了按摩。
words.en: The act of rubbing and pressing someone's body with the hands to reduce tension or pain in the muscles.

words.ex: He works in lexicography at a dictionary company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家词典公司从事词典编纂工作。
words.en: Lexicography is the activity or profession of writing dictionaries.

words.tr: adj. 可笑的；荒谬的；滑稽的
words.ex: It is ludicrous to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套真是荒谬。
words.en: If you describe something as ludicrous, you are emphasizing that you think it is foolish, unreasonable, or unsuitable.

words.tr: adj. 恶毒的；恶性的；恶意的
words.ex: His malignant words hurt everyone around him.
words.ex_cn: 他恶毒的话语伤害了周围的所有人。
words.en: If you say that someone is malignant, you mean they are very dangerous and cause harm to people.

words.tr:
n. 刺刀；卡销
v. 用刺刀刺
words.ex: The soldier fixed a bayonet to his rifle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵把刺刀装到了步枪上。
words.en: A bayonet is a long, sharp blade that can be attached to the end of a rifle and used as a weapon in close combat.

words.tr: v. 诱骗；消遣；迷住；消磨
words.ex: He beguiles her with sweet words.
words.ex_cn: 他用甜言蜜语哄骗她。
words.en: If someone beguiles you, they charm you in a way that makes you trust them or like them, often so that they can deceive you.

words.ex: He deluded himself into thinking he would win.
words.ex_cn: 他欺骗自己，以为自己会赢。
words.en: If you delude yourself, you let yourself believe that something is true, even though it is not true.

words.tr:
n. 大洪水；暴雨；泛滥
v. 泛滥；大量涌入
words.ex: The rain caused a deluge in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨在镇上引发了洪水。
words.en: A deluge is a severe flood or a very heavy fall of rain that causes a lot of damage.

words.tr: adj. 唱诗班的；合唱队的；合唱的
words.ex: The children sing in a choral group.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在一个合唱团里唱歌。
words.en: Relating to a choir or chorus; sung or performed by a choir.

words.ex: The statue was colossal, taller than the building.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像巨大，比大楼还高。
words.en: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.ex: The colt runs fast across the field.
words.ex_cn: 小马在田野上快速奔跑。
words.en: A colt is a young male horse, especially one that is less than four years old.

words.tr: adj. 寒冷的；冷淡的；性冷淡的（女子）
words.ex: The water is frigid in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的水很冰冷。
words.en: Frigid means extremely cold in temperature or lacking warmth or enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；衷心的；诚挚的；
words.ex: He is a devout Christian who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名虔诚的基督徒，每周日都去教堂。
words.en: If you describe someone as devout, you mean that they have a deep religious faith.

words.tr: n. 异常事物；反常现象；
words.ex: The strange weather this month is an anomaly.
words.ex_cn: 这个月奇怪的天气是一个异常现象。
words.en: Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.tr: adj. 在职的；负有义务的；
words.ex: The incumbent mayor won the election again.
words.ex_cn: 现任市长再次赢得了选举。
words.en: An incumbent is someone who currently holds a particular office or position, especially in politics. It can also refer to something that is necessary as a duty or responsibility.

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

words.tr: v. 对…表示极不赞成；强烈反对；轻视
words.ex: They deprecate old software.
words.ex_cn: 他们不推荐使用旧软件。
words.en: If you deprecate something, you criticize it or express your disapproval of it.

words.tr: adj. 休眠的；蛰伏的；暂停活动的
words.ex: The volcano is dormant now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Something that is dormant is not active or growing but has the ability to be active at a later time.

words.ex: The acme of his career was winning the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他职业生涯的顶点是获得诺贝尔奖。
words.en: The highest point of achievement or excellence.

words.tr: v. 迅速生长；急速增长
words.ex: The flowers burgeon in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，花朵绽放。
words.en: To grow or develop quickly; to flourish.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.ex: This medicine is efficacious for colds.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒有效。
words.en: An efficacious method or treatment is one that has the ability to produce a desired effect or result.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.tr: v. 传播；“diffuse”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The scent diffused through the room.
words.ex_cn: 香味弥漫了整个房间。
words.en: Spread over a wide area or between a large number of people.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

words.tr:
int. 喂；哈喽；
n. “喂”的招呼声或问候声；
words.ex: Hello, can you hear me?
words.ex_cn: 喂，你能听到我吗？
words.en: used as a greeting or to begin a telephone conversation

words.ex: The statue represents the divinity of the ancient gods.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像代表了古代众神的神性。
words.en: Divinity refers to the state or quality of being divine, or a divine being. It can also refer to the study of religion or theology.

words.ex: Jesus is central to Christian beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 耶稣是基督教信仰的核心。
words.en: Jesus is the central figure of Christianity, believed by Christians to be the Son of God and the savior of humanity.

words.tr: adj. 同等的；相等的；相当于
words.ex: Lying is tantamount to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎等于欺骗。
words.en: If you say that one thing is tantamount to a second, more serious thing, you are emphasizing how bad, unacceptable, or unfortunate the first thing is by comparing it to the second.

words.ex: He was accused of heresy for rejecting the church's teachings.
words.ex_cn: 他因拒绝教会的教义而被指控为异端。
words.en: Heresy is a belief or opinion that is contrary to the orthodox religious doctrine, especially in Christianity.

words.ex: The circles are concentric and share the same center.
words.ex_cn: 这些圆是同心的，拥有同一个中心。
words.en: Having a common center, as circles or spheres.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.tr: v. 使风格化； 仿效 ... 的风格；符合（传统）程式
words.ex: The artist stylize the flowers with bold lines.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家用粗线条使花朵风格化。
words.en: To stylize something means to design or represent it according to a particular style, especially in art or literature.

words.ex: He studied hard, thereby passing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习，因此通过了考试。
words.en: You use thereby to introduce an important result or consequence of the event or action you have just mentioned.

words.ex: This is his first foray into painting.
words.ex_cn: 这是他首次涉足绘画。
words.en: A foray is a sudden and brief incursion or attack into enemy territory, especially to obtain something; a raid. It can also refer to an initial attempt to become involved in a different activity or profession.

words.tr: adj. 狡猾的；诡计多端的
words.ex: The wily fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as wily, you mean that they are clever at achieving what they want, especially by tricking people.

words.tr: adj. 沉默寡言的；讳莫如深的
words.ex: He is reticent about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的感受很沉默。
words.en: If you are reticent about something, you are unwilling to talk about it or make your feelings known.

words.ex: The apex of the mountain is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 山的最高点被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or top of something; the climax or culmination of something.

words.ex: Noah built an ark to save animals from the flood.
words.ex_cn: 诺亚建造了一艘方舟来拯救动物免受洪水之灾。
words.en: An ark is a large boat mentioned in the Bible, built by Noah to save his family and two of every kind of animal from the Flood.

words.tr:
v. 钉牢；用臂互抱；达成（协议等）；最终解决
n. 钉牢；扭抱
words.ex: He clinched the board to the wall with nails.
words.ex_cn: 他用钉子把木板钉在墙上。
words.en: To settle something conclusively; to secure or fasten something by flattening the ends of nails, screws, etc.

words.tr:
n. 谷歌（网络搜索引擎）；
vt. 用搜索引擎搜索（尤指用谷歌搜索引擎）；
words.ex: I use Google to find information online.
words.ex_cn: 我使用谷歌在网上查找信息。
words.en: To use the Google search engine to find information on the internet.

words.ex: The hikers walked through a deep gorge.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者走过一个深峡谷。
words.en: A gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides, often carved by a river. It can also refer to the act of eating greedily.

words.tr: v. 跨坐；骑；分腿站立；横跨
words.ex: The boy straddled the fence to see the game.
words.ex_cn: 男孩跨坐在围栏上观看比赛。
words.en: To sit or stand with one leg on each side of something; to extend over or across something; to take a non-committal position on an issue.

words.tr: v. 遣散；（使）复员；使退伍
words.ex: The army will demobilize after the war ends.
words.ex_cn: 战争结束后，军队将解散。
words.en: To demobilize is to release someone from military service, especially at the end of a war.

words.tr:
n. 呼喊；高呼
v. 叫喊；高呼
words.ex: The crowd let out a loud whoop when the team scored.
words.ex_cn: 当球队得分时，观众发出了一声大声的呼喊。
words.en: A whoop is a loud, excited shout, often expressing joy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: He used to rove through the forests when he was young.
words.ex_cn: 他年轻时常常在森林里漫游。
words.en: To rove means to travel constantly without a fixed destination; wander.

words.ex: There was a large influx of tourists during the summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天期间涌入了大量游客。
words.en: An influx of people or things is a large number of them arriving somewhere at the same time.

words.ex: The inflow of water filled the tank quickly.
words.ex_cn: 水的流入很快填满了水箱。
words.en: The movement of a substance into a place or system.

words.tr: n. （阿拉伯的）酋长；（伊斯兰教）教主
words.ex: The sheik lives in a large desert tent.
words.ex_cn: 这位酋长住在一座大型沙漠帐篷里。
words.en: A sheik is an Arab leader, in particular the chief or head of an Arab tribe, family, or village.

words.tr:
adj. 裸体的
n. 裸体；裸体画；裸体像
words.ex: He painted a nude woman by the window.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一位在窗边的裸体女性。
words.en: A nude person is not wearing any clothes. A nude painting or sculpture shows a person who is not wearing any clothes.

words.ex: The umpire blew the whistle when the player broke the rule.
words.ex_cn: 当球员犯规时，裁判吹响了哨子。
words.en: An umpire is a person whose job is to make sure that a game is played fairly and that the rules are not broken.

words.ex: He ate a plate of steamed mussels for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚餐吃了一盘蒸贻贝。
words.en: A mussel is a small sea creature that has a dark shell with two parts that close tightly together. Mussels are often eaten as food.

words.tr: n. 传闻；谣传；道听途说
words.ex: He believed the hearsay without checking the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他没有核实事实就相信了这些流言。
words.en: Information received from other people that one cannot adequately substantiate; rumor.

words.tr: adj. 多边的；多国参加的
words.ex: The multilateral agreement helped many countries work together.
words.ex_cn: 这个多边协议帮助许多国家共同合作。
words.en: Involving or agreed upon by three or more parties, especially the governments of different countries.

words.ex: The small village lies on the periphery of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄位于城市的外围。
words.en: The outer limits or edge of an area or object.

words.ex: Honesty is a good trait.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种好的特性。
words.en: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.

words.ex: The doctor used drops to dilate her pupils.
words.ex_cn: 医生用了滴眼液来扩大她的瞳孔。
words.en: If you dilate something such as a part of your body, or if it dilates, it becomes larger or wider.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.tr:
adj. 可怕的；恐怖的；惨白的；令人不快的
adv. 可怖地；惨白地
words.ex: The ghost looked ghastly in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 那个幽灵在黑暗中看起来吓人极了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as ghastly, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant or shocking.

words.tr: adj. 使人晕眩的；头晕的；轻浮的
words.ex: She felt giddy after spinning around.
words.ex_cn: 她转圈后感到头晕目眩。
words.en: If you feel giddy, you feel unsteady and think that you are about to fall over, usually because you are not well or because you are excited or frightened.

words.ex: He is loitering near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他正在公园附近闲逛。
words.en: If someone loiters somewhere, they remain there or walk up and down without any real purpose.

words.tr:
n. 掠夺物；掠夺；赃物
v. 掠夺；洗劫
words.ex: The pirates found loot on the sunken ship.
words.ex_cn: 海盗们在沉船中找到了战利品。
words.en: Loot refers to goods stolen from a place, especially during a war or riot. It can also mean to steal goods from a place, especially during a war or riot.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；开玩笑的；闹着玩的
words.ex: He told a jocose joke to make everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个幽默的笑话来让大家笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as jocose, you mean that they are playful and humorous.

words.ex: The phone is expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机很贵。
words.en: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.

words.ex: The inert gas does not react with other elements.
words.ex_cn: 这种惰性气体不与其他元素发生反应。
words.en: If someone or something is inert, they are not moving or reacting in any way.

words.ex: He won't divulge the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不会泄露这个秘密。
words.en: If you divulge a piece of secret or private information, you tell it to someone.

words.ex: The smell of food whetted his appetite.
words.ex_cn: 食物的香味刺激了他的食欲。
words.en: To whet something means to make it sharper or more intense.

words.ex: He cooked the meal with gusto.
words.ex_cn: 他做这顿饭时很有兴趣。
words.en: If you do something with gusto, you do it with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr: n. 昏迷；不省人事；恍惚
words.ex: He fell into a stupor after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，他陷入了昏迷状态。
words.en: A state of near-unconsciousness or insensibility.

words.ex: He is an astute businessman who always makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他是个精明的商人，总是做出明智的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as astute, you think they are clever and can see through things quickly and make good judgments.

words.tr:
n. 皱眉蹙额；退缩
v. 皱眉蹙额；退避
words.ex: He let out a wince when he touched his sore arm.
words.ex_cn: 当他碰触到疼痛的手臂时，他皱了一下眉。
words.en: If you wince, you make a slight, sudden movement of your face, especially when you are in pain or when you see or hear something unpleasant.

words.ex: His calmness is the antithesis of her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他的冷静是她愤怒的反面。
words.en: The antithesis of something is its exact opposite.

words.ex: The old house looked dilapidated after years of neglect.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子因多年疏于维护而显得残破。
words.en: A building that is dilapidated is old and in a generally bad condition.

words.ex: He is a novice at playing the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吉他新手。
words.en: A novice is someone who has just started learning or doing something and does not have much experience.

words.ex: He is downright lazy.
words.ex_cn: 他完全懒惰。
words.en: You use downright to emphasize that something is completely the case, especially when you are describing something bad or negative.

words.tr: n. （证明品质的）优良标志；崇高的社会地位；声望；威望
words.ex: Wearing that brand gives him cachet.
words.ex_cn: 穿那个品牌让他有声望。
words.en: Cachet refers to a quality or characteristic that makes someone or something seem special or respected.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的；可靠的
words.ex: His unimpeachable honesty earned everyone's trust.
words.ex_cn: 他无可挑剔的诚实赢得了每个人的信任。
words.en: If you describe someone as unimpeachable, you mean that they are completely honest and reliable.

words.ex: He remained imperturbable even when the storm hit.
words.ex_cn: 即使风暴来袭，他依然镇定自若。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperturbable, you mean that they remain calm, even in disturbing or dangerous situations.

words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.ex: This high heel is too tall.
words.ex_cn: 这只高跟鞋太高了。
words.en: A high heel is a type of shoe in which the heel is significantly higher off the ground than the toes, making the wearer appear taller and often changing their posture.

words.ex: This apple is a variant of the red delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这种苹果是红富士的一个变体。
words.en: A variant is something that is slightly different from other similar things.

words.tr:
n. 狂乱；狂暴；狂怒
v. 使狂乱；使狂怒
words.ex: The crowd went into a frenzy when the singer appeared.
words.ex_cn: 当歌手出现时，人群陷入了狂热。
words.en: A frenzy is a state of uncontrolled excitement or wild behavior.

words.ex: The dove is an emblem of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征。
words.en: An emblem is a design that represents a country, organization, or family.

words.ex: He gave her an abusive shout.
words.ex_cn: 他对她大喊大叫，态度虐待。
words.en: If someone is abusive, they use rude and insulting words or behave violently towards someone else.

words.ex: He is on probation for one year.
words.ex_cn: 他被判缓刑一年。
words.en: Probation is a period of time during which someone who has committed a crime has to behave well and not commit any more crimes in order to avoid being sent to prison.

words.ex: She sings as a soprano in the opera choir.
words.ex_cn: 她在歌剧合唱团中担任女高音。
words.en: A soprano is a type of classical female singing voice and has the highest vocal range of all voice types.

words.tr:
adj. 用柏油覆盖的
v. 耽搁；逗留
words.ex: The workers tarry at the road, waiting for the asphalt to dry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在道路上耽搁，等着沥青变干。
words.en: To tarry means to stay longer than intended or to delay leaving a place.

words.ex: The city's sprawl has covered many farmlands.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的杂乱无序的拓展覆盖了许多农田。
words.en: If you sprawl somewhere, you sit or lie with your legs and arms spread out in a careless way.

words.ex: He passed the test by a fluke.
words.ex_cn: 他靠运气通过了考试。
words.en: A fluke is an unexpected stroke of good luck or a surprising success that happens by chance.

words.ex: He has a knack for fixing bikes.
words.ex_cn: 他有修自行车的技巧。
words.en: A knack is a special skill or ability that someone has, especially one that is hard to explain or teach.

words.ex: He ate venison at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚宴上吃了鹿肉。
words.en: The flesh of a deer used as food.

words.ex: The government decided to deregulate the airline industry.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定解除对航空业的管制。
words.en: To remove regulations or controls from something, especially an industry or sector.

words.ex: The manager decided to demote him for poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 经理因他表现不佳决定降职他。
words.en: If someone is demoted, they are given a lower rank or a less important position than they had before.

words.ex: The police told everyone to evacuate the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察让所有人撤离大楼。
words.en: To evacuate means to remove people from a place of danger to a safer place.

words.ex: Workers excavate the old ruins with shovels.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用铲子挖掘古代遗址。
words.en: To excavate means to dig in the ground in order to find things that have been buried there, such as archaeological remains.

words.tr:
adj. 秘密工作的；暗中做的
adv. 秘密地；暗中进行
words.ex: The police worked undercover to catch the thieves.
words.ex_cn: 警察卧底工作以抓捕小偷。
words.en: Involved in or relating to secret work within a community or organization, especially in the gathering of information.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: He spoke in the guise of a friend.
words.ex_cn: 他以朋友的伪装说话。
words.en: An external form, appearance, or manner of presentation, typically concealing the true nature of something.

words.ex: The projection of the movie started at 8 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 电影的放映晚上8点开始。
words.en: A projection is an estimate or forecast of a future situation or trend based on a study of present ones.

words.ex: The book begins with a short prologue.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以一个简短的序言开始。
words.en: A prologue is an introduction to a book, play, or other written work that sets the scene or provides background information.

words.ex: The old woman prophesied rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预告明天会下雨。
words.en: To say that something will happen in the future, especially as a result of divine inspiration.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.ex: She bought some earthenware pots at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上买了一些陶器。
words.en: Earthenware is pottery that has not been fired to the point of vitrification and is thus porous and coarser than porcelain or stoneware.

words.tr: n. 小袋；囊状袋；育儿袋；
words.ex: The kangaroo carries its baby in a pouch.
words.ex_cn: 袋鼠把幼崽放在小袋里。
words.en: A pouch is a small, flexible bag, typically made of leather or fabric, used for carrying small items.

words.tr:
n. 楔子；三角木；楔形物
v. 把…楔住 ；将…挤入（或塞进、插入）
words.ex: He used a wedge to split the wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用楔子把木头劈开。
words.en: A wedge is a piece of wood, metal, or other material with one thick end and one thin edge, used to keep something in position or to split something apart.

words.tr:
adj. 假装的；不真实的
v. 假装；装作；“feign”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He feigned sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone's behaviour or emotion is feigned, it is not genuine or sincere, but is pretended for effect.

words.tr: n. 令人讨厌的或繁重的工作；
words.ex: Washing dishes is a boring chore.
words.ex_cn: 洗碗是一件烦人的琐事。
words.en: A chore is a task or piece of work that is often boring or unpleasant but needs to be done regularly.

words.ex: She bought new apparel for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了新衣服。
words.en: Clothing, especially outer garments; attire.

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.tr: adj. 严格的；缜密的；严密的；
words.ex: The teacher is rigorous about homework deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业截止日期要求严格。
words.en: If you are rigorous in something, you are very thorough and strict in the way you do it.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.ex: He is adroit at fixing broken machines.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长修理坏掉的机器。
words.en: Someone who is adroit is quick and skillful in their thoughts, behavior, or actions.

words.tr: adj. 脱离正道的；脱离常轨的
words.ex: His aberrant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他反常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An aberrant person or thing is one that is unusual or unexpected, especially in an unwelcome way.

words.ex: They found paradise on a small island.
words.ex_cn: 他们在一个小岛上找到了天堂。
words.en: Paradise is a place of ideal beauty or loveliness, or a state of supreme happiness.

words.tr:
adj. 无足轻重的；琐碎的；极小的
v. 摆弄；虚度时光；拉小提琴；篡改；“fiddle”的现在分词
words.ex: He ignored the fiddling details and focused on the big picture.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了那些无足轻重的细节，专注于大局。
words.en: If you describe something as fiddling, you mean that it is unimportant and often involves spending too much time on small, unimportant details.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

words.ex: The politician lost his constituency after the scandal.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客在丑闻后失去了他的支持者。
words.en: A constituency is a group of people in a country or area who are entitled to vote in an election, or the area itself.

words.ex: The workers used dynamite to break the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 工人们使用炸药来炸开岩石。
words.en: Dynamite is a type of explosive that is used in mining and construction. It is also used metaphorically to describe something that is highly effective or potentially dangerous.

words.ex: He has been chronically ill since childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他从小长期患病。
words.en: In a way that continues for a long time or keeps happening, especially of a disease or problem.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.tr:
v. 轻推；轻触；劝说；鼓动
n. 轻推；轻触；劝说；鼓动
words.ex: He gave me a nudge to start the project.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻推了我一下，让我开始这个项目。
words.en: If you nudge someone, you push them gently, usually with your elbow, in order to draw their attention to something.

words.ex: The climb was perilous in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 在暴风雨中，这次攀登非常危险。
words.en: Full of danger or risk.

words.tr: n. 友好关系的恢复；和解
words.ex: The two countries began rapprochement after the war.
words.ex_cn: 两国在战争后开始和解。
words.en: An establishment or resumption of harmonious relations between two countries or groups.

words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.ex: His calm demeanor made everyone feel safe.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的举止让每个人都感到安心。
words.en: The way in which a person behaves towards others; outward behavior or bearing.

words.ex: Farmers spread manure on the fields to help crops grow.
words.ex_cn: 农民把肥料撒在田里以帮助庄稼生长。
words.en: Manure is organic matter used as fertilizer in agriculture.

words.ex: The soil has rich humus.
words.ex_cn: 这种土壤富含腐殖质。
words.en: A dark, rich, fertile soil formed by the decomposition of plant and animal matter.

words.ex: He collates the papers before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议前整理了这些文件。
words.en: To collate information or data means to collect it together and examine it carefully in order to compare it or find something out.

words.tr: v. 缓和；减弱（感觉）；降低（声音）
words.ex: The noise deadened after the door closed.
words.ex_cn: 门关上后，噪音减弱了。
words.en: If something deadens a feeling or a sound, it makes it less strong or loud.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.ex: The big black bug bit the brave boy.
words.ex_cn: 大黑虫咬了勇敢的男孩。
words.en: Alliteration is the occurrence of the same letter or sound at the beginning of adjacent or closely connected words.

words.tr: v. 起绰号；把…称作；配音；译制
words.ex: They dubbed him 'Captain Cool' for his calm style.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他冷静的风格给他起了个绰号叫‘冷静队长’。
words.en: To give a name, title, or nickname to someone or something; to provide a film or television program with a soundtrack in a different language from the original.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: He supports advocacy for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他支持清洁用水的倡导。
words.en: The act of pleading or arguing in favor of something, such as a cause, idea, or policy; active support.

words.ex: The word 'home' connotes comfort and safety.
words.ex_cn: ‘家’这个词意味着舒适和安全。
words.en: If a word or name connotes something, it makes you think of a particular idea or quality.

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.tr: v. 使变白；（脸色）变苍白；焯
words.ex: She blanches the vegetables before freezing them.
words.ex_cn: 她在冷冻蔬菜之前先焯水。
words.en: To blanch means to make something white or pale, often by removing color or by causing it to lose color. It can also refer to the process of briefly boiling vegetables and then plunging them into cold water to halt the cooking process.

words.ex: He has amnesia and cannot remember his name.
words.ex_cn: 他患有失忆症，想不起自己的名字。
words.en: Amnesia is a medical condition that affects someone's memory and they are unable to remember events or information.

words.tr:
n. 轻松说笑
v. 轻松说笑
words.ex: They enjoy banter during lunch break.
words.ex_cn: 他们在午餐休息时喜欢开玩笑。
words.en: the playful and friendly exchange of teasing remarks

words.tr: n. 狂热； 癖好；躁狂症
words.ex: He has a mania for collecting stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他痴迷于收集邮票。
words.en: An extreme enthusiasm or desire for something, often to the point of obsession.

words.tr:
n. 紫丁香；淡紫色
adj. 淡紫色的
words.ex: The lilac blooms in spring.
words.ex_cn: 丁香花在春天盛开。
words.en: A lilac is a type of shrub or small tree which has bunches of sweet-smelling pink, white, or purple flowers.

words.ex: He paid in lieu of cash.
words.ex_cn: 他用其他方式支付而不是现金。
words.en: If you do, get, or give one thing in lieu of another, you do, get, or give it instead of the other thing, because the two things are considered to have the same value or importance.

words.ex: His joke brought some levity to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话为会议带来了一些轻松气氛。
words.en: Levity refers to a lack of seriousness, especially at an inappropriate time, often characterized by frivolity or lightness of manner.

words.tr: n. 大破坏；大毁坏；大混乱；
words.ex: The storm caused havoc in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给这个小镇带来了大破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as havoc, you mean that it causes a great deal of disorder, confusion, or destruction.

words.ex: The matrix gave birth to all living things.
words.ex_cn: 母体孕育了所有生命。
words.en: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers, symbols, or expressions, arranged in rows and columns.

words.tr:
n. 漫画；讽刺画；滑稽模仿
v. 画成漫画讽刺
words.ex: He drew a caricature of the teacher with big eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一幅老师大眼睛的漫画。
words.en: A caricature is a drawing or description of someone that exaggerates their appearance or behavior in a humorous or critical way.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.ex: The dog follows its owner every day.
words.ex_cn: 狗每天跟随它的主人。
words.en: To go or come after (a person or thing proceeding ahead); move or travel behind.

words.tr: v. 打滚；躺卧；（船）颠簸；沉湎
words.ex: The pig wallow in the mud.
words.ex_cn: 猪在泥里打滚。
words.en: If you say that someone is wallowing in an unpleasant situation, you are criticizing them for being deliberately unhappy.

words.tr:
adj. 二次方的
n. 二次方程式
words.ex: He solved a quadratic equation yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天解了一个二次方程。
words.en: In mathematics, a quadratic equation is any equation that can be rearranged in standard form as ax² + bx + c = 0, where x represents an unknown, and a, b, and c represent known numbers, with a ≠ 0.

words.tr:
n. 名声；名誉；名望
v. 认为；以为
words.ex: He is of good repute in his town.
words.ex_cn: 他在镇上声誉很好。
words.en: The opinion generally held of someone or something; the state of being regarded in a particular way.

words.ex: The sentinel stands guard at the gate.
words.ex_cn: 哨兵站在门口站岗。
words.en: A sentinel is a soldier or guard whose job is to stand and keep watch.

words.tr:
n. 喷口；水管；水柱
v. 喷出；滔滔不绝地说
words.ex: The kettle has a small spout for pouring water.
words.ex_cn: 这个水壶有一个小喷口用来倒水。
words.en: If something spouts liquid or fire, or if liquid or fire spout out of something, it comes out very quickly with a lot of force.

words.ex: The chef made a deft cut with the knife.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用刀熟练地切了一下。
words.en: A deft action is skilful and often quick.

words.tr:
adj. 退步的；堕落的；腐化的
v. 退化；堕落
n. 堕落的人
words.ex: The old machine became degenerate and stopped working.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器退步了，停止工作了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something degenerates, you mean that they become worse in some way, for example, poorer, weaker, or less respectable.

words.tr: adj. 堕落的；颓废的；衰落的
words.ex: He ate a decadent chocolate cake.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块奢华的巧克力蛋糕。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as decadent, you think that they are morally corrupt or that they are living in an immoral way.

words.ex: The heavy fine is a deterrent to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款是一种威慑作弊的力量。
words.en: Something that discourages or is intended to discourage someone from doing something.

words.ex: He condescended to explain the simple math to his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他屈尊向弟弟解释了简单的数学。
words.en: If someone condescends to do something, they agree to do it in a way which shows that they think they are superior to the people they are doing it for.

words.ex: The travelers found an oasis with water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 旅行者们发现了一个有水和树木的绿洲。
words.en: An oasis is a small area in a desert where water and plants are found, making it a place of relief and beauty in an otherwise barren landscape.

words.tr: v. 罢免；废黜；宣誓证明
words.ex: The people deposed the corrupt leader.
words.ex_cn: 人民推翻了腐败的领导人。
words.en: To depose someone means to remove them from a position of power or authority, especially a monarch or political leader.

words.tr: adj. 绝望的；孤立无助的；被弃置的
words.ex: The forlorn dog sat by the door, waiting for its owner.
words.ex_cn: 那条孤单的狗坐在门边，等待它的主人。
words.en: If someone is forlorn, they feel alone and unhappy.

words.tr: n. 精神病学家；精神科医生
words.ex: He visits a psychiatrist every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周去看一次精神科医生。
words.en: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental illnesses and emotional disorders.

words.tr: adj. 反复出现的；再发生的；
words.ex: He has recurrent headaches every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周都反复出现头痛。
words.en: Happening or appearing again or repeatedly.

words.tr:
v. 感到刺痛；强烈地感到
n. 刺痛感；激动感
words.ex: Her fingers tingle when she holds ice.
words.ex_cn: 当她握着冰时，手指会发麻。
words.en: If you tingle, you feel a slight prickling or stinging sensation, often because you are excited or frightened.

words.ex: His conjecture was that the missing key was in the drawer.
words.ex_cn: 他猜测丢失的钥匙在抽屉里。
words.en: A conjecture is a conclusion that is based on information that is not certain or complete.

words.ex: The doctor explained the disease in layman terms.
words.ex_cn: 医生用通俗易懂的语言解释了这种疾病。
words.en: A layman is a person who does not have specialized or professional knowledge of a subject.

words.ex: He smokes marijuana on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他周末吸大麻。
words.en: A drug made from the dried leaves and flowers of the hemp plant, which is smoked or eaten to induce euphoria.

words.ex: He wants to study psychiatry after medical school.
words.ex_cn: 他想在医学院毕业后学习精神病学。
words.en: Psychiatry is the branch of medicine concerned with the study, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental illness.

words.ex: She is going through menopause at age 52.
words.ex_cn: 她在52岁时经历更年期。
words.en: The time in a woman's life when she stops menstruating, typically between the ages of 45 and 55.

words.tr: n. 大数目；多种多样；繁多
words.ex: There is a multiplicity of stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有大量星星。
words.en: A multiplicity of things or people means a large number or great variety of them.

words.tr: v. 使遭危险或伤害；危害；危及
words.ex: Pollution can endanger animals.
words.ex_cn: 污染会危及动物。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk or in danger.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.tr: n. 怀疑论者；怀疑宗教主张的人；无神论者
words.ex: He is a skeptic about new health claims.
words.ex_cn: 他对新的健康说法持怀疑态度。
words.en: A skeptic is a person who questions the validity or authenticity of something purporting to be factual.

words.tr: v. 给…洗礼；施洗礼时命名；开始使用
words.ex: They will christen the new ship tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将为这艘新船命名。
words.en: To christen someone means to give them a name at a Christian baptism ceremony, or to give a name to something in a ceremony that is not religious.

words.ex: His story is far-fetched and not believable.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事牵强附会，不可信。
words.en: If you describe a story or idea as far-fetched, you mean that it is very unlikely to be true or practical.

words.ex: He felt inferiority when he compared himself to his smarter brother.
words.ex_cn: 当他把自己和更聪明的哥哥比较时，他感到自己处于劣势。
words.en: The state of being lower in status or quality than another or others.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.tr:
adj. 巨型的；特大的
n. 大型喷气式客机
words.ex: He bought a jumbo burger for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐买了一个超大汉堡。
words.en: If you describe something as jumbo, you mean that it is very large.

words.tr: n. 用户；订户；捐献者；签署者
words.ex: He is a subscriber to the newspaper.
words.ex_cn: 他是这份报纸的订阅者。
words.en: A subscriber is a person who pays to receive a product or service regularly, such as a magazine or a service on the internet.

words.ex: He handed me a pamphlet about the new park.
words.ex_cn: 他递给我一份关于新公园的小册子。
words.en: A pamphlet is a small book containing information on a particular subject or expressing political or religious views.

words.tr:
n. 挂毯；织锦；壁毯；绣帷
v. 用壁毡装饰；罩上绣花罩毯
words.ex: The wall has a colorful tapestry.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一幅色彩斑斓的挂毯。
words.en: A tapestry is a large piece of heavy cloth on which colored threads are woven to produce a picture, pattern, or design.

words.tr: adj. 极无礼的；粗暴的；骇人的；
words.ex: His outrageous behavior made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他极无礼的行为让所有人都生气了。
words.en: If you describe something as outrageous, you are emphasizing that it is unacceptable because it is extremely bad, immoral, or shocking.

words.tr:
adj. 不拘一格的；兼收并蓄的；折中的
n. 折中主义者
words.ex: He has an eclectic taste in music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的品味很广泛多样。
words.en: An eclectic collection or group is a wide range of different things or people.

words.tr:
v. 摇摇摆摆地走；蹒跚
n. 摇摆的步子；蹒跚而行
words.ex: The duck waddle across the pond.
words.ex_cn: 鸭子摇摆着走过池塘。
words.en: To walk with short steps, swaying from side to side, like a duck.

words.ex: The grandeur of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的宏伟让每个人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being grand or splendid in appearance or style.

words.ex: At this juncture, we need to make a decision.
words.ex_cn: 在这一关键时刻，我们需要做出决定。
words.en: A particular point in events or time, especially one that is critical or decisive.

words.tr: v. 射精；射出；突然说出
words.ex: He cannot ejaculate due to medicine.
words.ex_cn: 由于药物，他无法射精。
words.en: To ejaculate means to say something suddenly and briefly, or to emit semen from the penis during orgasm.

words.tr:
n. 纹身；刺青
v. 给…纹身
words.ex: He has a tattoo on his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他的手臂上有一个纹身。
words.en: A tattoo is a design that is drawn on someone's skin using needles to put little holes in the skin and filling them with coloured ink.

words.ex: He made a table from teak wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用柚木做了一张桌子。
words.en: Teak is a type of hardwood tree native to south and southeast Asia, known for its durability and water resistance. It is widely used in furniture making and shipbuilding.

words.tr:
n. 甜食；好东西；佳品
int. （儿语）好哇
words.ex: The children love eating goody after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢在晚饭后吃甜食。
words.en: A goody is something that is pleasant or attractive, especially something nice to eat.

words.ex: She wrote mother-in-law with a hyphen.
words.ex_cn: 她写 mother-in-law 时用了连字符。
words.en: A hyphen is a short line (-) used to connect the parts of a compound word or the parts of a word that has been split at the end of a line.

words.ex: He used artifice to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计赢得了比赛。
words.en: Clever or cunning devices or expedients, especially as used to trick or deceive others.

words.ex: The artisan makes handmade pottery.
words.ex_cn: 这位工匠制作手工陶器。
words.en: An artisan is someone who makes things by hand, especially using traditional methods.

words.tr:
v. 扭动；摆动
n. 扭动；摆动
words.ex: The baby wiggles her toes when she laughs.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝笑的时候，她会动动脚趾。
words.en: To move or cause to move up and down or from side to side with small rapid movements.

words.tr: v. 求爱；求婚；寻求支持
words.ex: He tried to woo her with flowers and chocolates.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和巧克力追求她。
words.en: If you woo someone, you try to persuade them to marry you or to have a relationship with you, or you try to gain their support or favor.

words.ex: He overstates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸大自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you say that someone is overstating something, you mean they are describing it in a way that makes it seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: The larynx helps us speak and breathe.
words.ex_cn: 喉部帮助我们说话和呼吸。
words.en: The part of the throat that contains the vocal cords and is used for breathing, swallowing, and speaking.

words.ex: He sleeps in a hammock under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 他睡在树下的吊床上。
words.en: A hammock is a piece of strong cloth or netting which is hung between two supports and used as a bed.

words.tr:
v. 喷出；涌出；呕吐
n. 呕吐物；喷出物
words.ex: The factory spews smoke into the air.
words.ex_cn: 工厂向空气中排放烟雾。
words.en: To spew means to expel something, especially liquid, gas, or small particles, in large quantities and with force. It can also refer to the act of vomiting.

words.tr:
v. 挡开；避开；回避
n. 挡开；闪避
words.ex: He parries the punch with his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他用胳膊格挡了这一拳。
words.en: If you parry a question or argument, you cleverly avoid answering it or dealing with it. In fencing, if you parry a blow, you defend yourself against it by pushing it away with your weapon.

words.tr: v. 摇摇欲坠；摇摆；玩跷跷板
words.ex: The child teeters on the edge of the pool.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在泳池边摇摇晃晃。
words.en: To move or balance unsteadily; sway back and forth.

words.ex: The cat is agile and jumps high.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳得很高。
words.en: Someone who is agile can move quickly and easily.

words.tr:
n. 疯子；狂人；狂热分子
adj. 疯狂的；狂热的
words.ex: The maniac screamed loudly in the street.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯子在街上大声喊叫。
words.en: A maniac is a person who has a very strong interest in something or behaves in a very wild or violent way.

words.ex: The old man looked gaunt after his illness.
words.ex_cn: 这场病后，老人显得消瘦。
words.en: If someone looks gaunt, they look very thin, usually because they have been ill or worried.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；温暖的
words.ex: He is a genial man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Friendly and cheerful.

words.ex: There was a lull in the rain before the storm came back.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨再次来临前，雨下了一阵间歇。
words.en: A lull is a short period of quiet or calm in an otherwise noisy or hectic situation. To lull means to cause someone to feel calm or to fall asleep.

words.tr: n. （新用户的）“潜伏”（在 USENET 上作为旁观者，不参加讨论）
words.ex: He was lurking on the forum for weeks before posting his first question.
words.ex_cn: 他在论坛上潜伏了几个星期，才发布了第一个问题。
words.en: If someone is lurking, they are waiting somewhere secretly, often because they intend to do something wrong.

words.tr:
n. 埋伏；伏击
v. 埋伏；伏击
words.ex: The soldiers set an ambush at night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在夜间设下埋伏。
words.en: An ambush is a surprise attack by people lying in wait in a concealed position.

words.ex: They tried to lynch him after the false accusation.
words.ex_cn: 在虚假指控之后，他们试图对他处以私刑。
words.en: If a group of people lynch someone, they kill that person without a legal trial, often because they believe that person has committed a crime.

words.tr: n. 萎蔫，凋萎; v. （植物）枯萎；（人）变得委靡不振；将（饲料作物）晒成半干（wilt的现在分...
words.ex: The flowers showed signs of wilting after no water for days.
words.ex_cn: 这些花在几天没有浇水后出现了凋萎的迹象。
words.en: If a plant wilts, it bends over because it is dying due to lack of water or too much heat.

words.tr:
n. 砍痕；伤痕；斜线号；削减
v. 砍；大幅度削减
words.ex: The tree has a deep slash on its trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的树干上有一道深深的砍痕。
words.en: To cut something with a sharp object in a violent way; to reduce something by a large amount suddenly.

words.tr: n. 演说者；演讲者；雄辩家；
words.ex: He is a famous orator who speaks at large events.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位在大型活动中演讲的著名演说者。
words.en: An orator is a person who delivers speeches or lectures, especially one who is skilled at doing so.

words.tr: v. 热得难受；“swelter”的现在分词；
words.ex: The children were sweltering in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在烈日下热得难受。
words.en: If you describe the heat or weather as sweltering, you mean that it is extremely hot and makes you feel uncomfortable.

words.tr: v.取来; 接来; 到达; 吸引（fetch 的过去分词形式）; 拿; 取物; 卖得（fetch 的过去...
words.ex: He fetched water from the well.
words.ex_cn: 他从井里打水。
words.en: To go and bring back something or someone.

words.tr:
v. 非法制造或售卖
adj. 非法制造或售卖的；盗版的
n. 私货；靴帮
words.ex: He sold bootleg movies near the station.
words.ex_cn: 他在车站附近卖盗版电影。
words.en: Bootleg refers to something, especially alcohol or recordings, that is made, distributed, or sold illegally.

words.ex: He is a prospective student at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的预期学生。
words.en: Prospective is used to describe someone or something that is expected or likely to happen or be in the future.

words.ex: We will review the meeting agenda tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将审查会议议程。
words.en: An agenda is a list or plan of things to be done or considered, especially in a meeting.

words.ex: The two parties formed a coalition to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这两个政党联合起来以赢得选举。
words.en: A coalition is a temporary alliance for combined action, especially of political parties forming a government.

words.tr: n. 生活福利设施；便利设施；“amenity”的复数；
words.ex: The apartment has good amenities like a gym and a swimming pool.
words.ex_cn: 这套公寓有健身房和游泳池等良好的生活福利设施。
words.en: Amenities are things such as stores or sports facilities that are provided for people's convenience, enjoyment, or comfort.

words.ex: The children play near the fountain in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园的喷泉附近玩耍。
words.en: A fountain is a structure that squirts water into the air to create a visual or auditory effect, or a natural source of water.

words.tr:
v. 摔跤；扭斗；奋力对付
n. 摔跤；角力；扭斗
words.ex: He tries to wrestle the dog away from the trash.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把狗从垃圾桶旁拉开。
words.en: To engage in a physical contest, typically involving grappling and trying to throw or immobilize the opponent, or to struggle with a difficult problem or decision.

words.tr: n. 种族主义；种族歧视；
words.ex: Racism is wrong and hurts many people.
words.ex_cn: 种族主义是错误的，会伤害很多人。
words.en: Racism is the belief that people of some races are inferior to others, often resulting in unfair treatment of people based on their race.

words.ex: The toy store sells many novelty items for children.
words.ex_cn: 玩具店出售许多为儿童设计的新奇物品。
words.en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual; something new, original, or unusual.

words.ex: The fringe of the forest is full of wildflowers.
words.ex_cn: 森林的边缘长满了野花。
words.en: The outer, marginal, or extreme part of an area, group, or sphere of activity.

words.tr:
n. 猛跌；衰退；萧条期
v. 急剧下降；暴跌；重重地坐下（或倒下）
words.ex: The company's sales went into a slump last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月，这家公司的销售额下滑了。
words.en: If something such as the value of something slumps, it falls suddenly and by a large amount.

words.tr:
adj. 砾岩的；成球状的；结成团块的
n. 砾岩；企业集团；联合大公司；合成物
v. （使）结聚成一团
words.ex: The rock layer is conglomerate, made of small stones stuck together.
words.ex_cn: 这层岩石是砾岩，由小石头粘合而成。
words.en: A conglomerate is a large business firm consisting of several different companies.

words.ex: He posted an anonymous comment online.
words.ex_cn: 他在网上发布了一条匿名评论。
words.en: If you remain anonymous when you do something, you do not let people know that you were the person who did it.

words.ex: He decided to embark on a new career.
words.ex_cn: 他决定从事一份新职业。
words.en: To embark on something means to start it, especially something new, difficult, or exciting.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.tr: adj. 引人注目的；显眼的
words.ex: The poster is eye-catching with bright colors.
words.ex_cn: 这张海报用鲜艳的颜色很引人注目。
words.en: Something that is eye-catching is very noticeable because it is unusual or attractive.

words.ex: They are discussing marital problems.
words.ex_cn: 他们正在讨论婚姻问题。
words.en: Marital is used to describe things relating to marriage.

words.ex: She felt pure bliss when she held her newborn baby.
words.ex_cn: 当她抱住新生儿时，感受到了无上的幸福。
words.en: Bliss is a state of complete happiness.

words.ex: The milk is frothy after being steamed.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶经过蒸汽处理后变得泡沫丰富。
words.en: Frothy describes something that is full of or covered with a mass of small bubbles, or something that is light and entertaining but not serious.

words.ex: He talked with bravado, but he was scared.
words.ex_cn: 他装出勇敢的样子说话，但他其实很害怕。
words.en: A bold manner or a show of boldness intended to impress or intimidate.

words.ex: The outlay for the new computer was high.
words.ex_cn: 这台新电脑的花费很高。
words.en: An outlay is an amount of money that you have to spend in order to buy something or to start a project.

words.ex: A blizzard covered the town in snow.
words.ex_cn: 一场暴风雪将整个小镇覆盖在雪中。
words.en: A blizzard is a severe snowstorm with strong winds.

words.ex: The word 'home' has a warm connotation.
words.ex_cn: ‘家’这个词有温暖的含义。
words.en: An idea or feeling that a word invokes in addition to its literal or primary meaning.

words.tr:
n. 腰带；彩带；肩带；窗框
v. 系上腰带；装以窗框
words.ex: She wore a red sash around her waist.
words.ex_cn: 她腰上系着一条红色的丝带。
words.en: A sash is a long piece of cloth which people wear around their waist or over one shoulder, especially as part of a uniform or official dress. It can also refer to the frame of a window.

words.tr: n. （以往南非的）种族隔离制度
words.ex: He lived under apartheid in South Africa.
words.ex_cn: 他在南非生活在种族隔离制度下。
words.en: A policy or system of segregation or discrimination on grounds of race, especially the policy that was in place in South Africa from 1948 to 1994.

words.tr: n. 拖欠的款项；“arrear”的复数；
words.ex: He paid all his arrears last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周付清了所有拖欠的款项。
words.en: If someone is in arrears with their payments, or if their payments are in arrears, they have not paid the regular amounts of money that they should have paid.

words.ex: The student went to the infirmary after falling off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 学生骑自行车摔了之后去了医院。
words.en: A place where sick or injured people receive care and treatment, especially in a school, college, or other institution.

words.ex: This test is a benchmark for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这个测试是所有学生的标准。
words.en: A benchmark is something whose quality or quantity is known and which can therefore be used as a standard with which other things can be compared.

words.ex: Each cell has 46 chromosomes.
words.ex_cn: 每个细胞有46条染色体。
words.en: A chromosome is a thread-like structure of nucleic acids and protein found in the nucleus of most living cells, carrying genetic information in the form of genes.

words.ex: She has a flair for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她有绘画的天赋。
words.en: If you have a flair for a particular activity, you have a natural ability to do it well.

words.ex: He noticed the nuance in her voice.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了她声音中的细微差别。
words.en: A very slight difference in meaning, sound, color, or someone's feelings that is not usually very obvious.

words.tr:
n. 坏女人；讨厌的女人
v. 埋怨；发牢骚；搞糟
words.ex: They are calling her bitch for no reason.
words.ex_cn: 他们无缘无故地叫她婊子。
words.en: A bitch is a female dog. In informal use, it can also refer to a woman who is regarded as malicious or unpleasant. As a verb, it means to complain in a petulant or whining manner.

words.ex: The teacher has a long tenure at the school.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师在学校有很长的任期。
words.en: The period during which an office is held; the status of holding one's position on a permanent basis.

words.ex: The army will not capitulate to the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 军队不会向敌人投降。
words.en: If you capitulate, you stop resisting and do what someone else wants you to do.

words.ex: The iron fence will corrode in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 铁栅栏在雨中会生锈。
words.en: If metal or stone corrodes, or if something corrodes it, it is gradually destroyed by a chemical reaction.

words.tr: adj. 操劳过度的；疲惫不堪的; v. 使衰弱（debilitate 的过去分词）
words.ex: He felt debilitated after working 16 hours a day for a week.
words.ex_cn: 他连续一周每天工作16小时后感到操劳过度。
words.en: If you are debilitated by something such as an illness, it makes you feel physically or mentally weak.

words.ex: He was electrocuted by a broken wire.
words.ex_cn: 他被一根破损的电线电死了。
words.en: To kill someone by passing a high-voltage electric current through their body.

words.ex: The curator arranged the paintings in the museum.
words.ex_cn: 馆长在博物馆里布置了这些画作。
words.en: A curator is someone who is in charge of the objects or works of art in a museum or art gallery.

words.ex: The bishop lives in the diocese near the river.
words.ex_cn: 主教住在河边的教区。
words.en: A diocese is the area over which a bishop has control.

words.tr: v. 抢劫；掠夺；蹂躏；破坏
words.ex: The invaders despoiled the village.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者抢劫了村庄。
words.en: To despoil something means to steal from it or damage it, especially in a violent or destructive way.

words.tr:
v. 猛拉；急抽
n. 猛拉；急抽
words.ex: He yanked the door open quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速把门拽开了。
words.en: To pull something suddenly and with force.

words.tr: v. 蹒跚；踉跄；摇摇欲坠
words.ex: The old man totters when he walks.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人走路时摇摇晃晃。
words.en: To move in a feeble or unsteady way.

words.tr: v. 攻击；困扰；抨击；袭击
words.ex: The storm assailed the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴袭击了这个小村庄。
words.en: If someone assails you, they attack you violently, either physically or with words.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.tr:
n. 协约；契约
v. 订立契约
words.ex: They made a covenant to always help each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们立下契约，永远互相帮助。
words.en: A covenant is a formal agreement or promise between two or more people, often involving legal obligations.

words.tr:
n. 说笑；玩笑
v. 开玩笑
words.ex: He likes to jest with his friends during lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在午餐时和朋友开玩笑。
words.en: A jest is a remark that is intended to be amusing or funny, especially one that is made in a light-hearted or teasing manner.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.ex: He proved his innocence to vindicate his name.
words.ex_cn: 他证明了自己的清白以洗清自己的名声。
words.en: To clear someone of blame or suspicion.

words.tr: n. 轿子；小轿车；厢式轿车
words.ex: The man rode in a sedan carried by two servants.
words.ex_cn: 这个人坐在两个仆人抬的轿子里。
words.en: A sedan is a type of car that has a closed body and a separate trunk, typically seating four or more people.

words.tr:
n. 旗；旗帜；信号旗；
v. 用旗标记；
words.ex: The flag waves in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 旗帜在风中飘扬。
words.en: A flag is a piece of cloth with a special design or colors that is used as a symbol, or to give a signal.

words.ex: The workers used a hoist to lift the heavy beams.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用吊升机械吊起沉重的梁。
words.en: To hoist something means to lift or pull it up to a higher position, usually using some kind of equipment such as a crane or pulley.

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.ex: He has great proficiency in English.
words.ex_cn: 他的英语水平很高。
words.en: If you show proficiency in something, you show ability or skill at it.

words.tr:
v. 投入；跳入
n. 跳进；骤降
words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.ex_cn: 他跳进了冰冷的水里。
words.en: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

words.ex: The medicine is potent and works quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物非常有效，起效很快。
words.en: Something that is potent is very effective and powerful.

words.tr: n. 前进；进展；间隔时间
words.ex: He made headway in solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决这道数学题上取得了进展。
words.en: If you make headway, you progress towards achieving something.

words.tr: adj. 声名狼藉的；臭名昭著的；
words.ex: He is a notorious thief who stole from many stores.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个声名狼藉的小偷，偷过许多商店。
words.en: Someone or something that is notorious is well known for something bad.

words.ex: The company updated the payroll last Friday.
words.ex_cn: 公司上星期五更新了职工工资册。
words.en: A payroll is a list of employees and the amount of money they are to be paid, or the total amount of money paid to the employees of a company.

words.ex: The stain on the carpet is a mar.
words.ex_cn: 地毯上的污渍是一个污点。
words.en: To mar something means to spoil or damage it.

words.ex: Her talent trumped his experience.
words.ex_cn: 她的才华胜过了他的经验。
words.en: In card games, a trump is a card of a suit which has been chosen to rank above the other suits. As a verb, to trump means to beat someone or something by doing or producing something better.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

words.ex: The city needs better infrastructural support for public transport.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市需要更好的基础设施支持公共交通。
words.en: Relating to the basic physical and organizational structures and facilities needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.tr: adj. 难以达到的；无法接近的；
words.ex: The mountain peak is inaccessible in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这座山峰在冬天难以到达。
words.en: If a place is inaccessible, it is very difficult or impossible to reach or enter.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.ex: The mountain is immense.
words.ex_cn: 这座山非常巨大。
words.en: Extremely large or great, especially in scale or degree.

words.ex: He exploited the situation to get more money.
words.ex_cn: 他利用这个情况赚了更多钱。
words.en: To exploit someone or something means to use them in a way that benefits you, often unfairly or without considering their rights or feelings. It can also refer to the act of making full use of and deriving benefit from a resource.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.tr:
v. （使）失去光泽；使晦暗；玷污
n. 晦暗；污渍
words.ex: The silver spoon will tarnish if not cleaned.
words.ex_cn: 如果银勺不清洗，就会变暗。
words.en: If you say that something tarnishes someone's reputation or image, you mean that it causes people to have a worse opinion of them than they would otherwise have had.

words.ex: The small boat capsize in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 小船在风暴中倾覆了。
words.en: If a boat capsizes or if you capsize it, it turns over in the water.

words.tr:
v. 坐立不安；烦躁；摆弄
n. 坐立不安；烦躁
words.ex: She couldn't sit still and kept fidgeting during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 她无法静坐，在讲座中不停地烦躁不安。
words.en: If you fidget, you keep moving your hands or feet slightly or changing your position slightly, for example because you are nervous, bored, or excited.

words.tr: v. 清算；变卖；消除；铲除
words.ex: The company will liquidate its assets to pay debts.
words.ex_cn: 公司将变卖资产来偿还债务。
words.en: To liquidate a company means to sell its assets in order to pay its debts, or to sell an asset for cash.

words.tr: n. 教规；准则；真作集；精品集；大教堂教士
words.ex: The church follows the canon of its faith.
words.ex_cn: 教会遵循其信仰的教规。
words.en: A canon is a rule or principle that is considered to be established, accepted, or authoritative, especially in the fields of religion, literature, or law.

words.ex: He fell into a coma after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后陷入了昏迷。
words.en: A coma is a state of deep unconsciousness that lasts for a prolonged or indefinite period, caused especially by severe injury or illness.

words.ex: She intersperses flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里分散地种着花。
words.en: To place something at intervals among other things.

words.ex: The hero will vanquish the dragon.
words.ex_cn: 英雄将战胜龙。
words.en: To vanquish someone means to defeat them completely in a battle or a competition.

words.tr: v. 置于…之间；插入；插嘴；介入
words.ex: The mediator tried to interpose before the situation escalated.
words.ex_cn: 调解人试图在局势升级之前进行干预。
words.en: If you interpose something between two people or things, you place it between them. If you interpose, you interrupt with a comment or question.

words.tr:
v. 发出（油煎食物的）咝咝声
n. 咝咝声
words.ex: The bacon sizzle in the pan.
words.ex_cn: 培根在平底锅里滋滋作响。
words.en: If something sizzles, it makes a sound like the sound that hot oil makes when you put food into it, or like the sound of water falling onto a hot surface.

words.tr:
v. 使翘棱；使扭曲变形
n. 弯曲；歪曲
words.ex: The heat will warp the metal.
words.ex_cn: 热量会使金属变形。
words.en: To warp is to bend or twist something out of its natural shape, often as a result of heat or moisture. It can also refer to the state of being bent or twisted.

words.ex: He was called a heretic for his strange beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 因为他奇怪的信仰，他被称为异端。
words.en: A heretic is someone whose beliefs or actions are considered wrong by most people, because they disagree with beliefs that are generally accepted.

words.tr: v. 晒太阳（取暖）；沉浸于
words.ex: He basks in the warm sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 他沐浴在温暖的阳光下。
words.en: If you bask in the sunshine, you lie somewhere sunny and enjoy the heat.

words.tr:
n. 连枷
v. 用连枷打；胡乱摆动；用力地挥动
words.ex: The farmer flails the wheat to separate the grains.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用连枷打小麦以分离谷粒。
words.en: A flail is a tool used for threshing grain, consisting of a long handle with a freely swinging stick or bar attached to it. As a verb, to flail means to wave or swing wildly; to thrash about.

words.ex: The boss can override the rules if needed.
words.ex_cn: 如果需要，老板可以凌驾于规则之上。
words.en: If one thing in a situation overrides other things, it is more important than them.

words.ex: He will not forsake his family.
words.ex_cn: 他不会抛弃他的家人。
words.en: If you forsake someone, you leave them when you should have stayed, or you stop helping them or looking after them.

words.tr:
n. 额外费用；附加费
v. 额外索价；附加罚款
words.ex: He paid a surcharge for extra baggage.
words.ex_cn: 他为额外行李支付了附加费。
words.en: An additional charge or payment.

words.tr:
n. 救援；援助者
v. 救援
words.ex: The nurse gave succor to the injured man.
words.ex_cn: 护士向受伤的男人提供了援助。
words.en: Succor is assistance and support given to someone in times of hardship or distress.

words.ex: He found uranium in the old rock sample.
words.ex_cn: 他在旧岩石样本中发现了铀。
words.en: A heavy, silvery-white metallic element, radioactive and toxic, used as a fuel in nuclear reactors and in the manufacture of nuclear weapons.

words.tr: n. 几率；不利条件；不平等；
words.ex: The odds of winning the lottery are very low.
words.ex_cn: 中彩票的几率非常低。
words.en: The odds are the chances that a particular thing will happen.

words.ex: He will defer his trip until next month.
words.ex_cn: 他将把旅行推迟到下个月。
words.en: If you defer an event or action, you arrange for it to happen at a later date, rather than immediately or at the previously planned time.

words.tr:
v. 鼓起；集合；召集
n. 集合；集合的人群
words.ex: He must muster courage to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他必须鼓起勇气在公众面前发言。
words.en: To muster means to gather or assemble (troops, etc.), especially for inspection or in preparation for battle. It can also mean to summon up (a feeling, attitude, or response).

words.ex: The keys dangle from his belt.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙挂在他的腰带上。
