words.en: A headline is the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters at the top of the story, especially on the front page.

words.ex: The deer avoided the hemlock because it is poisonous.
words.ex_cn: 鹿避开了毒芹，因为它是有毒的。
words.en: Hemlock is a highly poisonous plant, especially the poison hemlock, Conium maculatum, of the parsley family. It is also the name of the poison derived from this plant.

words.ex: Hemophilia is a genetic disorder that impairs the body's ability to make blood clots.
words.ex_cn: 血友病是一种遗传性疾病，会损害身体形成血块的能力。
words.en: A hereditary disorder where the blood does not clot properly, leading to excessive bleeding.

words.tr:
n. 体内大出血；严重流失
v. 体内大出血；（使）严重流失
words.ex: The patient suffered a severe hemorrhage after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 病人在事故后发生了严重的出血。
words.en: A hemorrhage is a severe loss of blood from a burst blood vessel, either inside or outside the body.

words.ex: He has a hemorrhoid and feels pain when he sits.
words.ex_cn: 他有痔疮，坐着时感到疼痛。
words.en: A hemorrhoid is a swollen vein or group of veins in the region of the anus.

words.ex: They made rope from hemp.
words.ex_cn: 他们用大麻纤维制作绳子。
words.en: Hemp is a plant from the cannabis family, cultivated for its fiber, seeds, and oil. It is used in a variety of products, including textiles, paper, and biodegradable plastics.

words.ex: Henceforth, I will wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 从今以后，我会早起。
words.en: From this time on; from now on.

words.tr: n. 亲信；心腹；追随者；党羽
words.ex: The boss hired a henchman to scare his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 老板雇了一个打手去吓唬他的敌人。
words.en: A henchman is a loyal supporter or follower, especially one who supports a powerful person in a way that is morally wrong or criminal.

words.tr:
adj. “妻管严”的；惧内的
v. 惧内；“henpeck”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is a henpecked husband who always follows his wife's orders.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是听妻子吩咐的怕老婆的丈夫。
words.en: A henpecked man is one who is dominated by his wife or partner and is often criticized or nagged by her.

words.ex: He has hepatitis and needs to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他患有肝炎，需要休息。
words.en: Hepatitis is an inflammation of the liver, often caused by a viral infection.

words.ex: The deer is a herbivore.
words.ex_cn: 鹿是食草动物。
words.en: An herbivore is an animal that gets its energy from eating plants, and only plants.

words.ex: The deer is herbivorous.
words.ex_cn: 这只鹿是食草的。
words.en: Herbivorous animals are those that feed on plants.

words.tr:
adv. 从今以后；此后
n. 死后；来世
words.ex: Hereafter, he will work harder.
words.ex_cn: 从此以后，他会更加努力。
words.en: in the future; after this time

words.ex: His tall height is hereditary from his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他高高的身材是遗传自父母的。
words.en: A hereditary characteristic or illness is passed from the genes of a parent to a child.

words.ex: Heredity determines eye color in humans.
words.ex_cn: 遗传决定人类的眼睛颜色。
words.en: Heredity is the process by which features and characteristics are passed on from parents to their children before the children are born.

words.ex: The solution lies herein.
words.ex_cn: 解决方法就在这里。
words.en: in this place or thing, or in this document

words.ex: The contract is valid hereof.
words.ex_cn: 就此而言，合同是有效的。
words.en: of or concerning this; as a part of this

words.ex: His views were considered heretical by the religious authorities.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点被宗教权威认为是异端的。
words.en: If someone's beliefs or actions are heretical, they are contrary to the official or accepted beliefs or practices of a particular religion or group.

words.ex: I agree to the terms hereto.
words.ex_cn: 我同意此处的条款。
words.en: To this matter or document.

words.ex: Heretofore, he did not understand the problem.
words.ex_cn: 到目前为止，他不明白这个问题。
words.en: Up to this time; until now.

words.ex: I am enclosing the documents herewith.
words.ex_cn: 我随信附上文件。
words.en: used in formal writing to introduce a document or to say that something is included with a letter

words.tr: adj. 密封的；不透气的；与外界隔绝的
words.ex: The container was hermetic to ensure the contents stayed fresh.
words.ex_cn: 这个容器是密封的，以确保内容物保持新鲜。
words.en: If something is hermetic, it is so tightly sealed that no air can get in or out.

words.tr: n. 隐居处；修道院；偏僻的寺院
words.ex: The old monk lived in a small hermitage on the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位老僧人住在山上的一个小隐居处。
words.en: A hermitage is a place where a hermit lives in seclusion from the world.

words.ex: His heterodox ideas shocked the traditional scholars.
words.ex_cn: 他的非正统观点让传统学者感到震惊。
words.en: Heterodox ideas, opinions, or practices are different from the accepted or official ones.

words.ex: That park was in its heyday in the 1990s.
words.ex_cn: 那个公园在20世纪90年代是它的鼎盛时期。
words.en: The period of a person's or thing's greatest success, popularity, or vigor.

words.ex: He took a hiatus from work to travel.
words.ex_cn: 他休假去旅行了。
words.en: A hiatus is a pause or gap in a sequence, series, or process.

words.ex: Bears hibernate in winter to save energy.
words.ex_cn: 熊在冬天冬眠以保存能量。
words.en: To spend the winter in a dormant state.

words.ex: He had a loud hiccup during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间打了个响亮的嗝。
words.en: A hiccup is an involuntary spasm of the diaphragm and respiratory organs, with a sudden closure of the glottis and a characteristic sound.

words.tr:
n. 打嗝
v. 打嗝
words.ex: He tried to stop his hiccough by holding his breath.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过屏住呼吸来止住打嗝。
words.en: A hiccough is a sudden, involuntary contraction of the diaphragm that occurs repeatedly at intervals of a few seconds, often causing a characteristic sound.

words.tr: n. 藏身处；隐匿处；退隐处
words.ex: The kids found a hideaway in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在树林里发现了一个隐蔽的地方。
words.en: A hideaway is a place where someone goes because they want to be alone or because they want to hide from someone.

words.tr: adj. 顽固守旧的；死板保守的
words.ex: He is hidebound and refuses to change his old ways.
words.ex_cn: 他思想僵化，拒绝改变他的老办法。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as hidebound, you are criticizing them for having old-fashioned attitudes or ideas and being unwilling or unlikely to change.

words.ex: The school has a hierarchical system.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个等级制度。
words.en: A hierarchical system or organization is one in which people have different ranks or positions, depending on how important they are.

words.ex: Ancient Egyptians wrote in hieroglyphics.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人用象形字书写。
words.en: Hieroglyphics are symbols in the form of pictures which are used in some writing systems, especially those of ancient Egypt.

words.tr: n. 有文化修养的人；有高雅趣味的人；
words.ex: He is a highbrow who loves classical music and old novels.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有文化修养的人，喜欢古典音乐和古典小说。
words.en: A highbrow person or thing is interested in or concerned with intellectual or cultural matters, often to the exclusion of more practical or popular interests.

words.tr: n. 小孩吃饭时所用之高脚椅子
words.ex: The baby sits in the highchair to eat.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝坐在高脚椅上吃饭。
words.en: A highchair is a type of chair designed for babies and young children to sit in while eating. It is usually elevated to bring the child up to table height.

words.ex: The boss was highhanded and ignored the workers' requests.
words.ex_cn: 老板专横，无视工人的请求。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as highhanded, you disapprove of it because they use their authority in an unnecessarily forceful way without considering other people's feelings.

words.ex: His highness is the king of the country.
words.ex_cn: 他的殿下是这个国家的国王。
words.en: The state or quality of being high; a title used to address or refer to a royal person.

words.tr: adj. 声调高的；声音尖锐的；陡的（屋顶）；激烈
words.ex: The baby cried with a high-pitched sound.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿发出高亢的哭声。
words.en: A high-pitched sound is very high and sometimes loud or unpleasant.

words.tr: n. 徒步旅行者；远足者
words.ex: The hiker walked up the mountain slowly.
words.ex_cn: 这位徒步者慢慢爬上了山。
words.en: A hiker is a person who walks long distances, especially across country.

words.ex: The children played on a small hillock near the river.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在河边的小山丘上玩耍。
words.en: A hillock is a small hill or mound.

words.ex: He grabbed the hilt of his sword.
words.ex_cn: 他抓住了剑柄。
words.en: The hilt of a sword or dagger is the handle, especially the part by which it is held.

words.ex: He speaks Hindi at home with his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他在家和父母说印地语。
words.en: Hindi is one of the major languages of India, spoken by a large number of people as a first language and by many more as a second language. It is written in the Devanagari script and is one of the two official languages of the Government of India, alongside English.

words.tr: adj. 最后部的；在最后面的；“hind”的最高级
words.ex: The hindmost child in the line could not see the stage.
words.ex_cn: 队列最后面的孩子看不到舞台。
words.en: Situated at the very end; farthest back.

words.ex: The butcher expertly carved the hindquarter of the lamb.
words.ex_cn: 屠夫熟练地切开了羊的后腿及臀部。
words.en: The rear part of a side of beef, lamb, etc., including the leg and loin.

words.ex: With hindsight, I should have saved more money.
words.ex_cn: 事后看来，我本该多存些钱。
words.en: The understanding of a situation or event only after it has happened or developed.

words.ex: He practices hinduism every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天实践印度教。
words.en: Hinduism is a major religious and cultural tradition of South Asia, which developed from Vedic religion.

words.tr: adj. 西班牙的；西班牙和葡萄牙的；拉丁美洲的
words.ex: He is a Hispanic student from Spain.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名来自西班牙的西班牙裔学生。
words.en: relating to Spain or to Spanish-speaking countries, especially those of Latin America.

words.ex: His histrionic gestures made the play very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 他戏剧性的手势让这场戏非常精彩。
words.en: If you refer to someone's behaviour as histrionic, you are critical of it because it is very dramatic, exaggerated, and insincere.

words.ex: The bees built a hive in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂在树上建了一个蜂巢。
words.en: A hive is a structure where bees live, consisting of a series of cells in which they store honey and raise their young.

words.tr:
n. 临时的围篱；巨幅广告牌；囤积
v. 贮藏；囤积；“hoard”的现在分词
words.ex: He is hoarding food in his basement.
words.ex_cn: 他正在地下室囤积食物。
words.en: Hoarding refers to the act of collecting and storing large amounts of something, especially when it is not necessary or when it is done secretly.

words.tr: n. 玩具木马；爱反复讲的话题
words.ex: He keeps talking about his hobbyhorse, tax reform.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地谈论他的老话题——税收改革。
words.en: A hobbyhorse is a subject or idea that someone talks about a lot or is very interested in, often to the point of obsession.

words.ex: The child feared the hobgoblin under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 孩子害怕床下的小精灵。
words.en: A hobgoblin is a small, mischievous creature in folklore, often considered to be a type of fairy or elf.

words.ex: He wore hobnail boots to walk on rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着钉鞋在崎岖的地面上行走。
words.en: A hobnail is a short nail with a thick head used to reinforce the soles of boots or shoes.

words.ex: He hobnobs with famous actors at parties.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上与著名演员亲近交往。
words.en: To associate familiarly or socially; to drink together.

words.ex: The hod is cleaning the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 清洁工正在打扫教室。
words.en: A hod is a tool used by bricklayers to carry bricks or mortar.

words.tr: adj. 猪一般的；贪婪的；自私的
words.ex: He is hoggish and never shares his food.
words.ex_cn: 他很自私，从不分享他的食物。
words.en: If you describe someone as hoggish, you are criticizing them for being greedy or selfish.

words.ex: The wine was stored in a large hogshead.
words.ex_cn: 葡萄酒被存放在一个大酒桶里。
words.en: A large cask or barrel, especially one used for wine or beer, holding a specific volume.

words.tr: n. （旅行用的）手提箱或手提袋
words.ex: He packed his clothes in a holdall.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服装进了一个旅行包。
words.en: A holdall is a large bag that you carry your clothes and other possessions in when you are traveling.

words.ex: The old man prays for holiness every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人每天早上祈祷追求圣洁。
words.en: The state or quality of being holy; sanctity.

words.ex: The hologram floats in the air.
words.ex_cn: 全息图悬浮在空中。
words.en: A hologram is a three-dimensional image created by photographic projection.

words.ex: He uses homeopathy to treat his cold.
words.ex_cn: 他用顺势疗法治疗感冒。
words.en: Homeopathy is a system of alternative medicine created in 1796 by Samuel Hahnemann, based on his doctrine of like cures like, a claim that a substance that causes the symptoms of a disease in healthy people would cure similar symptoms in sick people.

words.ex: He lives on a small homestead with his family.
words.ex_cn: 他和家人住在一个小农场里。
words.en: A homestead is a house and the land around it, especially a farm.

words.tr: adj. 家庭般的；舒适自在的
words.ex: The little cabin feels homey and warm.
words.ex_cn: 这间小木屋感觉温馨而温暖。
words.en: If you describe a place or someone's house as homey, you mean it is nice, comfortable, and inviting.

words.ex: The police investigated the homicide case.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了这起凶杀案。
words.en: The act of killing another person, especially when it is considered a crime.

words.ex: The priest gave a short homily after the prayer.
words.ex_cn: 祷告后，牧师做了一个简短的讲道。
words.en: A homily is a religious discourse which is intended to edify a congregation, typically given by a priest or minister during a service.

words.tr:
adj. 有返回原地本能的；自动寻向的
v. 送…回家；提供住处；“home”的现在分词
words.ex: The pigeon is homing to its nest.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子正飞回它的巢。
words.en: Homing refers to the ability to return home or to a specific location, especially used in the context of animals or devices.

words.ex: The homogeneity of the sample made the test results reliable.
words.ex_cn: 样本的同种性使测试结果可靠。
words.en: The quality or state of being all the same or all of the same kind.

words.ex: The machine will homogenise the milk.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会将牛奶均质化。
words.en: To homogenise something means to change it so that all its parts or elements become the same or are evenly mixed.

words.ex: The machine will homogenize the milk.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会将牛奶均质化。
words.en: To homogenize something means to make it the same throughout, or to make it uniform.

words.tr:
adj. 同性恋的
n. 同性恋者
words.ex: He is homosexual and loves his partner.
words.ex_cn: 他是同性恋，爱他的伴侣。
words.en: A homosexual is someone who is sexually attracted to people of the same sex.

words.tr:
n. 蜂窝；蜂窝状物
v. 使布满小孔；成蜂窝状
words.ex: Bees build their nest in a honeycomb shape.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂用蜂窝形状建造它们的巢。
words.en: A honeycomb is a structure of hexagonal cells made by bees, used to store honey and pollen or to house their eggs and larvae.

words.tr:
n. 雁叫声；汽车喇叭声
v. （使汽车喇叭）鸣响；（雁）叫
words.ex: The honk of the geese echoed over the lake.
words.ex_cn: 大雁的叫声在湖面上回荡。
words.en: 1. The sound made by a car horn. 2. The cry of a goose. 3. To make a sound like a car horn or a goose.

words.ex: He tried to hoodwink her with a fake story.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个虚假的故事欺骗她。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.ex: The hooligan broke a window during the match.
words.ex_cn: 那个流氓在比赛期间砸了一扇窗户。
words.en: A hooligan is a violent young troublemaker, typically one of a gang.

words.tr:
n. 叫好声
int. 万岁；好哇；
words.ex: Hooray! We won the game!
words.ex_cn: 万岁！我们赢了比赛！
words.en: used to express joy or approval

words.ex: He turned on the hoover to clean the carpet.
words.ex_cn: 他打开吸尘器清理地毯。
words.en: To clean something, especially a carpet, with a vacuum cleaner.

words.ex: The farmer poured grain into the hopper.
words.ex_cn: 农夫把谷物倒进漏斗里。
words.en: A hopper is a person or thing that hops, especially a type of insect that can jump long distances.

words.ex: A horde of children ran to the ice cream truck.
words.ex_cn: 一群孩子跑向冰淇淋车。
words.en: A horde is a large group of people or animals, especially one that is moving or acting together.

words.ex: A hornet flew near my head.
words.ex_cn: 一只大黄蜂飞到了我的头附近。
words.en: A hornet is a large, stinging wasp that is typically more aggressive than a bee.

words.ex: The accident looked horrendous.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故看起来很可怕。
words.en: If you describe something as horrendous, you are emphasizing that it is very unpleasant or shocking.

words.tr: adj. 恐怖的；令人震惊的
words.ex: The accident was horrific.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故非常可怕。
words.en: If you say that something is horrific, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant and shocking.

words.ex: The boys were caught doing horseplay in the hallway.
words.ex_cn: 这些男孩在走廊里打闹，被抓住了。
words.en: Rough, boisterous play.

words.ex: The horseshoe is nailed to a horse's hoof.
words.ex_cn: 马蹄形铁掌被钉在马的蹄子上。
words.en: A horseshoe is a piece of metal shaped like a U, which is fixed with nails to the bottom of a horse's foot in order to protect it.

words.tr:
v. 用马鞭抽打；惩罚
n. 马鞭
words.ex: The farmer used a horsewhip to guide the horse.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用马鞭来引导马。
words.en: A horsewhip is a long, thin piece of leather or similar material attached to a handle, used for directing or urging a horse to move faster.

words.ex: The little girl rides a horsey at the park.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩在公园里骑小马。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a horse; fond of horses.

words.ex: The boy rides a horse every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩每天早上骑马。
words.en: A horse is a large animal which people can ride. Some horses are used for pulling ploughs and carts.

words.ex: She bought new hosiery for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了新的袜子。
words.en: Hosiery refers to stockings, socks, and tights collectively, especially those made of knitted fabric.

words.tr: n. （教会办的）旅客招待所；临终关怀医院；临终安养院
words.ex: He spent his last days in a hospice.
words.ex_cn: 他最后的日子是在临终关怀机构度过的。
words.en: A hospice is a special hospital or home for people who are dying, where they are cared for by specially trained nurses and doctors.

words.ex: The city is a hotbed of protests.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市是抗议活动的温床。
words.en: A hotbed is a place or situation that encourages the development of something, especially something bad.

words.tr: adj. 热血的；易激动的；感情冲动的
words.ex: He was a hot-blooded young man, always ready for a fight.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热血青年，随时准备打架。
words.en: If you describe someone as hot-blooded, you mean that they are very quick to express their emotions, especially anger and love.

words.ex: The kitchen is a hotchpotch of old pots and new tools.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里堆满了旧锅和新工具，杂乱无章。
words.en: A confused mixture of different things.

words.tr: n. 旅馆经理；旅馆老板；
words.ex: The hotelier welcomed guests with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 旅馆经理微笑着欢迎客人。
words.en: A person who owns or manages a hotel.

words.tr:
v. 急急忙忙地走
adv. 急匆匆地
words.ex: He hotfooted to the store when he ran out of milk.
words.ex_cn: 他一喝完牛奶就赶紧跑去了商店。
words.en: If you hotfoot it somewhere, you go there very quickly.

words.tr: n. 性急的人；鲁莽的人
words.ex: He was always known as a hothead, quick to anger.
words.ex_cn: 他总是以性急著称，容易发怒。
words.en: A hothead is someone who acts too quickly without thinking, often getting into trouble or arguments as a result.

words.ex: The flowers grow in a hothouse.
words.ex_cn: 这些花在温室里生长。
words.en: A hothouse is a building made of glass in which plants that need protection from cold weather are grown.

words.tr: n. 电炉；烤盘；（炉灶上的）加热板
words.ex: He cooks soup on a hotplate.
words.ex_cn: 他用热板煮汤。
words.en: A hotplate is a portable device with a flat heated surface, used for cooking food or keeping it warm.

words.tr: n. 火锅；热锅炖菜；罐焖菜肴
words.ex: We had hotpot for dinner last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚我们晚餐吃了罐焖土豆烧肉。
words.en: A hotpot is a dish that is cooked and served in a pot at the table, typically containing a variety of meats, vegetables, and sometimes noodles or tofu, cooked in a simmering pot of stock at the table.

words.ex: They live on a houseboat on the river.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在河上的一艘船屋里。
words.en: A houseboat is a boat that is designed to be lived in. It is often moored in one place on a river or canal, but can also be moved to different locations.

words.tr: adj. 不能外出的；不能离家的
words.ex: He is housebound because of his illness.
words.ex_cn: 他因病而足不出户。
words.en: If someone is housebound, they are unable to go out of their house, often because they are ill or have a disability.

words.tr: n. 居家女式便服；（女式）家居袍
words.ex: She wears a housecoat while cleaning the house.
words.ex_cn: 她打扫房子时穿一件家居袍。
words.en: A housecoat is a long, loose piece of clothing that you wear at home, especially over your nightclothes.

words.tr: n. 家政学；管家的技能
words.ex: She learned housecraft from her mother.
words.ex_cn: 她从母亲那里学会了家务技能。
words.en: Housecraft refers to the skills involved in managing a household, including cooking, cleaning, and other domestic tasks.

words.ex: The housemaster checks the students' rooms every morning.
words.ex_cn: 宿舍管理员每天早上检查学生的房间。
words.en: A housemaster is a male teacher in charge of a house at a boarding school.

words.tr: n. 新屋落成宴；乔迁庆宴
words.ex: They had a housewarming party last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他们上周末举办了乔迁派对。
words.en: A housewarming is a party that is held to celebrate moving into a new home.

words.ex: She practices housewifery every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天都在做家务。
words.en: The management of a household; the duties and activities associated with running a home.

words.ex: The old man lives in a small hovel.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人住在一间小破屋里。
words.en: A hovel is a small, dirty, and often poorly built house or shelter.

words.ex: The wolf is a howler at night.
words.ex_cn: 狼是夜晚嚎叫的动物。
words.en: A howler is a person or thing that howls, or a very stupid or embarrassing mistake.

words.tr: abbr. 殿下；“His/Her Royal Highness”的缩写
words.ex: HRH is attending the royal ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 王室成员正在参加王室典礼。
words.en: His/Her Royal Highness; a title used for members of the royal family.

words.tr:
v. 贩卖；叫卖；强行推销
n. 沿街叫卖的小贩；强行推销的人
words.ex: The huckster tried to sell us a cheap watch.
words.ex_cn: 那个小贩试图向我们推销一块廉价手表。
words.en: A huckster is a person who sells small items, often by calling out to people in the street or by going from place to place.

words.tr:
v. 挤作一团
n. 挤作一团
words.ex: The team huddled together to plan their next move.
words.ex_cn: 团队聚在一起规划下一步行动。
words.en: If people huddle together, they stand, sit, or lie close to each other because they are cold or frightened.

words.tr: n. 大型废弃物；巨大笨重的人（物）
words.ex: The old boat was left as a hulk on the shore.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船被遗弃在岸边，成为了一堆大型废弃物。
words.en: A hulk is a large, clumsy, or old ship that is no longer in use and is often left to decay in a harbor.

words.ex: The hulking man lifted the heavy box easily.
words.ex_cn: 那个魁梧的男人轻松地举起了沉重的箱子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as hulking, you mean that they are extremely large and often that they are also awkward or ugly.

words.tr:
n. 欺诈；谎话；骗子
v. 欺骗；行骗
words.ex: He was accused of being a humbug and spreading false information.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控为骗子，散布虚假信息。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behaviour as humbug, you mean that it is dishonest or insincere.

words.ex: His daily routine is humdrum.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活很单调。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as humdrum, you mean that they are ordinary, dull, or boring.

words.ex: The humpback swam near the shore.
words.ex_cn: 座头鲸游到了岸边附近。
words.en: A humpback is a large whale with a hump on its back and long flippers, known for its complex songs and acrobatic displays.

words.ex: The cat hunched its back when it saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫看到狗时，背部拱了起来。
words.en: A hunch is a feeling or guess based on intuition rather than known facts.

words.ex: The old man has a hunchback from years of hard work.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人因多年辛勤劳动而驼背。
words.en: A hunchback is a person who has a back that is bent forward, often because of a medical condition.

words.ex: The bag weighs one hundredweight.
words.ex_cn: 这个袋子重一英担。
words.en: A unit of weight equal to 112 pounds in Britain and 100 pounds in the US.

words.tr:
n. 跨栏；障碍；难关
v. 越过障碍；克服
words.ex: He jumped over the hurdle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速跳过了跨栏。
words.en: A hurdle is a problem or difficulty that you must deal with before you can achieve something.

words.tr: v. 猛冲；猛投；猛烈碰撞
words.ex: The car hurtled down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 汽车飞速冲下山坡。
words.en: If someone or something hurtles somewhere, they move there very quickly, often in a uncontrolled way.

words.ex: He learned husbandry from his father on the farm.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里学会了畜牧业。
words.en: Husbandry is the careful management of resources, especially in agriculture or farming, to ensure their efficient use and conservation.

words.ex: The rabbit lives in a small hutch.
words.ex_cn: 兔子住在一个小兔舍里。
words.en: A hutch is a type of cage or pen used to house small animals, especially rabbits, or a piece of furniture with shelves and a cupboard.

words.tr:
n. 杂交种；混合物；
adj. 混合的；
words.ex: The corn hybrid grows faster than the old type.
words.ex_cn: 这种玉米杂交种比旧品种长得更快。
words.en: A hybrid is a plant or animal that has been produced from two different types of plant or animal, especially to get better characteristics. It can also refer to something that is a mixture of two different things.

words.ex: The fire truck connected to the hydrant.
words.ex_cn: 消防车连接到消防栓。
words.en: A hydrant is an upright pipe with a spout, nozzle, or other outlet, usually in the street, for drawing water from a main or service line, especially for fighting fires.

words.tr: adj. 液压的；流体的；利用液体压力的；
words.ex: The hydraulic brake system stops the car quickly.
words.ex_cn: 液压制动系统能快速让汽车停下。
words.en: Hydraulic refers to the operation of machinery or systems by the movement and force of liquid, especially water or oil.

words.ex: The car burns hydrocarbon fuel.
words.ex_cn: 汽车燃烧碳氢化合物燃料。
words.en: A hydrocarbon is an organic compound consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon.

words.tr: adj. 盐酸的；含氢和氯的
words.ex: Hydrochloric acid burns the skin.
words.ex_cn: 盐酸会灼伤皮肤。
words.en: Hydrochloric refers to or denotes a compound of hydrogen and chlorine, especially hydrochloric acid.

words.ex: The dam produces hydroelectricity for nearby towns.
words.ex_cn: 这座水坝为附近的城镇提供水力电气。
words.en: Electricity generated by the movement of water.

words.ex: Sodium hydroxide is a strong base.
words.ex_cn: 氢氧化钠是一种强碱。
words.en: A hydroxide is a chemical compound containing an oxygen atom bonded to a hydrogen atom, which can dissociate in water to produce hydroxide ions.

words.tr: adj. 过分活跃的；多动的；亢奋的
words.ex: The hyperactive child runs around the room all day.
words.ex_cn: 这个多动的孩子整天在房间里跑来跑去。
words.en: If someone is hyperactive, they are extremely active and find it difficult to relax or concentrate on one thing for very long.

words.tr: adj. 苛求的；吹毛求疵的
words.ex: He is hypercritical about small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他对小错误非常吹毛求疵。
words.en: If you say that someone is hypercritical, you mean that they criticize things too much or too severely.

words.ex: He buys groceries at the hypermarket every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周都在超级市场买杂货。
words.en: A hypermarket is a very large supermarket that sells a wide range of products, often including groceries, clothing, and household goods, under one roof.

words.ex: He has hypertension and takes medicine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他有高血压，每天吃药。
words.en: Hypertension is a condition in which the force of the blood against the artery walls is too high.

words.ex: Please hyphenate the words 'well-being'.
words.ex_cn: 请把 'well-being' 这两个词用连字符连接。
words.en: To hyphenate means to join words or syllables with a hyphen.

words.ex: He entered a deep hypnosis during the therapy.
words.ex_cn: 他在治疗过程中进入了深度催眠状态。
words.en: Hypnosis is a state in which a person seems to be asleep but can still see, hear, or respond to things said to them.

words.tr: adj. 催眠的；引起睡眠的；
words.ex: The soft music had a hypnotic effect.
words.ex_cn: 柔和的音乐有催眠效果。
words.en: Something that is hypnotic holds your attention or makes you feel very relaxed, often in a way that is similar to being hypnotized.

words.ex: He uses hypnotism to help people relax.
words.ex_cn: 他使用催眠术帮助人们放松。
words.en: Hypnotism is the practice of hypnotizing people.

words.tr:
adj. 皮下注射的；皮下的
n. 皮下注射；皮下注射器
words.ex: The nurse used a hypodermic needle to give him a shot.
words.ex_cn: 护士用皮下注射针给他打了一针。
words.en: A hypodermic needle or syringe is a medical instrument with a hollow needle used to inject substances into the body or extract fluids from it.

words.ex: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right triangle.
words.ex_cn: 斜边是直角三角形中最长的一条边。
words.en: The side opposite the right angle in a right-angled triangle.

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: She stored the leftovers in the icebox to keep them fresh.
words.ex_cn: 她把剩菜放在冰箱里保鲜。
words.en: A refrigerator or a box where ice is used to keep food cold.

words.tr: n. 破冰船；打破僵局者
words.ex: He told a joke to start an icebreaker.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了个笑话来破冰。
words.en: An icebreaker is a ship designed to move through ice-covered waters, or something that serves to relieve tension or get conversation going in a social situation.

words.ex: An icicle hangs from the roof.
words.ex_cn: 一个冰锥挂在屋顶上。
words.en: An icicle is a pointed piece of ice that is formed when dripping water freezes, typically hanging from a surface.

words.tr:
n. 糖衣；糖霜
v. （使）结冰；“ice”的现在分词
words.ex: The cake has a thin layer of icing on top.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕顶部有一层薄薄的糖衣。
words.en: Icing is a sweet mixture made from sugar and water or milk, which is used to cover or fill cakes.

words.ex: He is an icon of pop music.
words.ex_cn: 他是流行音乐的偶像。
words.en: An icon is a small picture or symbol on a computer screen that represents a program or a file.

words.ex: His idiosyncrasy is talking to himself while reading.
words.ex_cn: 他的怪癖是读书时自言自语。
words.en: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar or unusual habit, way of behaving, or feature that someone or something has.

words.tr: n. 偶像崇拜；盲目崇拜
words.ex: He worships the pop star like idolatry.
words.ex_cn: 他像崇拜偶像一样崇拜这位流行歌手。
words.en: The worship of idols or excessive admiration for someone or something.

words.tr: v. 偶像化；过分崇拜；奉为神圣
words.ex: He idolizes his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他崇拜他的哥哥。
words.en: If you idolize someone, you admire them very much.

words.ex: The small village is idyllic with green fields and quiet streams.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄有着绿色的田野和宁静的溪流，十分宁静美好。
words.en: An idyllic place or experience is extremely pleasant, beautiful, and peaceful, often in a way that seems too good to be true.

words.ex: The car won't start because the ignition is broken.
words.ex_cn: 汽车无法启动，因为点火器坏了。
words.en: The process of starting the combustion of fuel in an engine.

words.tr: adj. 平民的；卑贱的；卑鄙的；不光彩的
words.ex: He came from an ignoble family, but worked hard to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他出身于平民家庭，但努力工作以取得成功。
words.en: If you describe something as ignoble, you mean that it is bad and something to be ashamed of.

words.tr: n. 耻辱；屈辱；名誉受损
words.ex: He faced ignominy after lying to the court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后遭到了耻辱。
words.en: Ignominy is a situation or event that causes you to feel ashamed or embarrassed, especially when this is public.

words.ex: His handwriting is illegible.
words.ex_cn: 他的字迹无法辨认。
words.en: If something is illegible, it is impossible to read because the letters or characters are not clear, are not formed properly, or are obscured in some way.

words.ex: The illegitimate business was shut down by the police.
words.ex_cn: 这个非法的生意被警察关闭了。
words.en: An illegitimate child is one whose parents were not married to each other when the child was born. Something that is illegitimate is not allowed by the rules or laws.

words.ex: The police seized illicit drugs from the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察从嫌疑人那里没收了非法毒品。
words.en: Illicit activities or substances are not allowed by law or by social or religious custom.

words.ex: He is an illustrator who draws pictures for children's books.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位为儿童书籍画画的插画师。
words.en: An illustrator is an artist who draws pictures, especially for books.

words.ex: He is an illustrious scientist who won many awards.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位杰出的科学家，获得过许多奖项。
words.en: If you describe someone as illustrious, you mean that they are very well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive.

words.tr: n. 低能；愚蠢的言行；愚蠢
words.ex: His imbecility was evident in the way he handled the situation.
words.ex_cn: 他处理事情的方式明显显示出他的愚钝。
words.en: The quality or state of being very stupid or foolish.

words.tr: adj. 清洁的；无瑕疵的；无过失的
words.ex: The kitchen was immaculate after she cleaned it.
words.ex_cn: 她打扫后，厨房非常干净。
words.en: If you describe something as immaculate, you mean that it is extremely clean, tidy, or neat.

words.tr: adj. 非物质的；无形的；不重要的
words.ex: The color is immaterial to the function.
words.ex_cn: 颜色对功能无关紧要。
words.en: If you say that something is immaterial, you mean that it is not important or not relevant.

words.ex: He immersed the cloth in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把布浸在水里。
words.en: To immerse something or someone means to put them into a liquid so that they are completely covered by it. It can also mean to involve oneself deeply in a particular activity or interest.

words.ex: The injured man was immobile after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，这名受伤的人无法移动。
words.en: If something is immobile, it is not moving or cannot move.

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.ex: The doctor will immunize the child against measles.
words.ex_cn: 医生会给这个孩子接种麻疹疫苗。
words.en: To immunize someone or something means to protect them against a disease by giving them a vaccine.

words.ex: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤损害了他走路的能力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.ex: The knight was impaled on the spear.
words.ex_cn: 骑士被长矛刺穿了。
words.en: To impale someone or something means to pierce them with a sharp object such as a spear or spike.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.tr:
adj. 慷慨激昂的；热烈的
v. 激起热情；使激动；“impassion”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He gave an impassioned speech about peace.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了充满激情的关于和平的演讲。
words.en: An impassioned speech or piece of writing is one that expresses very strong feelings about something.

words.ex: He remained impassive when he heard the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个坏消息时，他依然面无表情。
words.en: If someone is impassive, they do not show any emotion.

words.ex: The thick forest was impenetrable.
words.ex_cn: 这片茂密的森林无法穿越。
words.en: Impenetrable is used to describe something that cannot be passed through, entered, or understood.

words.tr: adj. 感觉不到的；极细微的
words.ex: The change was imperceptible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化肉眼无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is imperceptible is so small or slight that it cannot be seen or noticed.

words.ex: Smoking can imperil your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会危及你的健康。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk of being harmed, damaged, or destroyed.

words.ex: He tried to impersonate a police officer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图冒充一名警察。
words.en: To impersonate someone means to pretend to be that person, either to deceive people or to entertain them.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；无礼的；不相干的
words.ex: He gave an impertinent answer to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他给了老师一个鲁莽的回答。
words.en: If someone talks or behaves in a rather impolite and disrespectful way, especially towards someone who is older or in a position of authority, you can describe that person or their behaviour as impertinent.

words.ex: He made an impetuous decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他冲动地决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impetuous, you mean that they are likely to act quickly and suddenly without thinking or being careful.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: He made an impious joke about the sacred temple.
words.ex_cn: 他对神圣的寺庙开了一个不敬的玩笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as impious, you mean that they show a lack of respect for religious practices or beliefs.

words.tr: adj. 不能和解的；不能平息的
words.ex: He is an implacable enemy who never forgives.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个永不原谅的不可调和的敌人。
words.en: If you say that someone is implacable, you mean that they have very strong feelings of hostility or disapproval which nobody can change.

words.ex: She implored him to stay.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下。
words.en: If you implore someone to do something, you ask them to do it in a forceful, emotional way.

words.tr: n. 冒名顶替者；冒名行骗者
words.ex: He was exposed as an impostor who had been posing as a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他被揭露为一个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: An impostor is someone who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive people.

words.ex: The police impounded the stolen car.
words.ex_cn: 警察扣押了那辆被盗的汽车。
words.en: If something is impounded by police or other officials, they take it away because it is illegal or because it is evidence in a criminal case.

words.tr: adj. 坚不可摧的；不可战胜的
words.ex: The castle was impregnable during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争期间固若金汤。
words.en: An impregnable building or place is so strong and secure that it cannot be entered or captured by force.

words.tr: v. 使充满；灌注；使怀孕
words.ex: The rain impregnates the soil quickly.
words.ex_cn: 雨水迅速浸透了土壤。
words.en: To make a woman or female animal pregnant; to saturate or fill something with a substance.

words.ex: He is impressionable and easily believes what others say.
words.ex_cn: 他容易受影响，很容易相信别人说的话。
words.en: Someone who is impressionable is easily influenced by other people's opinions or actions.

words.tr:
v. 盖印；印刻；使铭记
n. 盖印；痕迹
words.ex: He used a stamp to imprint his name on the box.
words.ex_cn: 他用印章在盒子上盖印了他的名字。
words.en: To imprint something means to mark or stamp it with a design or a symbol. It can also mean to fix something firmly in someone's mind.

words.ex: The chair is inanimate.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是没有生命的。
words.en: Something that is inanimate is not alive, such as a rock or a chair. It can also describe something that lacks energy or spirit.

words.tr: adj. 不善言辞的；口齿不清的
words.ex: He was inarticulate when he tried to explain the problem.
words.ex_cn: 当他试图解释这个问题时，他表达不清。
words.en: If someone is inarticulate, they are unable to express themselves easily or well in speech.

words.tr: adj. 嵌入的；内在的；与生俱来的；
words.ex: The phone has an inbuilt camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有嵌入的摄像头。
words.en: If something is inbuilt, it is an original part of something or someone and cannot be separated from them.

words.tr:
adj. 化身的；人体化的
v. 化身为；体现
words.ex: He is the incarnate form of justice.
words.ex_cn: 他是正义的化身。
words.en: If you say that someone is a quality incarnate, you mean that they represent that quality or are typical of it in an extreme form.

words.tr:
adj. 引火的；燃烧的；纵火的；煽动的
n. 燃烧弹
words.ex: The incendiary device set the building on fire.
words.ex_cn: 这个引火装置把大楼点燃了。
words.en: An incendiary device is designed to cause fires. Incendiary remarks or actions are likely to cause anger or violence.

words.tr:
adj. 愤怒的；激怒了的
v. 使愤怒；激怒；“incense”的过去式与过去分词
words.ex: He was incensed when they lied to him.
words.ex_cn: 当他们对他撒谎时，他非常愤怒。
words.en: If you are incensed by something, it makes you extremely angry.

words.ex: He told the story about incest in the old family.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了那个关于家族乱伦的旧事。
words.en: Incest is sexual activity between family members or close relatives.

words.tr: v. 焚化；焚毁；把…烧成灰烬
words.ex: The city will incinerate the trash tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市明天将焚烧垃圾。
words.en: To incinerate something means to burn it until it is reduced to ash.

words.ex: His incisive comment solved the problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他一针见血的评论迅速解决了问题。
words.en: An incisive remark, question, or piece of writing is very clear and direct, and shows that the person understands something very well.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.tr: adj. 不连贯的；语无伦次的
words.ex: He was tired and gave an incoherent answer.
words.ex_cn: 他很累，给出了一个混乱的回答。
words.en: If someone is incoherent, they are talking in a confused and unclear way.

words.tr: adj. 即将开始的；新任的；
words.ex: The incoming class will start next week.
words.ex_cn: 即将开始的班级将在下周开课。
words.en: An incoming thing or person is arriving or being received.

words.ex: It is inconceivable that he forgot his own birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他忘了自己生日，这简直难以想象。
words.en: If something is inconceivable, it is impossible to imagine or believe because it is so unlikely.

words.tr: adj. 不容置疑的；无可否认的
words.ex: The evidence is incontrovertible.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If something is incontrovertible, it is definitely true and cannot be disputed.

words.ex: He looked incredulous when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他一脸难以置信。
words.en: If someone is incredulous, they are unable to believe something because it is very surprising or shocking.

words.ex: The hen incubate eggs until they hatch.
words.ex_cn: 母鸡孵化鸡蛋直到小鸡孵出。
words.en: to keep eggs warm so that they develop and hatch, or to keep cells, bacteria, etc. at a suitable temperature so that they develop

words.ex: The incubation of eggs takes about 21 days.
words.ex_cn: 鸡蛋的孵化需要大约21天。
words.en: The process of keeping eggs at the right temperature so that they develop and hatch, or the period of time that a disease takes to develop before symptoms appear.

words.tr: n. 孵卵器；育婴箱；培养的器具
words.ex: The eggs are kept in an incubator to hatch.
words.ex_cn: 鸡蛋放在孵卵器里孵化。
words.en: An incubator is a piece of hospital equipment which helps weak or small babies to survive. It consists of a transparent container in which the oxygen supply, temperature, and humidity can be controlled.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.ex: The army stopped the incursion at the border.
words.ex_cn: 军队在边境阻止了入侵。
words.en: An incursion is a sudden attack on or invasion of a place.

words.tr: n. 优柔寡断；犹豫不决
words.ex: He showed indecision when choosing between the two jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择两份工作时表现出犹豫不决。
words.en: Indecision is the inability to make decisions quickly and effectively.

words.ex: The memory of her smile is indelible.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的记忆是无法磨灭的。
words.en: If you say that something leaves an indelible impression, you mean that it is very unlikely to be forgotten.

words.ex: The insurance company agreed to indemnify the victims for their losses.
words.ex_cn: 保险公司同意赔偿受害者的损失。
words.en: To indemnify someone means to compensate them for harm or loss they have suffered.

words.ex: The company paid indemnity for the damaged car.
words.ex_cn: 公司为损坏的汽车支付了保险赔偿。
words.en: If something provides indemnity, it provides insurance or protection against damage or loss, especially in the form of a legal agreement.

words.ex: He did an in-depth study of the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题进行了深入的研究。
words.en: If you do something in depth, you do it very thoroughly and consider all the details.

words.tr: adj. 不确定的；不明确的
words.ex: The result is indeterminate.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不确定的。
words.en: If something is indeterminate, you cannot say exactly what it is.

words.ex: The court will indict him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将对他提起盗窃指控。
words.en: If someone is indicted for a crime, they are officially charged with it.

words.ex: He ate too much and had indigestion.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多了，导致消化不良。
words.en: Indigestion is pain or discomfort in your stomach, usually after eating, which is caused by difficulty in digesting food.

words.ex: The dye came from indigo plants.
words.ex_cn: 这种染料来自靛青植物。
words.en: A deep blue dye obtained from the indigo plant, or a color between blue and violet in the spectrum.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；不慎重的；鲁莽的
words.ex: He was indiscreet and told everyone the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不够谨慎，把秘密告诉了所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone as indiscreet, you mean that they do or say things in public which they should only do or say secretly or in private.

words.tr: adj. 不加选择的；不加区别的；
words.ex: The bombing was indiscriminate and hurt many civilians.
words.ex_cn: 这次轰炸是不加选择的，伤害了许多平民。
words.en: If you describe an action as indiscriminate, you are critical of it because it does not involve any careful thought or choice.

words.tr:
adj. 不舒服的；有病的；不愿意的
v. 使厌恶；使不适当；使不能；“indispose”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is indisposed today and cannot come to work.
words.ex_cn: 他今天身体不适，不能来上班。
words.en: If you say that someone is indisposed, you mean that they are not available because they are ill, or for a reason that you do not want to mention.

words.ex: The evidence is indisputable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可争辩的。
words.en: Something that is indisputable is true and cannot be denied or questioned.

words.ex: The two twins are indistinguishable in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 照片中的这对双胞胎难以区分。
words.en: If one thing is indistinguishable from another, the two things are so similar that it is difficult to know which is which or to tell them apart.

words.ex: They tried to indoctrinate the children with their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图用他们的信仰灌输孩子们。
words.en: To indoctrinate someone means to teach them a particular belief or set of beliefs, especially with the aim of making them accept it without questioning it.

words.tr: adj. 懒惰的；懒散的；好逸恶劳的
words.ex: He is indolent and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as indolent, you mean that they are lazy.

words.ex: His genius is indubitable.
words.ex_cn: 他的天才是不容置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something as indubitable, you mean that it is definitely true.

words.tr: v. 使正式就任；给予职位
words.ex: They inducted the new mayor with a ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过一场仪式使新市长正式就任。
words.en: To induct someone into a position or organization means to formally install them in that position or officially introduce them into that organization.

words.tr: adj. 无能的；不起作用的
words.ex: His attempts to solve the problem were ineffectual.
words.ex_cn: 他试图解决问题的尝试是无效的。
words.en: If someone or something is ineffectual, they lack the ability or power to achieve something.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的
words.ex: The outcome was ineluctable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不可避免的。
words.en: Something that is ineluctable cannot be avoided or escaped from.

words.tr: adj. 不适当的；无能的；笨拙的
words.ex: His inept reply made the situation worse.
words.ex_cn: 他不适当的回答让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you say that someone is inept, you are criticizing them because they do something with a complete lack of skill.

words.ex: The heat was inescapable in the small room.
words.ex_cn: 小房间里热得无法逃避。
words.en: If you describe a fact, situation, or activity as inescapable, you mean that it is difficult not to notice it or be affected by it.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；无法估计的
words.ex: Her kindness is inestimable.
words.ex_cn: 她的善良是无法估量的。
words.en: If you describe the value, benefit, or importance of something as inestimable, you mean that it is extremely great and cannot be calculated.

words.tr: adj. 用不完的；无穷无尽的；
words.ex: The sun provides an inexhaustible source of energy.
words.ex_cn: 太阳提供一种用不完的能量来源。
words.en: If you describe something as inexhaustible, you are emphasizing that there is a very large quantity of it and that it is not likely to be used up or to run out.

words.ex: The pope is considered infallible in matters of faith by some Catholics.
words.ex_cn: 一些天主教徒认为教皇在信仰问题上是一贯正确的。
words.en: If a person or thing is infallible, they are never wrong or never fail.

words.tr: adj. 婴儿的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: The infantile smile made everyone feel warm.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿般的微笑让每个人都感到温暖。
words.en: Infantile behavior or illnesses are typical of very young children.

words.ex: The infantry marched through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 步兵穿过森林行进。
words.en: Infantry refers to soldiers who fight on foot, especially in contrast to cavalry or artillery.

words.tr:
adj. 热恋着的；冲昏头脑的；入迷的
v. 使冲昏头脑；使着迷；“infatuate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She was infatuated with the new pop star.
words.ex_cn: 她对这位新晋流行歌手非常着迷。
words.en: If you are infatuated with someone, you have a very strong feeling of love or attraction for them, which usually does not last very long.

words.ex: Her infatuation with the movie star lasted only a few weeks.
words.ex_cn: 她对那位电影明星的迷恋只持续了几个星期。
words.en: An infatuation is an intense but short-lived passion or admiration for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 地狱的；恶魔似的；可憎的
words.ex: The heat in the room was infernal.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的热量像地狱一样。
words.en: If you describe something as infernal, you are emphasizing that it is extremely annoying or unpleasant.

words.ex: The company is suffering from severe infighting among senior executives.
words.ex_cn: 公司正遭受高层管理人员之间的严重内斗。
words.en: Infighting refers to conflict or competition between members of the same group or organization, often leading to a negative impact on the group's effectiveness or cohesion.

words.ex: The spy tried to infiltrate the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 间谍试图渗透敌方基地。
words.en: To enter or gain access to (an organization, place, etc.) surreptitiously and gradually, especially in order to acquire secret information.

words.ex: The old man is infirm and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人身体虚弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: If someone is infirm, they are weak or ill, and often old.

words.ex: His infirmity made it hard to walk.
words.ex_cn: 他的虚弱使他走路困难。
words.en: An infirmity is a physical or mental weakness.

words.ex: His rude words inflamed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了人群。
words.en: To inflame a situation or feeling means to make it much more intense or serious.

words.tr:
adj. 发炎的；红肿的
v. 激怒；加剧；发炎；“inflame”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His skin is inflamed after the bug bite.
words.ex_cn: 他被虫子叮咬后皮肤发炎了。
words.en: If part of your body is inflamed, it is red or swollen, usually as a result of an infection, injury, or illness.

words.ex: The sign says the material is inflammable.
words.ex_cn: 标志上说这种材料是易燃的。
words.en: Easily set on fire; capable of burning quickly and intensely.

words.tr: n. 发炎；炎症；燃烧；激动
words.ex: The redness and swelling show inflammation.
words.ex_cn: 发红和肿胀表明有炎症。
words.en: Inflammation is a condition in which a part of your body becomes red, swollen, and painful as a reaction to infection or injury.

words.ex: The swollen area is inflammatory and painful.
words.ex_cn: 这个肿胀的部位是发炎的，并且很痛。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behaviour as inflammatory, you mean that it is likely to cause people to react very angrily.

words.tr: n. 变音；转调；曲折变化
words.ex: The dog's voice has a happy inflection.
words.ex_cn: 狗的声音带着愉快的语调。
words.en: Inflection refers to the modification of a word to express different grammatical categories such as tense, case, voice, aspect, person, number, gender, and mood.

words.ex: The rules are inflexible and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则是不灵活的，不能更改。
words.en: If you say that someone is inflexible, you are criticizing them because they refuse to change their mind or alter their way of doing things.

words.tr:
adj. 红外线的
n. 红外线
words.ex: The remote uses infrared to change the TV channel.
words.ex_cn: 遥控器使用红外线来切换电视频道。
words.en: Infrared refers to the region of the electromagnetic spectrum with wavelengths longer than visible light but shorter than microwaves, often used in technology for night vision and heat sensing.

words.ex: The teacher tried to infuse confidence into the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师试图向学生注入信心。
words.en: If you infuse a quality into someone or something, you fill them with it. If a quality infuses something, it is present throughout it.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；天真的；坦率的
words.ex: He gave an ingenuous smile when he told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当他讲真话时，他露出了天真无邪的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as ingenuous, you mean that they are innocent, trusting, and honest, often in a way that seems naive.

words.tr: adj. 不名誉的；不光彩的
words.ex: He felt inglorious after losing the match without trying.
words.ex_cn: 他在没有努力的情况下输掉比赛后，感到很丢脸。
words.en: If you describe something as inglorious, you mean that it is completely without fame or glory and is considered shameful.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；生染的； v. “ingrain”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: His ingrained habits are hard to change.
words.ex_cn: 他根深蒂固的习惯很难改变。
words.en: If something is ingrained, it is firmly established and therefore difficult to change.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.tr:
adj. 讨好的；逢迎的
v. 使讨好；使得到…的欢心；“ingratiate”的现在分词
words.ex: His ingratiating manner made him many friends.
words.ex_cn: 他讨好的态度为他赢得了很多朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as ingratiating, you mean that they try to make people like them by being very pleasant and agreeable, often in a way that seems insincere.

words.ex: He inhale the fresh air in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他早上吸入新鲜空气。
words.en: To inhale means to breathe in air, smoke, or gas.

words.ex: The court issued an injunction to stop the construction.
words.ex_cn: 法院下达了命令，停止施工。
words.en: An injunction is a court order, usually one telling someone not to do something.

words.ex: Smoking is injurious to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is injurious causes harm or damage.

words.ex: She had only the faintest inkling of what he was planning.
words.ex_cn: 她对他正在策划的事情只有一点模糊的概念。
words.en: An inkling is a slight knowledge or suspicion of something.

words.tr: adj. 嵌入的；镶嵌的；镶饰的； v. “inlay”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The table has an inlaid wooden design.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子有嵌入的木制图案。
words.en: Inlaid is the past tense and past participle of inlay, which means to embed pieces of a material into a surface to create a decorative pattern.

words.ex: The innermost part of the box was empty.
words.ex_cn: 盒子最内部是空的。
words.en: The innermost part of something is the part that is farthest from its edges or its surface.

words.ex: The company wants to innovate its production process.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司想改革它的生产流程。
words.en: To innovate means to introduce changes and new ideas in the way something is done or made.

words.tr: adj. 无害的；不触犯人的；不讨厌的
words.ex: He gave an inoffensive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个无害的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as inoffensive, you mean that they are not unpleasant or unacceptable in any way.

words.ex: He spent inordinate time on video games.
words.ex_cn: 他花了过多的时间玩电子游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as inordinate, you are emphasizing that it is unusually or excessively large in amount or degree.

words.ex: The inquisition into the company's financial records uncovered fraudulent activities.
words.ex_cn: 对公司财务记录的调查揭露了欺诈行为。
words.en: An inquisition is an official investigation, especially one which is very thorough and uses harsh methods.

words.tr: n. 精神错乱；精神失常；疯狂
words.ex: He was sent to a hospital because of insanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因精神错乱被送进了医院。
words.en: Insanity is the state of being seriously mentally ill; madness.

words.ex: He has an insatiable hunger for knowledge.
words.ex_cn: 他对知识有着无法满足的渴望。
words.en: If someone is insatiable, they always want more of something and are never satisfied.

words.tr:
n. 插入物；嵌图
v. 嵌入（作为装饰）；套印
adj. 镶嵌着…的
words.ex: He put an inset of the map on the poster.
words.ex_cn: 他在海报上加了一个地图的小插图。
words.en: An inset is a small picture or diagram that is inserted into a larger one.

words.tr: adj. 淡而无味的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The soup was insipid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as insipid, you mean that it is very weak, tasteless, or uninteresting.

words.tr: adv. 在这个范围；到这种程度
words.ex: I agree with you insofar as you want to help others.
words.ex_cn: 在你想帮助别人的范围内，我同意你。
words.en: to the degree or extent that

words.tr: adj. 无法解决的；不能溶解的
words.ex: The problem is insoluble with the current tools.
words.ex_cn: 用当前的工具无法解决这个问题。
words.en: If a problem or mystery is insoluble, it is impossible to solve or explain.

words.ex: He has insomnia and cannot sleep at night.
words.ex_cn: 他有失眠症，晚上睡不着。
words.en: If someone suffers from insomnia, they find it difficult to sleep.

words.tr:
n. 失眠患者
adj. 患失眠症的
words.ex: He is an insomniac and sleeps very little at night.
words.ex_cn: 他是个失眠者，晚上睡得很晚。
words.en: An insomniac is a person who is regularly unable to sleep.

words.ex: The car stopped in an instantaneous moment.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在瞬间停了下来。
words.en: Happening or done immediately.

words.ex: He walks in step with his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友齐步走。
words.en: If people are in step, they are moving in time to a rhythm or in agreement with each other.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.ex: The language barrier was insuperable for him.
words.ex_cn: 语言障碍对他来说是难以克服的。
words.en: If you describe a problem or obstacle as insuperable, you mean that it is impossible to overcome.

words.tr:
n. 起义者；叛乱者；造反者
adj. 叛乱的；起义的
words.ex: The insurgent attacked the village at night.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱分子在夜里袭击了村庄。
words.en: An insurgent is a person who rises in active revolt against an established authority or government.

words.tr: adj. 无法克服的；难以解决的；不可逾越的
words.ex: The problem seemed insurmountable.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题似乎无法克服。
words.en: If you describe something as insurmountable, you mean that it is so great or severe that it cannot be dealt with.

words.ex: The doctor checked his daily intake of sugar.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他每天的糖摄入量。
words.en: The process of taking something in, especially food, air, or information.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.ex: The number 5 is an integer.
words.ex_cn: 数字5是一个整数。
words.en: An integer is a whole number that can be positive, negative, or zero.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.tr: adj. 互相依赖的；相倚的；
words.ex: The two countries are interdependent in trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上互相依赖。
words.en: If two or more things are interdependent, they depend on each other.

words.ex: The phone has a simple interface.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个简单的界面。
words.en: An interface is a point where two systems, subjects, organizations, etc. meet and interact.

words.ex: He interjected during the meeting to ask a question.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议中插话问了一个问题。
words.en: To say something that interrupts someone who is speaking.

words.tr: n. 感叹词；插入之语词
words.ex: He shouted 'Wow!' as an interjection.
words.ex_cn: 他喊了一声‘哇！’作为感叹词。
words.en: An interjection is a word or phrase that expresses a strong feeling or emotion, such as surprise, pleasure, or anger, and is often used in speech to interrupt or emphasize a statement.

words.ex: The interlocutor asked a series of probing questions.
words.ex_cn: 对话者提出了一系列尖锐的问题。
words.en: An interlocutor is someone who takes part in a conversation or dialogue, often in a formal or official capacity.

words.tr: n. 闯入者；干涉他人事务者
words.ex: The interloper walked into the meeting without permission.
words.ex_cn: 那个闯入者未经允许走进了会议。
words.en: An interloper is someone who becomes involved in a situation or place where they are not wanted or are considered not to belong.

words.tr: n. 间歇；插曲；幕间节目
words.ex: He took an interlude to drink water.
words.ex_cn: 他休息了一下喝水。
words.en: An interlude is a short period of time that comes in the middle of something, or a short piece of music, talk, or entertainment that comes between the main parts of a performance or event.

words.ex: He acted as an intermediary between the two sides.
words.ex_cn: 他充当了双方之间的中间人。
words.en: An intermediary is a person who acts as a link between people or groups in order to try to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: The interment took place at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 葬礼在日出时举行。
words.en: The act or ceremony of burying a dead body.

words.ex: The meeting felt interminable.
words.ex_cn: 这场会议感觉没完没了。
words.en: If you describe something as interminable, you are emphasizing that it continues for a very long time and indicating that you find it boring or annoying.

words.ex: The interplay between light and shadow creates beauty.
words.ex_cn: 光与影的相互作用创造了美。
words.en: The way in which two or more things have an effect on each other.

words.ex: The police will interrogate the suspect tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 警察明天会审问嫌疑人。
words.en: To interrogate someone means to ask them a lot of questions for a long time in order to get information, sometimes using threats.

words.ex: The doctor checked his intestinal health.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的肠道健康。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the intestines.

words.ex: They share intimacy through quiet talks at night.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过夜晚的安静交谈建立亲密感。
words.en: A close, familiar, and usually affectionate or loving personal relationship with another person or group.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.tr:
adj. 醉人的
n. 酒精饮料；致醉药物
words.ex: Alcohol is a common intoxicant.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是一种常见的致醉物。
words.en: An intoxicant is a substance that can cause intoxication, such as alcohol or drugs.

words.tr: v.  使中毒；使醉；使 ...陶醉
words.ex: The dirty water can intoxicate animals.
words.ex_cn: 脏水会使动物中毒。
words.en: To intoxicate someone means to make them lose control of their actions or behavior because they have drunk alcohol or taken drugs. It can also mean to make someone feel very excited and happy.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.tr: adj. 不妥协的；不让步的
words.ex: He is intransigent about his opinions.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的观点毫不让步。
words.en: If you describe someone as intransigent, you mean that they refuse to behave differently or to change their attitude to something.

words.ex: The bird sang intransitively.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟唱了，没有宾语。
words.en: An intransitive verb is a verb that does not take a direct object.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.ex: The intricacy of the clock made it very special.
words.ex_cn: 这座钟的复杂精细让它非常特别。
words.en: The quality of being intricate; complexity.

words.tr:
v. 密谋；激起…的兴趣
n. 阴谋诡计；密谋策划
words.ex: They intrigue to take over the company.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋接管这家公司。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.tr: adj. 引起兴趣的；引人入胜的； v. “intrigue”的现在分词；
words.ex: The mystery story was intriguing.
words.ex_cn: 这个侦探故事很引人入胜。
words.en: If you describe something as intriguing, you mean that it is interesting or strange.

words.ex: He spent the evening in introspection.
words.ex_cn: 他整个晚上都在反省。
words.en: The examination of one's own thoughts, feelings, and sensations; self-examination.

words.tr: n. 内向的人；不喜欢与人交往的人
words.ex: He is an introvert who likes reading alone.
words.ex_cn: 他是个喜欢独自读书的内向者。
words.en: An introvert is a person who tends to shrink from social contacts and to become preoccupied with their own thoughts.

words.ex: His intrusive questions made her uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他打搅的问题让她感到不舒服。
words.en: Something that is intrusive disturbs your privacy or peace in an unwanted way.

words.ex: I trusted my intuition and chose the right answer.
words.ex_cn: 我相信自己的直觉，选了正确的答案。
words.en: Intuition is the ability to understand or know something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.

words.ex: The app has an intuitive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个应用程序具有直观的设计。
words.en: An intuitive idea or feeling is based on an instinctive emotional response rather than on conscious thought.

words.ex: The mistake will invalidate the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误会使结果无效。
words.en: To invalidate something such as a contract or an election means to make it officially not valid.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；积习难改的
words.ex: He is an inveterate smoker who cannot quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个根深蒂固的吸烟者，无法戒掉。
words.en: If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.

words.tr: adj. 招致不满的；不公平的；难以决定的
words.ex: He made an invidious comparison between his two students.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的两个学生做了令人不快的比较。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as invidious, you mean that it is likely to make you unpopular because it is unpleasant or difficult to do.

words.ex: The teacher will invigilate the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师将监考这场考试。
words.en: To supervise candidates during an examination to prevent cheating.

words.ex: The invigilator walked around the exam room.
words.ex_cn: 监考员在考场里走动。
words.en: An invigilator is someone whose job is to watch people taking an examination in order to check that they do not cheat.

words.tr: adj. 不可征服的；不能战胜的
words.ex: He felt invincible after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 赢得比赛后，他觉得自己不可战胜。
words.en: If someone or something is invincible, they are impossible to defeat or overcome.

words.ex: The priest's invocation helped the crowd feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 牧师的祈祷让人群感到平静。
words.en: An invocation is a request for help or forgiveness made to a god.

words.tr:
n. 发票；发货单；
v. 开发票；记清单；
words.ex: He paid the bill after receiving the invoice.
words.ex_cn: 他收到发票后付了款。
words.en: An invoice is a document that lists goods or services that have been provided and says how much money you owe for them.

words.tr: adj. 不会受伤害的；攻不破的；固若金汤的
words.ex: The fortress was said to be invulnerable.
words.ex_cn: 这座要塞据说无懈可击。
words.en: If someone or something is invulnerable, they cannot be harmed or damaged.

words.ex: The doctor gave him iodide to help his thyroid.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他碘化物来帮助他的甲状腺。
words.en: A compound of iodine with another element or group, especially a salt of the anion I⁻.

words.ex: He took iodine to help his thyroid.
words.ex_cn: 他服用碘来帮助他的甲状腺。
words.en: A chemical element of the halogen group, essential for the production of thyroid hormones.

words.ex: The ion moves quickly in the water.
words.ex_cn: 这个离子在水中快速移动。
words.en: An ion is an atom or molecule with a net electric charge due to the loss or gain of one or more electrons.

words.ex: He is irascible when he wakes up late.
words.ex_cn: 他起床晚时容易发怒。
words.en: If you describe someone as irascible, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.tr: v. 使恼怒；使厌烦；使烦恼
words.ex: The loud noise irks her every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早上，巨大的噪音都让她感到烦躁。
words.en: To irritate, annoy, or exasperate someone.

words.tr: adj. 使人厌烦的；令人生气的
words.ex: The irksome noise from the construction site kept me awake all night.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的恼人噪音让我整晚都没睡着。
words.en: If something is irksome, it annoys you.

words.tr: v. 照射；用放射线处理；使明亮
words.ex: The sun irradiates the earth every day.
words.ex_cn: 太阳每天照射地球。
words.en: To expose to radiation; to illuminate or enlighten.

words.tr: adj. 不能调和的；无法化解的；不兼容的
words.ex: Their views are irreconcilable.
words.ex_cn: 他们的观点无法调和。
words.en: If two things such as opinions or proposals are irreconcilable, they are so different from each other that it is not possible to believe or have both of them.

words.tr: adj. 不能减缩的；无法减轻的
words.ex: This fraction is irreducible.
words.ex_cn: 这个分数是最简形式。
words.en: If you describe something as irreducible, you mean that it cannot be made smaller or simpler.

words.tr: adj. 不能修复的；不可弥补的；无可挽救的
words.ex: The damage was irreparable.
words.ex_cn: 损坏是无法修复的。
words.en: If something is irreparable, it cannot be repaired or corrected.

words.ex: Her irrepressible laugh filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 她抑制不住的笑声充满了房间。
words.en: If someone is irrepressible, they are full of energy and enthusiasm and cannot be controlled or stopped.

words.ex: He went for a walk irrespective of the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾下雨去散步了。
words.en: If something is done or happens irrespective of particular factors, it is not influenced or affected by them.

words.tr: adj. 不能挽回的；不能复原的
words.ex: The damage to the painting was deemed irretrievable.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的损坏被认为是无法修复的。
words.en: If something is irretrievable, it cannot be recovered or corrected.

words.tr: adj. 不敬的；不逊的；无礼的
words.ex: He made an irreverent joke about the king.
words.ex_cn: 他对国王开了一个不敬的玩笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as irreverent, you mean that they do not show respect for people or things that are generally respected.

words.ex: The damage to the environment is irreversible.
words.ex_cn: 对环境的破坏是不可逆转的。
words.en: If a change is irreversible, it cannot be changed back to how it was before.

words.tr: adj. 无法改变的；不能取消的
words.ex: The decision was irrevocable.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定是不可撤销的。
words.en: If a decision, action, or process is irrevocable, it cannot be changed or reversed.

words.tr: n. 刺激物；令人烦恼的事物；
words.ex: Smoke is an irritant to the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾对眼睛是一种刺激物。
words.en: An irritant is something that causes irritation, especially physical irritation.

words.tr: n. 突然冲入；急速增加
words.ex: The irruption of birds scared the children.
words.ex_cn: 鸟群的突然涌入吓到了孩子们。
words.en: An irruption is a sudden, violent, or forcible entry or invasion.

words.ex: The map shows an isotherm at 20 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 地图上标出了20度的等温线。
words.en: A line on a map connecting points having the same temperature at a given time or on average over a given period.

words.tr:
adj. 等温的；等温线的
n. 等温线
words.ex: The gas expands in an isothermal process.
words.ex_cn: 气体在一个等温过程中膨胀。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a process or condition in which the temperature remains constant.

words.ex: This isotope is used in medical tests.
words.ex_cn: 这种同位素用于医学检查。
words.en: An isotope is one of two or more forms of the same chemical element. Different isotopes of an element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in their nuclei.

words.ex: The issuance of new passports takes two weeks.
words.ex_cn: 新护照的发放需要两周时间。
words.en: The act of officially making something available or known to the public, especially a new product or a piece of information.

words.tr:
n. 痒；渴望
v. （使）痒；渴望
words.ex: The mosquito bite caused an itchy on my arm.
words.ex_cn: 蚊子叮咬让我的手臂发痒。
words.en: If you have an itch, you have an unpleasant feeling on your skin that makes you want to scratch. If you itch to do something, you are very eager or impatient to do it.

words.tr: v. 列出清单；逐条列记
words.ex: He will itemize his expenses on the form.
words.ex_cn: 他将在表格上逐项列出他的开支。
words.en: To itemize means to list things separately, often including details about each one.

words.tr:
adj. 巡回的；流动的
n. 四处奔波的人；流浪者
words.ex: The itinerant worker moves from town to town for jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这位流动工人为了工作从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: Someone who is itinerant travels from place to place, usually because they have no permanent home or job, or because they are involved in a particular activity that requires this.

words.ex: Ivy climbs the old wall.
words.ex_cn: 常春藤爬上了旧墙。
words.en: Ivy is a climbing plant with dark green shiny leaves.

words.ex: The child laughed when the jack-in-the-box popped out.
words.ex_cn: 当玩偶从盒子里弹出来时，孩子笑了。
words.en: A toy consisting of a box from which a figure on a spring jumps up when the lid is opened.

words.tr: n. 万事通；杂而不精的人
words.ex: He is a jack-of-all-trades who fixes cars, cooks meals, and teaches kids.
words.ex_cn: 他是个万能的人，会修车、做饭和教孩子。
words.en: A person who can do many different types of work but who perhaps does not do any of them very well.

words.ex: She wore a necklace made of jade.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条玉制的项链。
words.en: A hard, typically green stone used for ornaments and implements and consisting of the minerals jadeite or nephrite.

words.tr: adj. 锯齿状的； v. “jag”的过去式；
words.ex: The jagged edge of the rock cut his hand.
words.ex_cn: 岩石的锯齿状边缘割伤了他的手。
words.en: Something that is jagged has a rough, uneven shape or edge with lots of sharp points.

words.ex: The janitor cleans the school every night.
words.ex_cn: 门卫每天晚上打扫学校。
words.en: A janitor is a person whose job is to take care of a building, especially by cleaning it.

words.ex: He used too much jargon in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中用了太多行话。
words.en: Special words or expressions that are used by a particular profession or group and are difficult for others to understand.

words.ex: She smells the jasmine in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里闻着茉莉花的香味。
words.en: A shrub or climbing plant which bears fragrant flowers used in perfumery or tea.

words.ex: He threw the javelin farther than anyone else.
words.ex_cn: 他投出的标枪比任何人都远。
words.en: A javelin is a light spear designed primarily for casting as a ranged weapon.

words.ex: He jaywalks across the street without looking.
words.ex_cn: 他不看路就横穿马路。
words.en: To jaywalk means to cross a street in a careless and dangerous way, or in an illegal place.

words.ex: The jellyfish floated gently in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 水母在海里轻轻漂浮。
words.en: A jellyfish is a sea creature with a soft, clear body and long tentacles that can sting.

words.ex: Don't jeopardize your health by skipping meals.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为不吃饭而危及你的健康。
words.en: To jeopardize something means to do something that may destroy it or cause it to be lost.

words.tr:
adj. 急动的；颠簸的；抽筋的
n. 肉干
words.ex: His jerky movements made the camera footage blurry.
words.ex_cn: 他急动的动作让视频画面变得模糊。
words.en: If you describe something as jerky, you mean that it moves in a way that is not smooth, but rather with sudden stops and starts.

words.tr:
n. 防波堤；码头
adj. 乌黑发亮的；黑玉似的
words.ex: The fisherman walks on the jetty to check his nets.
words.ex_cn: 渔夫走在码头上检查他的渔网。
words.en: A jetty is a structure that extends from the shore into the water and is used to protect a harbor or shoreline from the effects of currents, tides, and waves, or to provide a berthing place for vessels.

words.ex: He used a jigsaw to cut the wooden board.
words.ex_cn: 他用竖锯切割木板。
words.en: A jigsaw is a machine with a fine blade used for cutting shapes in wood or metal. It is also a puzzle consisting of a picture printed on cardboard or wood and cut into various pieces of different shapes that have to be fitted together.

words.tr:
n. 叮当声；广告歌
v. （使）发出叮当声
words.ex: The bells make a happy jingle in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天里，铃铛发出愉快的叮当声。
words.en: A jingle is a short, simple tune, often with words, that is used to advertise a product or service on the radio or television.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；爱开玩笑的；滑稽的
words.ex: He is jocular during breaks, making everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他在休息时很幽默，让大家笑个不停。
words.en: If you say that someone has a jocular manner, you mean that they are cheerful and often make jokes or try to make people laugh.

words.ex: He jogs every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上慢跑以保持健康。
words.en: To run at a slow, steady pace, especially as a form of exercise.

words.tr: n. 操纵杆；（游戏机的）游戏棒
words.ex: The boy moves the character with a joystick.
words.ex_cn: 男孩用操纵杆控制角色移动。
words.en: A joystick is an input device consisting of a stick that pivots on a base and reports its angle or direction to the device it is controlling.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使杂乱
n. 杂乱；混乱
words.ex: He jumbled the letters and could not read the word.
words.ex_cn: 他把字母弄乱了，无法认出这个单词。
words.en: To mix things together in a confused or untidy way.

words.tr: n. 管辖权；司法权；裁判权；
words.ex: The court has jurisdiction over this case.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这个案件有管辖权。
words.en: The official power to make legal decisions and judgments.

words.ex: The juror voted guilty after listening to the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 这位陪审员在听取证据后投票判定有罪。
words.en: A juror is a member of a jury, which is a group of people in a court of law who listen to the facts of a case and decide whether someone is guilty or not.

words.ex: He juxtaposes old photos with new ones.
words.ex_cn: 他把老照片和新照片放在一起。
words.en: To place or deal with close together for contrasting effect.

words.ex: The ship's keel was damaged in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 船的龙骨在风暴中受损了。
words.en: The keel is the central structural basis of a ship or boat, running along the bottom from the bow to the stern. It is the first part of a ship's hull to be constructed and is the primary structural element that provides stability and strength to the vessel.

words.tr:
n. 狗舍；养狗场
v. 把…置于狗舍
words.ex: The dog sleeps in a kennel at night.
words.ex_cn: 狗晚上睡在狗窝里。
words.en: A kennel is a small hut made for a dog to sleep in, or a place where dogs are bred or looked after.

words.ex: The kernel of the computer is the operating system.
words.ex_cn: 计算机的核心是操作系统。
words.en: The kernel of something such as a nut or a seed is the part inside the shell. The kernel of an idea or a theory is the central and most important part of it.

words.tr: n. （足球）开球；（社会集会等）开始
words.ex: The kick-off is at 7 p.m. tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 开场时间是明天晚上7点。
words.en: The kick-off is the start of a football game or other event, marked by the first kick of the ball.

words.ex: She invited all her kin to the family reunion.
words.ex_cn: 她邀请了所有亲属参加家庭聚会。
words.en: Your kin are your relatives.

words.tr:
n. 亲属；血缘关系
adj. 同源的；类似的
words.ex: He visited his kindred during the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 他在假期里探望了他的亲属。
words.en: If two people or things are kindred, they are similar in some way, often because they are related.

words.ex: The kiwi is a flightless bird from New Zealand.
words.ex_cn: 几维鸟是一种来自新西兰的不会飞的鸟。
words.en: A kiwi is a flightless bird native to New Zealand, or the fruit of a Chinese gooseberry vine, which is also known as kiwifruit.

words.ex: He kneads dough every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上揉面团。
words.en: To knead is to press and stretch dough or another substance with your hands in order to make it smooth and ready to use.

words.tr: n. 实际知识；技术；窍门
words.ex: He has the know-how to fix the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他有修理这台机器的诀窍。
words.en: Practical knowledge or expertise in a particular field or area.

words.ex: Cleaning the whole house is a laborious task.
words.ex_cn: 打扫整个房子是一项耗时费力的任务。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as laborious, you mean that it takes a lot of time and effort.

words.tr: n. 拉格啤酒；贮藏啤酒
words.ex: He drinks lager at the pub.
words.ex_cn: 他在酒吧喝拉格啤酒。
words.en: A type of beer that is stored at a low temperature for a period of time to allow it to mature and develop its flavor.

words.ex: The children swam in the clear lagoon.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在清澈的潟湖里游泳。
words.en: A lagoon is a body of water separated from larger bodies of water by a natural barrier such as a sandbar, coral reef, or barrier island.

words.ex: The knight held a long lance in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 骑士手中握着一支长矛。
words.en: A lance is a long weapon used in the past by soldiers on horseback, consisting of a wooden shaft with a pointed metal end. As a verb, to lance means to pierce or cut open with a sharp instrument, especially a lance.

words.tr: adj. 无精打采的；疲倦无力的
words.ex: He gave a languid smile before lying down.
words.ex_cn: 他躺下前给了一个慵懒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as languid, you mean that they show little energy or interest and are very slow and casual in their movements.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.ex: He has laryngitis and cannot speak loudly.
words.ex_cn: 他得了喉炎，不能大声说话。
words.en: Laryngitis is an inflammation of the larynx, typically resulting in huskiness or loss of the voice, harsh breathing, and a painful cough.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.tr:
n. 车床
v. 用车床加工
words.ex: He uses a lathe to shape wood.
