words.en: Sleep is the natural state of rest in which your eyes are closed, your body is inactive, and your mind is unconscious.

words.ex: The school used to segregate students by race.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去按种族隔离学生。
words.en: To segregate means to separate one group of people, animals, or things from another, especially because they are of different types or belong to different categories.

words.tr: n. 隔离；分离；种族隔离；
words.ex: The school practiced racial segregation in the past.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去实行种族隔离。
words.en: Segregation is the policy or practice of separating people of different races, sexes, or religions and treating them in a different way.

words.ex: Selenium is often used in solar cells.
words.ex_cn: 硒常用于太阳能电池中。
words.en: Selenium is a nonmetal with properties that are intermediate between those of its periodic table column-adjacent chalcogen elements sulfur and tellurium.

words.ex: His philosophy embraced the concept of self-annihilation as a path to spiritual enlightenment.
words.ex_cn: 他的哲学接纳了自我消失作为精神启迪之路的概念。
words.en: The act of destroying oneself or causing one's own destruction.

words.tr: adj. 自我谦避的；不求闻达的
words.ex: She was self-effacing and never sought the limelight.
words.ex_cn: 她为人谦逊，从不追求聚光灯下的生活。
words.en: Someone who is self-effacing does not like to attract attention to themselves or to their abilities or achievements.

words.tr: adj. 自我应验的；自我实现的
words.ex: The prophecy became a self-fulfilling prophecy when people started to act as if it were true.
words.ex_cn: 当人们开始表现得好像预言是真的时，预言就变成了自我实现的预言。
words.en: A self-fulfilling prophecy or prediction is one that becomes true because people expect it to be true and behave in ways that make it happen.

words.ex: He is a self-made businessman.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位白手起家的商人。
words.en: A self-made person is someone who has become successful and rich through their own efforts, especially if they started life without money, education, or high social status.

words.ex: He was criticized for being self-opinionated and unwilling to listen to others.
words.ex_cn: 他因固执己见、不愿听取他人意见而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe someone as self-opinionated, you are critical of them because they are very confident of their own opinions and unwilling to accept that they may be wrong.

words.tr: adj. 有自制力的；沉着的；镇静的
words.ex: She remained self-possessed even when the news shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 即使这个消息让所有人都震惊了，她依然保持冷静自制。
words.en: If you are self-possessed, you are calm and confident and in control of your emotions.

words.tr: n. 自卫；自保；自我保护
words.ex: The animal acted out of self-preservation when it ran away from the predator.
words.ex_cn: 当动物从捕食者身边逃跑时，它是出于自卫。
words.en: Self-preservation is the instinctive behavior that protects an organism from harm or death.

words.ex: He is a self-styled expert in ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 他自称是古代历史专家。
words.en: If you describe someone as self-styled, you disapprove of them because they have given themselves a title or description that you think they have no right to.

words.tr: adj. 固执己见的；任性的
words.ex: She was known for her self-willed nature, often going against the advice of others.
words.ex_cn: 她以任性的性格著称，经常不听别人的建议。
words.en: Someone who is self-willed is determined to do what they want and not what other people want them to do.

words.ex: The word 'bank' has different semantic meanings.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'bank' 有不同的语义含义。
words.en: Semantic is used to describe something that relates to the meanings of words and sentences.

words.ex: He is learning semantics in his linguistics class.
words.ex_cn: 他正在语言学课上学习语义学。
words.en: Semantics is the study of meaning in language, including the ways in which words and sentences convey information.

words.tr: n. 外观；样子；相似；表象
words.ex: She tried to maintain a semblance of normality.
words.ex_cn: 她试图维持一种正常的假象。
words.en: The outward appearance or apparent form of something, especially when the reality is different.

words.ex: That paper was a seminal work in computer science.
words.ex_cn: 那篇论文是计算机科学领域一部影响深远的著作。
words.en: Seminal is used to describe things such as books, works, events, and people that have a great influence in a particular field.

words.tr: adj. 参议院的；参议员的
words.ex: He was elected to the senatorial office.
words.ex_cn: 他被选举为参议员。
words.en: Relating to a senate or a senator.

words.ex: Her senility made it difficult for her to remember recent events.
words.ex_cn: 她的衰老使她难以记住最近发生的事情。
words.en: Senility refers to the mental and physical decline associated with old age, often characterized by memory loss, confusion, and a decrease in cognitive abilities.

words.ex: The robot uses a sensor to detect walls.
words.ex_cn: 机器人使用传感器来检测墙壁。
words.en: A sensor is a device which reacts to certain physical conditions or impressions such as heat or light, and which is used to provide information.

words.ex: The sensory experience of eating chocolate is wonderful.
words.ex_cn: 吃巧克力的感觉体验很棒。
words.en: Sensory means relating to the physical senses of touch, smell, taste, hearing, and sight.

words.tr: adj. 感官的；肉欲的；愉悦感官的；耽于肉欲的
words.ex: The sensual smell of fresh bread made her hungry.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的感官香味让她感到饥饿。
words.en: Relating to or involving gratification of the senses and physical, especially sexual, pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 感觉上的；感官的；（引起）美感的
words.ex: She wore a sensuous silk dress.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件性感的丝绸裙子。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the senses rather than the intellect; characterized by a pleasing or luxurious quality that appeals to the senses.

words.ex: The sentry stands guard at the gate.
words.ex_cn: 哨兵站在门口站岗。
words.en: A sentry is a soldier stationed at a place to stand guard and prevent surprise attacks.

words.tr:
n. 分离主义者；独立主义者
adj. 分裂主义的；独立主义的
words.ex: The separatist group wants to leave the country.
words.ex_cn: 这个分离主义团体希望脱离这个国家。
words.en: A separatist is a person who supports the separation of a particular group of people from a larger body on the basis of ethnicity, religion, or gender.

words.tr: n. 坟墓；圣物置放处; vt. 埋葬
words.ex: The ancient sepulcher was discovered during the excavation.
words.ex_cn: 在挖掘过程中发现了这座古老的坟墓。
words.en: A sepulcher is a burial chamber or tomb, especially one that is large and impressive.

words.ex: The movie had a sequel that came out last year.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有一部去年上映的续集。
words.en: A sequel is a book, film, or play that continues the story of a previous one.

words.tr:
adj. 锯齿状的；有锯齿的
v. 使成锯齿状；“serrate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The blade of the knife was serrated for cutting bread.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀的刀刃是锯齿状的，适合切面包。
words.en: Having a row of small sharp projections along the edge like a saw.

words.tr: n. 血清；（植物分泌的）浆液
words.ex: The doctor tested his serum for bacteria.
words.ex_cn: 医生检测了他的血清是否含有细菌。
words.en: Serum is the liquid part of the blood that remains after the blood has clotted, containing antibodies and other proteins.

words.tr: adj. 能用的；耐用的；有用的
words.ex: The old car is still serviceable.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧车仍然可以使用。
words.en: If something is serviceable, it is in good enough condition to be used.

words.ex: He despised the servility of his subordinates.
words.ex_cn: 他鄙视下属的奴性。
words.en: Servility is the quality of being too willing to serve or please someone else, often in a way that shows a lack of self-respect.

words.tr:
n. (小说，电影，戏剧等中）固定套路；防攻套路
adj. 事先精心安排的
words.ex: The set-piece goal was a result of meticulous planning.
words.ex_cn: 定位进攻的进球是精心策划的结果。
words.en: A set-piece is a part of a film, play, etc. that is planned and rehearsed carefully and is often designed to be very exciting or impressive.

words.tr: n. 制定者；塞特种猎犬
words.ex: He is the setter of new rules for the team.
words.ex_cn: 他是团队新规则的制定者。
words.en: A setter is a person or thing that sets something, especially a type of dog trained to find and indicate the position of game birds.

words.ex: He was fired for showing sexism at work.
words.ex_cn: 他因在工作中表现出性别歧视而被解雇。
words.en: Sexism is the belief that the members of one sex are less intelligent, able, skillful, etc. than the members of the other sex, especially that women are less able than men.

words.tr:
n. 性别歧视者
adj. 性别歧视的
words.ex: He made a sexist comment about women drivers.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了关于女司机的性别歧视言论。
words.en: A sexist person shows prejudice or discrimination based on a person's sex, especially against women.

words.tr:
n. 棚屋；简陋的小屋
v. 居住
words.ex: He lives in a small shack near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一间小木屋里。
words.en: A shack is a small, simple building, often made of wood or metal, which is not very well built or comfortable.

words.tr:
n. 粗毛；蓬乱一团
v. 使蓬松；使杂乱
words.ex: The carpet has a thick, shag texture.
words.ex_cn: 这块地毯有着厚厚的粗毛质感。
words.en: Shag refers to a type of rough, coarse hair or a dance style characterized by energetic movements.

words.tr: adj. 毛发粗浓杂乱的；毛发蓬松的
words.ex: The dog has a shaggy coat.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗有一身蓬乱的毛。
words.en: Having or covered with long, rough, and thick hair or fur.

words.tr: v. 上海（中国城市）；诱骗（某人）做某事；
words.ex: They shanghai the tourists to visit the Bund.
words.ex_cn: 他们带游客去参观外滩。
words.en: To shanghai someone means to trick or force them into doing something they do not want to do, especially to make them join a ship's crew.

words.tr: adj. 样子好看的；匀称的；线条优美的
words.ex: She has a very shapely figure.
words.ex_cn: 她有着非常匀称的身材。
words.en: Having an attractive shape; well-proportioned.

words.ex: The farmer tied the sheaf of wheat with rope.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用绳子把一束小麦捆在一起。
words.en: A sheaf is a bundle of grain stalks laid lengthwise and tied together after reaping.

words.ex: The farmer shears sheep every spring.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每年春天给羊剪毛。
words.en: To shear means to cut the wool off a sheep or to cut or trim something with scissors or shears.

words.ex: The sword slid easily into its sheath.
words.ex_cn: 剑很容易地滑入鞘中。
words.en: A sheath is a close-fitting cover for the blade of a knife or sword, or a similar protective covering for something else.

words.ex: The wet stone has a soft sheen.
words.ex_cn: 湿石头有柔和的光泽。
words.en: A sheen is a soft, smooth, shiny quality on the surface of something.

words.tr: adj.  羞怯的；腼腆的；局促不安的
words.ex: He gave a sheepish smile after forgetting his lines.
words.ex_cn: 他忘记台词后，尴尬地笑了笑。
words.en: If you look sheepish, you look slightly embarrassed because you feel foolish or you have done something silly.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；发微光
n. 微光；闪光
words.ex: The lake shimmers under the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 湖面在月光下闪烁。
words.en: To shine with a soft, slightly wavering light.

words.tr:
adj. 浅的
n. 浅水处；鱼群；一大群
v. （使）变浅
words.ex: The boat ran aground on the shoal.
words.ex_cn: 船在浅水处搁浅了。
words.en: A shoal is a large number of fish swimming together. It can also refer to a shallow place in a body of water.

words.tr: adj. 劣质的；次品的；卑劣的
words.ex: He bought a shoddy chair that broke after one day.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一把劣质的椅子，一天就坏了。
words.en: If you describe something as shoddy, you mean that it has been done or made carelessly or badly.

words.tr: v. （给顾客）少找钱；不公平对待
words.ex: The shopkeeper short-changed me by five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 店主给我少找了五美元。
words.en: To give someone less change than they are owed, especially deliberately.

words.ex: There is a shortfall in food supplies this winter.
words.ex_cn: 今年冬天食物供应不足。
words.en: A shortfall is a situation in which there is not enough of something, especially money.

words.ex: She wore a showy dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件显眼的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is showy is very noticeable because it is large, colorful, or exaggerated.

words.ex: The shrew ran quickly under the leaves.
words.ex_cn: 鼩鼱在树叶下快速奔跑。
words.en: A shrew is a small, mouse-like mammal with a pointed snout, or it can refer to a bad-tempered or aggressively assertive woman.

words.ex: The cloth shows shrinkage after washing.
words.ex_cn: 这块布在洗涤后出现了缩水。
words.en: The process, fact, or amount of shrinking.

words.ex: The apple shrivels in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 苹果在阳光下皱缩。
words.en: If something shrivels or if you shrivel it, it becomes dryer and smaller, often with lines in its surface, as a result of losing the water it contains.

words.ex: The garden was filled with colorful shrubbery.
words.ex_cn: 花园里种满了五彩缤纷的灌木。
words.en: A shrubbery is a part of a garden where shrubs are planted.

words.tr: adj. 灌木的；灌木状的；灌木丛生的
words.ex: The hillside was covered in shrubby vegetation.
words.ex_cn: 山坡上覆盖着灌木丛生的植被。
words.en: Consisting of or resembling shrubs.

words.ex: He is sick and cannot go to school.
words.ex_cn: 他生病了，不能去上学。
words.en: If you are sick, you are ill. Sick can also mean feeling nauseous or wanting to vomit. Additionally, it can describe being very tired of something or someone because you have experienced too much of them.

words.ex: The injured sailor was taken to the sickbay for treatment.
words.ex_cn: 受伤的水手被带到医务室接受治疗。
words.en: A sickbay is a place on a ship or in the military where medical treatment is given to people who are sick or injured.

words.tr:
adj. 使人厌恶的；令人不快的；令人恶心的
v. 患病；恶心；（使）厌倦；“sicken”的现在分词
words.ex: The smell of rotten food is sickening.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的气味令人作呕。
words.en: If you describe something as sickening, you mean that it makes you feel disgusted or horrified.

words.ex: He works as a teacher but his sideline is selling handmade crafts.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名教师，但他的副业是卖手工制品。
words.en: A sideline is an activity that you do in addition to your main job in order to earn extra money.

words.tr:
v. 向旁侧避让；回避
n. 向侧方跨步
words.ex: He sidestepped the question during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在采访中回避了这个问题。
words.en: If you sidestep a problem or question, you avoid answering it or dealing with it.

words.tr: v. 侧向移动；悄悄贴近
words.ex: She sidled up to him and whispered in his ear.
words.ex_cn: 她侧身悄悄靠近他，在他耳边低语。
words.en: To move sideways or obliquely, especially in a stealthy or furtive manner.

words.ex: He climbed the sierra with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友们爬了山。
words.en: A sierra is a mountain range, especially in Spain or Spanish America.

words.ex: He used his signet to seal the document.
words.ex_cn: 他用他的印章密封了文件。
words.en: A signet is a small seal, especially one set in a ring, used historically to authenticate documents by pressing it into wax or another soft material.

words.ex: The farmer stores silage for his cows in winter.
words.ex_cn: 农夫为他的奶牛储存青贮饲料过冬。
words.en: Silage is grass or other green fodder compacted and stored in airtight conditions, typically in a silo, without first being dried, and used as animal feed in the winter.

words.ex: The tree's silhouette stood against the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 树的剪影映在落日背景下。
words.en: A silhouette is the dark shape and outline of someone or something visible against a lighter background, especially in dim light.

words.ex: The sand contains a lot of silica.
words.ex_cn: 这种沙子含有大量的二氧化硅。
words.en: A hard, unreactive, colorless compound that occurs as the mineral quartz and as a principal constituent of sandstone and other rocks.

words.tr:
v. 煨；用文火炖；充满；即将爆发
n. 炖；即将发作
words.ex: The soup is simmering on the stove.
words.ex_cn: 汤正在炉子上慢炖。
words.en: To cook something slowly at a temperature slightly below boiling point.

words.tr: n. 头脑简单的人；傻瓜；笨蛋
words.ex: He is a simpleton who believes everything he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他是个傻瓜，什么都信。
words.en: A simpleton is someone who is not very intelligent and who is easily tricked or deceived.

words.tr:
n. 肌腱；力量的来源
v. 给…以力量
words.ex: The sinew held the muscle to the bone.
words.ex_cn: 肌腱将肌肉连接到骨头。
words.en: A sinew is a tendon, the strong tissue that connects muscles to bones, or it can refer to the strength and energy that makes someone able to do something difficult.

words.ex: The river has a sinuous path through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河在森林中蜿蜒流淌。
words.en: Something that is sinuous has many smooth turns and curves.

words.tr:
n. 虹吸管
v. 用虹吸管吸；抽取；挪用
words.ex: He used a siphon to transfer gasoline from one tank to another.
words.ex_cn: 他用虹吸管将汽油从一个油箱输送到另一个油箱。
words.en: A siphon is a tube that is used to move liquids from one container to another at a lower level by atmospheric pressure and gravity.

words.tr: n. 牛里脊肉；牛上腰肉
words.ex: He grilled a sirloin steak for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他为晚餐烤了一块西冷牛排。
words.en: A cut of beef from the lower part of the back, just in front of the rump.

words.ex: He earned a sizeable amount of money from his business.
words.ex_cn: 他从生意中赚了一笔可观的钱。
words.en: A sizeable amount or quantity of something is fairly large.

words.tr:
v. 打滑；侧滑
n. 打滑；侧滑
words.ex: The car skid on the wet road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在湿滑的路面上打滑了。
words.en: If a vehicle skids, it slides sideways or forwards while moving, usually because of bad weather conditions or because the driver is going too fast.

words.tr: n. 撇取物；泛泛阅读者；剪嘴鸥科水禽
words.ex: He uses a skimmer to remove oil from the soup.
words.ex_cn: 他用捞勺从汤里捞出油。
words.en: A skimmer is a device used for removing substances from the surface of a liquid. It can also refer to a person who reads or looks through something quickly, or a type of bird that flies low over water to catch fish.

words.tr: n. 潜游运动；赤身潜水
words.ex: He loves skin-diving in the sea on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在周末去海里裸潜。
words.en: The activity of swimming underwater without the use of scuba gear, often using only a mask, snorkel, and fins.

words.tr: adj. 皮包骨头的；极瘦的；
words.ex: The skinny dog had no meat on its bones.
words.ex_cn: 那只皮包骨头的狗身上一点肉都没有。
words.en: Very thin, especially in a way that is unattractive.

words.ex: The factory dumped slag near the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂把矿渣倒在河边。
words.en: Slag is the glass-like by-product left over after a desired metal has been separated (i.e., smelted) from its raw ore. Slag is usually a mixture of metal oxides and silicon dioxide. However, slags can contain metal sulfides and elemental metals.

words.ex: The article contained slanderous remarks about the company.
words.ex_cn: 这篇文章包含了对公司的诽谤性评论。
words.en: If something is slanderous, it falsely harms someone's reputation by saying something bad about them that is not true.

words.tr: adj. 好用俚语的；俗话多的
words.ex: He uses slangy words when talking to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时用很口语化的词。
words.en: Using or containing slang; characteristic of slang.

words.ex: She added a little salt to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 她在汤里加了一点盐。
words.en: Salt is a white crystalline substance that is used for seasoning or preserving food. It is also used in various industrial processes.

words.ex: The sleeper breathed deeply in the quiet room.
words.ex_cn: 睡眠者在安静的房间里深呼吸。
words.en: A sleeper is someone who is sleeping, or a thing that unexpectedly becomes very successful.

words.tr:
adj. 光滑的；圆滑的；熟练的；华而不实的
n. 浮油层；光滑之处
v. 使平滑
words.ex: The ice on the road was slick.
words.ex_cn: 路上的冰很光滑。
words.en: If something is slick, it is done smoothly and efficiently, often in a way that is intended to be impressive.

words.ex: The slime at the bottom of the river smells bad.
words.ex_cn: 河底的污泥闻起来很难闻。
words.en: Slime is a thick, wet, slippery substance, often unpleasant to touch.

words.ex: The cat slinked away in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 猫在黑暗中悄悄溜走了。
words.en: To move in a smooth, quiet, and secretive manner, typically because of guilt or a desire to avoid attention.

words.ex: The slit in the curtain let in a thin beam of light.
words.ex_cn: 窗帘上的裂缝透进了一束细光。
words.en: A long, narrow cut or opening.

words.ex: A sliver of wood stuck in his finger.
words.ex_cn: 一小片木头扎进了他的手指。
words.en: A sliver is a small, thin piece of something that has been cut, broken, or torn off from a larger piece.

words.tr:
v. 没精打采地站（或坐、走）；低头垂肩地站（或坐、走）
n. 没精打采的样子
words.ex: He slouches in his chair while watching TV.
words.ex_cn: 他看电视时驼背坐着。
words.en: If someone slouches, they sit or stand with their shoulders and head bent so that they look lazy and tired.

words.tr:
n. 蛞蝓；懒汉；重击；一大口；金属块；子弹
v. 动作迟缓；偷懒；重击
words.ex: A slug crawled slowly across the wet grass.
words.ex_cn: 一只鼻涕虫在湿草地上缓慢爬行。
words.en: A slug is a small, slow-moving creature with a soft body, often found in gardens. It can also refer to a bullet or a lazy person. As a verb, it means to hit hard or to move slowly or lazily.

words.tr:
v. 含混不清地说话；诋毁；诽谤
n. 诽谤；诋毁；污辱
words.ex: He slurrs his words when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，说话含糊不清。
words.en: If someone slurs their speech or if their speech slurs, they do not pronounce each word clearly, because they are drunk, ill, or sleepy. A slur is an insulting remark which could damage someone's reputation.

words.tr:
v. 郁积；（无明火）闷烧；（眼睛）放电
n. 冒烟闷烧
words.ex: Anger smouldered in his heart for years.
words.ex_cn: 愤怒在他心中郁积了多年。
words.en: To burn slowly with smoke but without flame; to exist in a suppressed state; to feel strong emotions without showing them.

words.tr:
v. 闷烧；冒烟；郁积
n. 闷烧
words.ex: The fire still smolders in the fireplace.
words.ex_cn: 火还在壁炉里闷烧。
words.en: To burn slowly with smoke but without flame, or to exist in a suppressed state.

words.tr:
n. 小困难或障碍；划破处；钩丝处
v. 被钩住；划破；抢先获得
words.ex: He found a snag in the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他在计划中发现了一个问题。
words.en: A snag is a small problem or difficulty that you did not expect.

words.tr:
v. 抽鼻子；抽噎
n. 抽鼻子（声）；鼻塞
words.ex: He sniffled while holding a tissue.
words.ex_cn: 他拿着纸巾抽鼻子。
words.en: To sniffle means to sniff repeatedly, especially because you are crying or have a cold.

words.tr:
n. 沙锥鸟；鹬
v. 猎鸟；狙击；抨击
words.ex: The snipe flew quietly over the wetland.
words.ex_cn: 沙锥鸟静静地飞过湿地。
words.en: To shoot at someone from a hidden place; to criticize someone in a sly or petty manner.

words.ex: The sniper shot the target from far away.
words.ex_cn: 狙击手从远处射中了目标。
words.en: A sniper is a person who shoots at someone from a hidden position.

words.tr:
v. 吸鼻子；流鼻涕；啜泣
n. 吸鼻子；流鼻涕；啜泣
words.ex: He keeps sniveling about his broken toy.
words.ex_cn: 他一直哭哭啼啼地说他的玩具坏了。
words.en: If someone snivels, they cry or sniff in a way that irritates you.

words.tr: adj. 自大的；傲慢的；目中无人的
words.ex: The snooty waiter ignored our questions.
words.ex_cn: 那位傲慢的侍者无视了我们的提问。
words.en: If you say that someone is snooty, you disapprove of them because they behave as if they are superior to other people.

words.tr:
n. （潜水艇或潜水者的）通气管
v. 戴潜水通气管潜泳
words.ex: He put on his mask and snorkel to swim over the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 他戴上口罩和通气管，在珊瑚礁上游泳。
words.en: A snorkel is a tube that allows a swimmer to breathe while floating face down on the surface of the water.

words.tr: n. 鼻口部；猪嘴；鼻状物；
words.ex: The pig stuck its snout in the mud.
words.ex_cn: 猪把它的鼻口部伸进了泥里。
words.en: The projecting nose and mouth of an animal, especially a mammal.

words.tr:
v. 冷落；怠慢；不理睬；掐灭
n. 冷落；怠慢
adj. 短平而上翘的
words.ex: He snubbed his friend at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上冷落了朋友。
words.en: To snub someone means to deliberately ignore them or treat them with disrespect, often by refusing to acknowledge their presence or by failing to respond to a greeting or request.

words.tr:
n. 鼻烟；烛花
v. 用鼻子使劲吸；熄灭；断气
words.ex: He takes snuff every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都吸鼻烟。
words.en: Snuff is powdered tobacco that people take by sniffing it into their noses. It can also refer to the act of extinguishing a candle or the burnt part of a candle wick.

words.tr: n. 清醒；镇定；严肃；节制
words.ex: He values sobriety after his accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后重视清醒。
words.en: The state of being sober, especially in terms of not being under the influence of alcohol.

words.ex: The bread became soggy after sitting in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 面包在雨中放了一会儿后变得湿软。
words.en: Something that is soggy is unpleasantly wet.

words.tr:
adj. 唯一的；
n. 鞋底；
words.ex: He is the sole owner of the shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是这家商店唯一的主人。
words.en: If you describe something as the sole thing of a particular kind, you mean that it is the only one of that kind.

words.ex: The solemnity of the ceremony made everyone quiet.
words.ex_cn: 仪式的庄重让所有人都安静了下来。
words.en: The state or quality of being serious and dignified.

words.ex: He spoke a soliloquy alone on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他独自在舞台上说了一段独白。
words.en: A soliloquy is a speech in a play in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud, often when they are alone on stage.

words.tr: adj. 独自的；单独的；孤寂的；
words.ex: He lives in a solitary house far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 他住在离城镇很远的独自一人的房子里。
words.en: A solitary person or thing is the only one in a place.

words.ex: The company's solvency was in question after the financial scandal.
words.ex_cn: 财务丑闻后，该公司的偿付能力受到了质疑。
words.en: The ability of an individual or entity to meet its financial obligations as they come due.

words.tr: adj.  忧郁的；阴沉的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room had a somber mood.
words.ex_cn: 房间里有一种阴郁的气氛。
words.en: If someone is somber, they are serious or sad.

words.ex: He plays a beautiful sonata on the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他用钢琴演奏一首优美的奏鸣曲。
words.en: A sonata is a piece of music written for one or two instruments that has three or four large sections that are different from each other but form a unified whole.

words.ex: The ancient Sophists were known for their teachings on rhetoric and philosophy.
words.ex_cn: 古希腊的诡辩家以其修辞学和哲学教导而闻名。
words.en: A sophist is a person who uses clever but false arguments, especially in order to deceive people.

words.tr: n. 短程旅行；出动；突击
words.ex: The pilot went on a sortie to drop supplies.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员执行了一次出动任务来投送物资。
words.en: A sortie is a sudden attack made by troops, especially by troops who are defending a place.

words.tr: n. 西班牙猎犬；恭顺的人; vi. 嬉戏; vt. 向……摇尾乞怜
words.ex: The boy plays with a spaniel in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在花园里和一只西班牙猎犬玩耍。
words.en: A spaniel is a type of dog known for its long ears and its ability to hunt or retrieve game.

words.tr:
v. 轻拳出击；拌嘴
n. 粗杆；桅
words.ex: He sparred with his friend in the boxing ring.
words.ex_cn: 他在拳击台上和朋友进行了对练。
words.en: To spar means to engage in boxing or to argue. As a noun, it can refer to a mast of a ship or a type of mineral.

words.ex: Use water sparingly during the drought.
words.ex_cn: 在干旱期间要节约用水。
words.en: If you do something sparingly, you do it in a very limited or restrained way.

words.tr: n. 痉挛；抽搐；一阵发作
words.ex: He had a spasm in his leg.
words.ex_cn: 他的腿抽筋了。
words.en: A spasm is a sudden and involuntary contraction of a muscle or group of muscles, often causing pain or discomfort.

words.tr: adj. 痉挛的；间歇的；一阵阵的
words.ex: He had spasmodic coughing at night.
words.ex_cn: 他晚上有阵发性的咳嗽。
words.en: Something that is spasmodic happens suddenly and irregularly, often in short periods of time.

words.tr: n. 泛滥；猛涨；大批；一连串
words.ex: A spate of rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 一场暴雨淹没了街道。
words.en: A spate of things, especially unpleasant ones, is a large number of them that happen or appear within a short period of time.

words.ex: He has good spatial skills for drawing maps.
words.ex_cn: 他画地图有很好的空间能力。
words.en: Relating to or occupying space.

words.tr:
v. 溅；洒
n. 洒、溅等的声音
words.ex: Rain spattered the windows.
words.ex_cn: 雨点溅在窗户上。
words.en: To spatter means to scatter or splash (a liquid) in small drops over an area. It can also refer to the act of defaming or sullying someone's reputation.

words.tr:
n. 小斑点
v. 弄上斑点
words.ex: The bird's wings have a speckle of white dots.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟的翅膀上有小白斑点。
words.en: A speckle is a small spot or mark, especially one of a number of spots or marks, on something.

words.tr: n. 鬼怪；幽灵；缠绕心头的恐惧
words.ex: The spectre of hunger haunted the village.
words.ex_cn: 饥饿的幽灵萦绕着这个村庄。
words.en: A spectre is a ghost or a spirit, or something that people are afraid of because it might cause them harm or trouble.

words.ex: The colors in the rainbow cover a wide spectrum.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹中的颜色覆盖了广泛的范围。
words.en: A spectrum is a range of a particular type of thing, often a range of colors, ideas, or opinions.

words.tr:
n. 纺锤；锭子；心轴
v. 装锭子于
words.ex: The spinner turns the spindle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 纺纱工快速转动纺锤。
words.en: A spindle is a rod or pin, tapered at one end and usually weighted at the other, on which fibers are spun by hand into thread and then wound.

words.tr: n. 纺纱机；纺纱工；转盘
words.ex: The spinner turned wool into thread.
words.ex_cn: 这台纺纱机将羊毛纺成线。
words.en: A spinner is a person or machine that spins wool, cotton, or other material into thread or yarn.

words.ex: He finds peace through spirituality.
words.ex_cn: 他通过灵性找到平静。
words.en: Spirituality involves the recognition of a feeling or sense or belief that there is something greater than oneself, something more to being human than sensory experience, and that the greater whole of which we are part is cosmic or divine in nature.

words.ex: The old engine spluttered and then stopped.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧引擎发出劈啪声，然后熄火了。
words.en: If someone splutters, they make short sounds and have difficulty speaking clearly, for example because they are embarrassed or angry.

words.tr:
n. 鬼；幽灵；间谍
v. 鬼怪般出没；吓唬
words.ex: The children were scared of the spook in the haunted house.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们害怕鬼屋里的鬼。
words.en: A spook is a ghost or a spy. It can also mean to frighten or scare someone.

words.ex: The fungus releases a spore into the air.
words.ex_cn: 真菌向空气中释放一个孢子。
words.en: A spore is a reproductive cell that is capable of developing into a new individual without fusion with another reproductive cell. Spores are thus agents of asexual reproduction, whereas gametes are agents of sexual reproduction.

words.tr:
n. 争吵
v. 争吵
words.ex: The two boys squabble over toys every day.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天为玩具争吵。
words.en: A squabble is a noisy disagreement about something unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 肮脏的；污秽的；卑劣的
words.ex: The squalid apartment had dirty floors and broken windows.
words.ex_cn: 这间肮脏的公寓地板很脏，窗户也破了。
words.en: If you describe a place as squalid, you mean that it is dirty, untidy, and in bad condition.

words.tr:
n. 狂风；暴风雪；大喊大叫
v. 狂风吹袭；哇哇地叫嚷
words.ex: A sudden squall knocked over the small boat.
words.ex_cn: 一阵突如其来的狂风掀翻了小船。
words.en: A squall is a sudden, violent gust of wind or a localized storm, especially one bringing rain, snow, or sleet. It can also refer to a loud, harsh cry or scream.

words.tr: n. 肮脏；污秽；恶劣条件
words.ex: The family lived in squalor with no clean water.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭生活在肮脏的环境中，没有干净的水。
words.en: A state of being extremely dirty and unpleasant, especially as a result of poverty or neglect.

words.tr:
n. 球类运动（squash）；
v. 压碎；
words.ex: He plays squash every weekend with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末和朋友打壁球。
words.en: To squash something means to press or squeeze it so that it becomes flat, soft, or out of shape. It can also refer to the sport of squash or a type of vegetable.

words.tr:
v. 咯咯地叫；大声抱怨
n. 刺耳的叫声；大声抱怨
words.ex: The parrot squawked loudly when it saw the visitor.
words.ex_cn: 鹦鹉看到访客时咯咯地叫了起来。
words.en: To squawk means to make a loud, harsh noise, often used to describe the sound made by birds. It can also mean to complain loudly or protest about something.

words.tr:
n. 长声尖叫；长而尖的声音
v. 尖声长叫
words.ex: The child let out a loud squeal when she saw the spider.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子看到蜘蛛时，发出了一声长长的尖叫。
words.en: If someone or something squeals, they make a long, high-pitched sound.

words.tr: adj. 易恶心的；易受惊的；神经质的；过于拘谨的
words.ex: She was too squeamish to watch the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 她太容易呕吐了，不敢看手术过程。
words.en: If you are squeamish, you are easily upset by unpleasant sights or situations.

words.ex: The child squirted water from the hose.
words.ex_cn: 孩子从软管里喷出水。
words.en: To squirt means to force out liquid in a thin fast stream or to be forced out in this way.

words.tr:
adj. 断音的；不连贯的
adv. 断音地；不连贯地
n. 断奏；断续的一段音乐
words.ex: The piano played staccato notes.
words.ex_cn: 钢琴弹奏了断奏的音符。
words.en: In music, staccato is a method of playing notes in a detached, separated manner, as opposed to legato.

words.ex: The stag ran through the forest quickly.
words.ex_cn: 那头成年雄鹿在森林中快速奔跑。
words.en: A stag is an adult male deer.

words.ex: He is a staid man who never wears casual clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个古板的人，从不穿休闲服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as staid, you mean that they are serious, dull, and rather old-fashioned.

words.tr:
n. 僵局；和棋；僵持状态
v. 使陷入僵局
words.ex: The two players are in a stalemate.
words.ex_cn: 两位选手陷入了僵局。
words.en: A situation in which further action or progress by opposing parties seems impossible.

words.ex: The stallion runs fast in the field.
words.ex_cn: 这匹公马在田野里跑得很快。
words.en: A stallion is an adult male horse that has not been castrated, especially one kept for breeding.

words.ex: He is a stalwart of the environmental movement.
words.ex_cn: 他是环保运动的坚定分子。
words.en: A stalwart person is someone who is very loyal and committed to a person, belief, or cause and is not likely to change their views or behavior.

words.ex: He has great stamina for running long distances.
words.ex_cn: 他有很强的耐力来跑长距离。
words.en: Stamina is the physical or mental energy needed to do a tiring activity for a long time.

words.ex: He changed his stance on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他改变了对气候变化的立场。
words.en: A stance is a particular way of standing, especially in sports such as golf or baseball, or a person's attitude or opinion about something, especially when it is stated publicly.

words.ex: The poem has four stanzas.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗有四节。
words.en: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem that are separated from other groups by a space.

words.ex: The boat turned to starboard to avoid the rock.
words.ex_cn: 船向右转以避开岩石。
words.en: The right side of a ship or aircraft when facing forward.

words.ex: He dreams of stardom after winning the talent show.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得才艺比赛后梦想着成名。
words.en: The status of being a very famous or popular performer, especially in the entertainment industry.

words.tr: adj. 庄重的；庄严的；堂皇的；
words.ex: The stately mansion stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 那座庄重的豪宅矗立在山上。
words.en: Something that is stately is impressive because of its size, beauty, or grandeur.

words.tr: n. 秘密行动；偷偷摸摸
words.ex: The cat moved in stealth to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫悄悄地移动去抓老鼠。
words.en: Stealth is the action of moving or behaving in a secretive way in order to avoid being noticed.

words.ex: He moved stealthily through the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 他悄悄地在黑暗的房间里移动。
words.en: In a way that is intended not to be seen or noticed; secretly.

words.tr: adj. 似钢的；钢色的；坚硬如钢的
words.ex: She had steely determination to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 她有着钢铁般的决心要成功。
words.en: Resembling steel in color, brightness, or strength; hard and unyielding.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.ex: He stereotypically wears a suit to work.
words.ex_cn: 他传统地穿西装去上班。
words.en: In a way that is based on a fixed, general image or idea of a particular type of person or thing, which is often not true in reality.

words.ex: The doctor uses a stethoscope to listen to his heart.
words.ex_cn: 医生用听诊器听他的心跳。
words.en: A stethoscope is an instrument that a doctor uses to listen to someone's heart and breathing. It consists of a small disc that is placed against the chest, and two tubes connected to earpieces.

words.tr: n. （供人翻越田地处所设栅栏的）台阶；梯磴
words.ex: He climbed over the stile to get to the field.
words.ex_cn: 他翻过石阶进入田野。
words.en: A stile is a structure which provides people a passage through or over a fence or boundary via steps, ladders, or narrow gaps.

words.ex: Caffeine is a common stimulant.
words.ex_cn: 咖啡因是一种常见的兴奋剂。
words.en: A stimulant is a substance that raises levels of physiological or nervous activity in the body.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.ex: He receives a small stipend for his internship.
words.ex_cn: 他因实习获得少量薪金。
words.en: A stipend is a sum of money paid regularly as a salary or allowance.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.ex: He adjusted his stirrup before mounting the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他上马前调整了马镫。
words.en: A stirrup is a loop, ring, or other contrivance of metal, wood, leather, etc., suspended from the saddle of a horse to support the rider's foot.

words.tr:
n. 斯多葛派人；坚忍克己之人；
adj. 斯多葛派的；坚忍克己的；
words.ex: He is a stoic who never shows his emotions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个从不流露情感的斯多葛派人。
words.en: Someone who is stoic does not show their feelings or complain when bad things happen to them.

words.tr: adj. 斯多葛派的；坚忍克己的
words.ex: He remained stoical after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后依然表现得冷静淡然。
words.en: If you are stoical, you do not show your feelings or complain even in a situation that is difficult or painful.

words.ex: The speech stoked anger among the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 这篇演讲激起了人群的愤怒。
words.en: To stoke a fire means to add fuel to it to make it burn more strongly. It can also mean to encourage or increase strong feelings or emotions.

words.ex: The strike caused a stoppage of the train service.
words.ex_cn: 罢工导致了列车服务的停止。
words.en: A stoppage is an instance of stopping or the state of being stopped, especially in a work context.

words.tr: v. 装载；装填；妥善放置
words.ex: He stowed the boxes in the truck.
words.ex_cn: 他把箱子装上了卡车。
words.en: To stow something means to pack it or store it neatly in a particular place.

words.tr: v. 蔓延；散乱地分布；落伍
words.ex: Weeds straggle across the garden.
words.ex_cn: 杂草蔓延在整个花园里。
words.en: If people straggle, they move along slowly, spread out over a wide area, and are not in a group.

words.tr: adj. （道德观念上）极拘谨的，古板的（等于 straight-laced）
words.ex: He is a strait-laced man who never breaks the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个恪守规矩、从不违反规则的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as strait-laced, you mean that they have very strict views about what kind of behavior is moral or acceptable.

words.ex: The teacher will stratify the students by age.
words.ex_cn: 老师会按年龄将学生分层。
words.en: To arrange or form into layers or strata.

words.tr: n. 岩层；地层；社会阶层
words.ex: The geologist examined the stratum for fossils.
words.ex_cn: 地质学家检查了岩层以寻找化石。
words.en: A stratum is a layer of material, naturally or artificially formed, often one of a number of parallel layers one upon another.

words.ex: The exam was stressful for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这次考试对所有学生来说压力很大。
words.en: If a situation or experience is stressful, it makes you feel worried and tense because of difficulties or problems.

words.ex: The wind strews leaves on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得满地都是。
words.en: To scatter or spread things untidily over a surface or area.

words.tr:
n. 结构；建筑物；
v. 组织；
words.ex: The structure of the bridge is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。
words.en: The arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.

words.ex: Her strident voice broke the silence.
words.ex_cn: 她尖锐的声音打破了寂静。
words.en: If you use strident to describe someone or the way they express themselves, you mean that they make their feelings or opinions known in a very strong way that perhaps makes people uncomfortable.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.ex: Strontium is a chemical element with the symbol Sr and atomic number 38.
words.ex_cn: 锶是一种化学元素，符号为Sr，原子序数为38。
words.en: A soft silver-white or yellowish metallic element of the alkali metal group, occurring naturally in celestite and strontianite. It is used in fireworks, flares, and in the production of glass for color television tubes.

words.tr:
n. 撑杆；支柱
v. 趾高气扬地走；昂首阔步
words.ex: The bridge has metal struts to support the weight.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有金属撑杆来支撑重量。
words.en: If someone struts, they walk in a proud way, with their chest out and trying to look important.

words.ex: He has a little stubble on his chin.
words.ex_cn: 他的下巴上有一点胡茬。
words.en: Stubble refers to the short, stiff stalks of grain or other crops left in a field after harvesting, or to the short, stiff hairs on a man's face when he has not shaved for a few days.

words.ex: He is a studious student who always does his homework carefully.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个认真学习的学生，总是认真完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is studious spends a lot of time studying and reading.

words.ex: The room was stuffy and hard to breathe in.
words.ex_cn: 房间闷热得让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a place as stuffy, you mean that it is unpleasantly warm and has no fresh air.

words.ex: He stared in stupefaction at the sudden crash.
words.ex_cn: 他震惊地盯着突如其来的撞击声。
words.en: The state of being stupefied; astonishment.

words.ex: The view from the mountain was stupendous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色令人惊叹。
words.en: Something that is stupendous is extremely impressive or large.

words.ex: The subjection of the people to the law is important.
words.ex_cn: 人民对法律的服从很重要。
words.en: The act of subjecting or the state of being subjected, especially to control or authority.

words.ex: His answer shows subjectivity.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答体现了主观性。
words.en: Subjectivity refers to the influence of personal beliefs, feelings, or opinions on one's perception or interpretation of events or facts.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.tr: adj. 本质上的；实质性的；
words.ex: The change was substantive, not just cosmetic.
words.ex_cn: 这个改变是本质上的，而不仅仅是表面上的。
words.en: Something that is substantive is significant, meaningful, or important in a way that is not just superficial or formal.

words.ex: The suburbanite drives to work every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这位郊区居民每天早上开车去上班。
words.en: A suburbanite is a person who lives in a suburb.

words.ex: The plot involved subversion of the government.
words.ex_cn: 这个情节涉及对政府的颠覆。
words.en: Subversion is the act of trying to destroy or damage an established system or government.

words.tr:
adj. 颠覆性的；破坏性的
n. 颠覆分子；危险分子
words.ex: The subversive poster tried to break the government's rules.
words.ex_cn: 那张颠覆性的海报试图破坏政府的规则。
words.en: A subversive person or activity is one that is intended to weaken or destroy a political system or government.

words.ex: The cactus has succulent leaves to store water.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有多汁的叶子来储存水分。
words.en: (of food) tender, juicy, and tasty; (of a plant) having thick, fleshy tissues adapted to water storage.

words.tr: adj. 受得住的；可忍受的
words.ex: The pain was sufferable, so she didn't call the doctor.
words.ex_cn: 疼痛还能忍受，所以她没有叫医生。
words.en: Capable of being endured or tolerated; bearable.

words.tr: n. 容许；忍耐；勉强同意
words.ex: He stayed out of pity, out of sufferance.
words.ex_cn: 他留下来是出于同情，出于容忍。
words.en: If you do something on sufferance, you do it because someone allows you to, although they do not really want you to.

words.tr: n. 求婚者；起诉者；有意收购另一公司的机构
words.ex: He is a suitor who brings flowers every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天送花的追求者。
words.en: A suitor is a man who wants to marry a particular woman.

words.tr:
v. 愠怒；生闷气
n. 愠怒；生闷气
words.ex: He sulked in his room after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 争吵后，他生闷气待在房间里。
words.en: If you sulk, you are silent and bad-tempered for a while because you are annoyed about something.

words.ex: He sullied his reputation by lying.
words.ex_cn: 他通过撒谎玷污了自己的声誉。
words.en: To sully something means to spoil or reduce the value of something, especially someone's reputation or the purity of something.

words.tr: adj. 硫磺的；含有硫磺的
words.ex: The air smelled sulphurous after the volcano erupted.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷发后，空气中有一股硫磺味。
words.en: Relating to or containing sulfur, especially with a valence of 4.

words.tr: adj. 闷热的；性感的；撩人的
words.ex: The sultry weather made everyone feel tired.
words.ex_cn: 闷热的天气让每个人都感到疲惫。
words.en: Sultry weather is hot and damp in a way that makes you feel uncomfortable.

words.ex: The king ate a sumptuous meal in his palace.
words.ex_cn: 国王在他的宫殿里享用了一顿丰盛的饭菜。
words.en: Something that is sumptuous is very impressive and expensive, especially in a way that involves large amounts of money.

words.tr: adj. 各种各样的；杂七杂八的
words.ex: He bought sundry items at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店买了各种物品。
words.en: If someone refers to sundry people or things, they are referring to several people or things that are all different from each other.

words.ex: The sunken ship lies at the bottom of the sea.
words.ex_cn: 沉没的船位于海底。
words.en: Having descended below the surface; submerged or depressed.

words.tr: v. 置于某物之上；添加
words.ex: He superimposes a map on the photo.
words.ex_cn: 他把地图叠加在照片上。
words.en: To superimpose something means to place or lay one thing over another, typically so that both are still evident.

words.tr: v. 监督；管理；主管；指挥
words.ex: He superintends the construction site every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天监督建筑工地。
words.en: To be in charge of something and make sure that it is working as it should.

words.ex: The new law will supersede the old one.
words.ex_cn: 新法律将取代旧法律。
words.en: If something is superseded by something newer, it is replaced because it has become old-fashioned or unacceptable.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.tr: adj. 柔软的；灵活的；思维敏捷的
words.ex: The yoga teacher has supple legs.
words.ex_cn: 瑜伽老师腿很柔软。
words.en: A supple object or material bends or changes shape easily without breaking or cracking.

words.tr: adj. 增补性的；补充性的；
words.ex: The teacher gave supplementary notes for the lesson.
words.ex_cn: 老师为这节课提供了增补性的笔记。
words.en: Supplementary things are added to something in order to improve it or make it more complete.

words.ex: His supposition is that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是明天会下雨。
words.en: A supposition is a guess or a theory that you have about something, which may not be true.

words.tr: n. 至高无上；最大权力；最高地位；
words.ex: The king claimed supremacy over all other rulers.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣称自己对所有其他统治者拥有至高无上的权力。
words.en: Supremacy is the state or condition of being superior to all others in authority, power, or status.

words.tr: adj. 超现实主义的；离奇的；怪诞的
words.ex: The dream was surreal.
words.ex_cn: 这个梦很超现实。
words.en: If you describe something as surreal, you mean that the elements in it are combined in a strange way that you would not normally expect, like in a dream.

words.tr:
n. 超现实主义者
adj. 超现实主义的
words.ex: He is a surrealist painter.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位超现实主义画家。
words.en: A surrealist is someone who creates or appreciates surrealism, an artistic and literary movement that seeks to release the creative potential of the unconscious mind, for example by the irrational juxtaposition of images.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；鬼鬼祟祟的；偷偷摸摸的
words.ex: He gave a surreptitious glance at his phone during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时偷偷瞥了一眼手机。
words.en: If something is done surreptitiously, it is done secretly, often because it would not be approved of.

words.tr:
adj. 代理的；代用的
n. 代理人；代用品
words.ex: He acted as a surrogate father to the child.
words.ex_cn: 他作为孩子的代理父亲。
words.en: A surrogate is a person or thing that takes the place of or acts for another, especially in a role or function that is typically filled by someone else.

words.ex: Children have higher susceptibility to colds.
words.ex_cn: 儿童更容易感冒。
words.en: The condition of being susceptible; the state of being easily affected, influenced, or harmed by something.

words.tr:
v. 神气十足地走；大摇大摆地走
n. 大摇大摆；神气十足
words.ex: He walks with swagger down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他大摇大摆地走在街上。
words.en: If someone swaggers, they walk in a very proud and confident way, often in a way that annoys other people.

words.tr:
v. 交换；
n. 交换；
words.ex: They swap books every week.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周交换书籍。
words.en: If you swap something with someone, you give it to them and receive a different thing in exchange.

words.tr:
v. 用布包裹；用绷带缠
n. 长而宽的一长条；割刈的带状地
words.ex: She swathed the baby in a soft blanket.
words.ex_cn: 她用一条柔软的毯子把婴儿裹起来。
words.en: To wrap or bind in or as if in a bandage or cloth.

words.tr: v. 扫；“sweep”的现在分词； adj. 全面的；
words.ex: He sweeping the floor every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上扫地。
words.en: If you describe something as sweeping, you mean it is very extensive or has a very wide effect.

words.ex: The farmer feeds the swine every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上喂猪。
words.en: A swine is a pig, especially when considered as a farm animal, or a person who behaves in a very unpleasant way.

words.ex: He swiped his card to pay for the coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他刷卡支付了咖啡的钱。
words.en: If you swipe at a person or thing, you try to hit them with a stick or other object, making a swinging movement with your arm.

words.tr:
v. （使）旋转
n. 转环；旋轴
words.ex: The chair can swivel easily.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子可以轻松旋转。
words.en: A swivel is a device that allows something to turn around freely, or to turn something around freely.

words.ex: He gave a synoptic view of the history.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史做了概括性的概述。
words.en: Relating to or constituting a synopsis; presenting a summary or general view of a whole.

words.tr: v. 使系统化；使成体系；使条理化
words.ex: He tries to systematise his notes before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前试图整理他的笔记。
words.en: To arrange according to a system; make systematic.

words.tr: v. 使系统化；使成体系；使条理化
words.ex: He tries to systematize his notes before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前试图系统化他的笔记。
words.en: To systematize means to arrange according to an organized system; make systematic.

words.tr: adj. 心照不宣的；不作声的
words.ex: They have a tacit understanding about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们对规则有一种心照不宣的理解。
words.en: If you refer to someone's tacit agreement or approval, you mean they are agreeing to something or approving it without actually saying so, often because they are unwilling to admit to doing so.

words.tr: adv. 默默地；心照不宣地
words.ex: They tacitly agreed to wait.
words.ex_cn: 他们默许了等待。
words.en: If you tacitly agree to something, you agree to it without actually saying so.

words.ex: He is taciturn and rarely speaks.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默寡言，很少说话。
words.en: A taciturn person does not say very much and can seem unfriendly.

words.tr: adj. 发粘的；俗气的；破烂的
words.ex: The glue was still tacky after an hour.
words.ex_cn: 一小时后，胶水仍然发粘。
words.en: If you describe something as tacky, you dislike it because it is cheap and badly made or vulgar.

words.tr: adj. 机智的；圆滑的；得体的
words.ex: He was tactful when he said no to her request.
words.ex_cn: 当他拒绝她的请求时，他很得体。
words.en: If you describe someone as tactful, you approve of them because they are careful not to say or do anything that would offend or upset other people.

words.tr: adj. 战术上的；有谋略的；手段高明的
words.ex: He made a tactical move to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个战术性的举动来赢得比赛。
words.en: relating to or constituting actions carefully planned to gain a specific military end.

words.tr: n. 有策略的人；手段高明的人
words.ex: He was known as a brilliant tactician in the field of military strategy.
words.ex_cn: 他是军事战略领域中著名的战术家。
words.en: A tactician is someone who is skilled in planning the best way to achieve something, especially in war or politics.

words.tr: n. 塔夫绸；平纹皱丝织品
words.ex: She wore a taffeta dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条塔夫绸连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Taffeta is a crisp, smooth, plain woven fabric made from silk or synthetic fibers, used especially for women's garments.

words.tr: n. （飞机的）横尾翼；水平安定面
words.ex: The tailplane helps the airplane stay steady.
words.ex_cn: 水平尾翼帮助飞机保持稳定。
words.en: A tailplane is a small horizontal wing at the tail of an aircraft, which helps to stabilize the aircraft in flight.

words.ex: The shop's takings were higher this week.
words.ex_cn: 这家店这周的收入更高了。
words.en: The amount of money earned by a business, especially a shop or cinema, in a particular period of time.

words.ex: The line touches the circle at one point and is a tangent.
words.ex_cn: 这条线与圆在一个点相切，是一条切线。
words.en: A tangent is a straight line or plane that touches a curve or curved surface at a point, but if extended does not cross it at that point. In a more general sense, it can also refer to a sudden digression or change of course.

words.ex: The tea has a tannic taste.
words.ex_cn: 这种茶有单宁的苦味。
words.en: Relating to or containing tannin, especially as derived from the bark or galls of oak trees.

words.tr: v. （以可望而不可即之物）逗引；使干着急
words.ex: The smell of food cooking in the kitchen began to tantalise him.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里做饭的香味开始让他垂涎欲滴。
words.en: If you tantalise someone, you tease or torment them by offering them something they want but then withholding it or making it difficult to obtain.

words.tr: v. （以可望而不可及之物）逗引；使干着急
words.ex: The smell of cookies tantalize him.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味让他垂涎欲滴。
words.en: If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have it.

words.tr: v. 逐渐变细；逐渐减少；
words.ex: The candle tapers toward the top.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛向顶部逐渐变细。
words.en: A taper is a long thin candle or a gradual decrease in width or thickness.

words.ex: The dog has a tapeworm in its stomach.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗的胃里有绦虫。
words.en: A tapeworm is a long, flat worm that lives in the intestines of humans and animals.

words.tr:
adj. 酸的；辛辣的；尖酸的；刻薄的
n. 甜果馅饼；骚货；妓女
words.ex: The lemon taste is too tart.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬的味道太酸了。
words.en: If something such as fruit is tart, it has a sharp taste. If someone is tart, they are sharp or cutting in their manner or speech.

words.tr: n. 苏格兰格子呢；格子图案；独桅三角帆船
words.ex: He wore a tartan scarf in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天戴了一条格子围巾。
words.en: A tartan is a pattern consisting of criss-crossed horizontal and vertical bands in multiple colours, associated particularly with Scottish culture.

words.tr: adv. （非标准用法）起初；开始时（注：此词在标准英语中不常见，可能是 'start' 的副词形式，但通常使用 'at first' 或 'initially'）
words.ex: He startly woke up when the bell rang.
words.ex_cn: 当铃声响起时，他猛地醒了过来。
words.en: In a sudden or startled manner.

words.tr:
n. 破烂的衣服；千疮百孔
n. 破布；碎纸片；“tatter”的复数
words.ex: His clothes were in tatters after the long journey.
words.ex_cn: 长途旅行后，他的衣服破烂不堪。
words.en: Pieces of cloth that are old and torn.

words.ex: The tattooist drew a dragon on his arm.
words.ex_cn: 纹身师在他手臂上画了一条龙。
words.en: A tattooist is a person who tattoos, that is, makes permanent designs on the skin with ink.

words.ex: He taunted his brother for losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他奚落弟弟比赛输了。
words.en: If someone taunts you, they say unkind or insulting things to you, especially about your weaknesses or failures.

words.tr: adj. 拉紧的；绷紧的；紧张的
words.ex: The sail was taut in the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 帆在强风中绷得紧紧的。
words.en: If something such as a rope or wire is taut, it is stretched very tight. If muscles or parts of the body are taut, they are stretched tight, often because of physical effort or anxiety.

words.tr: adj. 俗丽而不值钱的；花里胡哨的
words.ex: She wore a tawdry dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着一件俗丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as tawdry, you mean that it is showy and bright but of very poor quality.

words.tr: n. 技术性问题；技术细节
words.ex: He won the case because of a technicality.
words.ex_cn: 他因为一个技术性细节赢得了诉讼。
words.en: A technicality is a small detail in a law or a set of rules, especially one that forces a particular result.

words.tr: n. 专家治国制度；技术官僚政治；技术专家政府
words.ex: The country is ruled by a technocracy of engineers and scientists.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家由一群工程师和科学家统治。
words.en: A technocracy is a system of governance where decision-makers are selected on the basis of their expertise in a given area of responsibility, particularly with regard to scientific or technical knowledge.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.ex: The drummer changed the tempo of the song.
words.ex_cn: 鼓手改变了这首歌的拍子。
words.en: The speed at which a piece of music is played or the rate or speed of motion or activity.

words.ex: The surgeon repaired the torn tendon in the athlete's leg.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生修复了运动员腿上的撕裂肌腱。
words.en: A tendon is a tough band of fibrous connective tissue that usually connects muscle to bone and is capable of withstanding tension.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.ex: Their agreement was tenuous and easily broken.
words.ex_cn: 他们的协议很脆弱，容易破裂。
words.en: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

words.ex: The hikers struggled across the rough terrain.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者艰难地穿越了崎岖的地形。
words.en: Terrain is used to refer to an area of land or a type of land when you are considering its physical features.

words.ex: The terrestrial animals live on land.
words.ex_cn: 陆地动物生活在陆地上。
words.en: Of, on, or relating to the earth.

words.ex: The will of the testator was contested by his heirs.
words.ex_cn: 立遗嘱者的遗嘱被他的继承人质疑。
words.en: A person who has made a will or given a testament.

words.tr:
n. 系绳；系链；界限
v. 用绳拴住
words.ex: The horse was tied to the post with a tether.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马被用拴绳系在了柱子上。
words.en: A tether is a rope or chain used to tie an animal to a post or other fixed point so that it cannot move away.

words.ex: The textual evidence supports the author's argument.
words.ex_cn: 文本证据支持作者的观点。
words.en: Relating to or based on a text.

words.ex: I will protect thee from all harm.
words.ex_cn: 我会保护你免受一切伤害。
words.en: Thee is an archaic or dialect form of 'you', used as the object of a verb or preposition.

words.ex: The movie has a thematic focus on friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的主题聚焦于友谊。
words.en: Relating to or constituting a theme or themes.

words.tr: n. 神学家；神学研究者
words.ex: The theologian wrote a book about God.
words.ex_cn: 这位神学家写了一本关于上帝的书。
words.en: A theologian is someone who studies the nature of God, religion, and religious beliefs.

words.ex: The therapeutic massage helped her relax.
words.ex_cn: 这种治疗性的按摩帮助她放松了。
words.en: If something is therapeutic, it helps you to relax or to feel better about things, especially if you have been feeling worried or upset.

words.tr: adv. 在其中；在那里；在那一点上
words.ex: The document outlines the terms and conditions therein.
words.ex_cn: 该文件概述了其中的条款和条件。
words.en: In that place, matter, or respect.

words.ex: He went thereto without hesitation.
words.ex_cn: 他毫不犹豫地去了那里。
words.en: To that place, thing, or matter.

words.ex: He lied, and thereupon he was punished.
words.ex_cn: 他撒了谎，因此受到了惩罚。
words.en: Immediately after that; as a result of that.

words.tr: adv. 与此；与之；随即；立即
words.ex: He signed the contract, therewith agreeing to the terms.
words.ex_cn: 他签署了合同，从而同意了条款。
words.en: Therewith is used to indicate that something happens immediately after something else or as a result of it.

words.ex: The thermocouple measures the temperature of the oven.
words.ex_cn: 热电偶测量烤箱的温度。
words.en: A thermocouple is a device for measuring temperature, consisting of a pair of wires of different metals connected at two points, a voltage being developed between the two junctions in proportion to the temperature difference.

words.ex: He is learning thermodynamics in physics class.
words.ex_cn: 他正在物理课上学习热力学。
words.en: Thermodynamics is the branch of physical science that deals with the relations between heat and other forms of energy (such as mechanical, electrical, or chemical energy), and, by extension, of the relationships between all forms of energy.

words.ex: The sun produces energy through thermonuclear reactions.
words.ex_cn: 太阳通过热核反应产生能量。
words.en: Thermonuclear refers to the process or phenomena that involve the fusion of atomic nuclei at very high temperatures, as in the sun or in a hydrogen bomb.

words.ex: They made their way through the dense thicket.
words.ex_cn: 他们穿过浓密的灌木丛。
words.en: A thicket is a dense group of bushes or trees.

words.ex: The rabbit ate a thistle in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在花园里吃了一株蓟。
words.en: A thistle is a wild plant which has leaves with sharp points and purple flowers.

words.ex: His coat is threadbare from many years of use.
words.ex_cn: 他的外套因为用了多年而变得破旧。
words.en: Worn out by overuse; shabby and old.

words.tr:
v. 跳动；悸动；颤动
n. 跳动；搏动；悸动
words.ex: His heart throbbed with fear.
words.ex_cn: 他的心脏因恐惧而跳动。
words.en: If part of your body throbs, you feel a series of strong and usually painful beats there.

words.ex: The mechanic checked the throttle on the car engine.
words.ex_cn: 机械师检查了汽车发动机的节流阀。
words.en: To throttle someone means to kill or injure them by squeezing their throat or tightening something around it and preventing them from breathing. A throttle is a device that controls the amount of fuel going into an engine.

words.tr: n. 工作量；生产量；吞吐量
words.ex: The factory increased its throughput last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂上个月提高了工作量。
words.en: The amount of work or goods produced by a machine, system, or factory in a given period of time.

words.tr:
v. 发出砰的一声
n. 重击声；砰的一声
words.ex: The book fell to the floor with a thud.
words.ex_cn: 书掉到地板上，发出一声闷响。
words.en: A thud is a dull sound, such as that which a heavy object makes when it hits something soft.

words.ex: The thug stole the wallet from the man.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍从那人身上偷了钱包。
words.en: A thug is a violent person, especially a criminal.

words.ex: A loud thunderclap woke me up.
words.ex_cn: 一声响亮的雷声把我吵醒了。
words.en: A thunderclap is the sudden loud noise that comes from the sky during a storm.

words.tr: adj. 雷声隆隆的；雷鸣般的
words.ex: The audience gave a thunderous applause.
words.ex_cn: 观众们报以雷鸣般的掌声。
words.en: If you describe a noise as thunderous, you mean that it is very loud and deep.

words.ex: Thy book is on the table.
words.ex_cn: 你的书在桌子上。
words.en: Used as the possessive form of 'thou', equivalent to 'your' in modern English.

words.ex: He takes medicine for his thyroid.
words.ex_cn: 他为甲状腺服用药物。
words.en: The thyroid is a large ductless gland in the neck that secretes hormones regulating growth and development through the rate of metabolism.

words.ex: The princess wore a shiny tiara at the ball.
words.ex_cn: 公主在舞会上戴着一顶闪亮的王冠。
words.en: A tiara is a jeweled, ornamental crown traditionally worn by women on formal occasions.

words.ex: The two companies made a tie-up to share resources.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司达成了合作以共享资源。
words.en: A tie-up is a connection or association between two or more things, especially a business partnership or collaboration.

words.ex: The teacher gave timely help when I was stuck.
words.ex_cn: 当我遇到困难时，老师及时提供了帮助。
words.en: done or occurring at a favorable or useful time; opportune.

words.tr: n. 火种；引火物；易燃物
words.ex: He swiped right on Tinder to find a date.
words.ex_cn: 他在Tinder上向右滑动以寻找约会对象。
words.en: Tinder is a dry, flammable material that can be used to start a fire.

words.tr: adj. 极小的；微小的；微量的；
words.ex: The tiny ant carried a big leaf.
words.ex_cn: 这只极小的蚂蚁搬着一片大叶子。
words.en: Very small in size or amount.

words.tr: n. 长篇抨击激烈演说
words.ex: He went on a tirade about slow internet.
words.ex_cn: 他大发雷霆，抱怨网速太慢。
words.en: A tirade is a long, angry speech of criticism or accusation.

words.ex: The titan built a huge bridge with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 这位巨人用手建造了一座巨大的桥。
words.en: A titan is someone or something that is extremely large, powerful, or important.

words.ex: Tom is a big tom cat that lives next door.
words.ex_cn: 汤姆是一只住在隔壁的大公猫。
words.en: A male animal, especially a male cat; also a given name for males.

words.ex: The song has a tonal melody that sounds harmonious.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌具有调性的旋律，听起来很和谐。
words.en: relating to or using tones or a scale of tones in music or art

words.ex: The topographer drew a detailed map of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 地形测绘员画了一张详细的山脉地图。
words.en: A topographer is a person who studies and describes the physical features of a place or region, especially by making maps.

words.ex: The wire shows torsion when twisted.
words.ex_cn: 当电线被扭转时，会出现扭转。
words.en: Torsion is the action of twisting or the state of being twisted, especially of one end of an object relative to the other.

words.tr:
adj. 极权主义的
n. 极权主义者
words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A totalitarian political system is one in which there is only one political party which controls everything and does not allow any opposition parties.

words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: Totalitarianism is a political system in which the state holds total authority over the society and seeks to control all aspects of public and private life wherever possible.

words.tr: n. 大片土地；体内管道；
words.ex: The farmer owns a large tract of land near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民拥有靠近河边的一大片土地。
words.en: A tract is a large area of land or a system of connected organs in the body.

words.tr: n. 悲剧作家；悲剧演员
words.ex: The tragedian performed a sad play on stage.
words.ex_cn: 这位悲剧演员在舞台上表演了一出悲伤的戏剧。
words.en: A tragedian is an actor who specializes in tragic roles or a writer who writes tragedies.

words.ex: The cows trample the grass in the field.
words.ex_cn: 牛在田野里践踏草地。
words.en: If someone tramples something or tramples on it, they step heavily and carelessly on it and damage it.

words.ex: The entrance to the building is on the left.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的入口在左边。
words.en: An entrance is a way into a place, such as a door or gate. It can also refer to the act of entering a place or the right to enter.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.tr:
adj. （尤指宗教或精神方面）超验的；超自然的
n. 超越数；超越物；抽象的普遍概念
words.ex: His transcendental philosophy influenced many thinkers.
words.ex_cn: 他的先验哲学影响了众多思想家。
words.en: Transcendental refers to something that is beyond ordinary or physical experience, often relating to spiritual or metaphysical realms.

words.ex: He believes in transcendentalism and loves nature.
words.ex_cn: 他相信超验主义，热爱自然。
words.en: Transcendentalism is a philosophical movement that developed in the late 1820s and 1830s in the eastern United States. It arose as a reaction to or protest against the general state of intellectualism and spirituality at the time.

words.ex: The lab technician transcribes the DNA sequence into RNA.
words.ex_cn: 实验室技术员将DNA序列转录成RNA。
words.en: To transcribe something means to write it down or to copy it from one form of recording to another.

words.tr: v. 使变形；使改观；美化
words.ex: The makeup artist transfigured the actress for the role.
words.ex_cn: 化妆师为演员的角色进行了改观。
words.en: To transform into something more beautiful or elevated.

words.ex: The doctor will transfuse blood to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 医生将给病人输血。
words.en: To transfer (as a fluid) into a vein or an artery of a person or animal; to instill or communicate gradually.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: The glass is translucent, so you can see light through it.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃是半透明的，所以你能看到光透过它。
words.en: If a material or substance is translucent, it is almost transparent, allowing some light to pass through it but not detailed shapes.

words.ex: The magic spell caused the transmutation of the frog into a prince.
words.ex_cn: 魔法咒语让青蛙变成了王子。
words.en: The act or process of changing something completely, especially into something different and better.

words.ex: The wizard can transmute lead into gold.
words.ex_cn: 巫师可以把铅变成金子。
words.en: To change something completely, especially into something different and better.

words.tr: v. 使掉换顺序；使转移；使换位
words.ex: You need to transpose the elements to solve the equation.
words.ex_cn: 你需要调换元素来解这个方程。
words.en: To transpose something means to change its order, position, or nature, especially in mathematics or music.

words.tr: n. 调换；变换；转位；转座
words.ex: The error was caused by a simple transposition of digits.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是由于简单的数字调换造成的。
words.en: The act of changing the order or position of something.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.ex: The king suffered from treachery by his own friend.
words.ex_cn: 国王被自己朋友背叛了。
words.en: Treachery is behavior that involves betraying someone's trust or being disloyal.

words.tr:
adj. 三部分的；三方的；三倍的
n. 三倍；最高音部；高音
v. 成为三倍；使增至三倍
words.ex: The pie has a treble layer of chocolate.
words.ex_cn: 这个派有三层巧克力。
words.en: Treble can be used as an adjective to describe something that is three times as much or as many, as a noun to refer to the highest range of musical notes, or as a verb to mean to make or become three times as much or as many.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a strong tremor in the building.
words.ex_cn: 地震使大楼发生了强烈的震动。
words.en: A tremor is a small earthquake or a shaking or vibrating movement, especially one caused by fear or nervousness.

words.ex: He walked over the wooden trestle.
words.ex_cn: 他走过木制的支架。
words.en: A trestle is a framework consisting of a horizontal beam supported by two pairs of sloping legs, used in pairs to support a flat surface such as a tabletop.

words.tr:
n. 颤声；颤音；啭鸣
v. 发颤声；啭鸣；发短促的响声
words.ex: The bird sang a beautiful trill.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿唱出了一段优美的颤声。
words.en: A trill is a musical effect where a note is alternated rapidly with the note above it.

words.ex: He watched the Harry Potter trilogy last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他上周末看了《哈利·波特》三部曲。
words.en: A trilogy is a series of three books, plays, or films that have the same subject or the same characters.

words.tr: n. 小装饰品；廉价首饰
words.ex: She bought a small trinket at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上买了一个小饰物。
words.en: A trinket is a small ornament or item of jewelry that is of little value.

words.ex: He put the camera on a tripod.
words.ex_cn: 他把相机放在三脚架上。
words.en: A tripod is a three-legged stand or support, especially for a camera or telescope.

words.ex: The tripper bought a souvenir at the market.
words.ex_cn: 这个旅行者在市场买了一件纪念品。
words.en: A person who travels or visits a place for pleasure; someone who stumbles or trips; a person who uses hallucinogenic drugs.

words.ex: The team trounced their rivals in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在决赛中大胜对手。
words.en: To defeat someone decisively in a competition or fight.

words.tr: v. 缓慢滚动；缓缓行进；艰难移动
words.ex: The boy trundles his toy car down the hallway.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把他的玩具车在走廊里推着走。
words.en: To move slowly and noisily, especially of a wheeled vehicle or object.

words.ex: He will try out for the soccer team tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天将参加足球队的选拔。
words.en: A tryout is an opportunity to show that you are suitable for a particular job or activity, especially in sports or acting.

words.tr: n. 大号（低音铜管乐器）
words.ex: He plays the tuba in the school band.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校乐队里吹大号。
words.en: A tuba is a large, low-pitched brass musical instrument that is played by blowing into a mouthpiece and pressing valves to change the pitch.

words.ex: The pipe is tubular and long.
words.ex_cn: 这根管道是管状的，很长。
words.en: Something that is tubular is shaped like a tube or is made of tubes.

words.ex: A tuft of grass grew by the fence.
words.ex_cn: 一簇草长在篱笆旁边。
words.en: A tuft is a small bunch of grass, hair, feathers, or other similar material, held or growing together at the base.

words.tr: adj. 浑浊的；污浊不清的；
words.ex: The river water looks turbid after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后河水看起来浑浊。
words.en: If you describe something as turbid, you mean that it is cloudy, dirty, or muddy.

words.ex: The wind turbine spins to make electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风力涡轮机旋转以发电。
words.en: A turbine is a machine or engine which uses a stream of air, gas, water, or steam to turn a wheel and produce power.

words.ex: The chef cooked a fresh turbot for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 厨师为晚餐烹制了一条新鲜的比目鱼。
words.en: A turbot is a large flatfish that is highly valued as food.

words.tr: n. 参与人（数）；装束；产量；清理
words.ex: The turnout for the election was very high.
words.ex_cn: 这次选举的投票率很高。
words.en: The number of people attending or participating in an event, especially a political meeting or election.

words.ex: The castle has a small turret on each corner.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡的每个角落都有一个小塔。
words.en: A turret is a small tower on top of a building, especially a castle, or a structure on a military vehicle that can turn around and from which guns are fired.

words.ex: He learned piano under his teacher's tutelage.
words.ex_cn: 他在老师的指导下学习钢琴。
words.en: The act of guarding, protecting, or guiding; the office or function of a guardian; guardianship; protection; as, the king's right of seigniory and tutelage.

words.tr:
v. （使）旋转；快速转动
n. 扭转；旋转的东西
words.ex: The dancer twirls gracefully on stage.
words.ex_cn: 舞者在舞台上优雅地旋转。
words.en: To spin around quickly or to twist something around with your fingers.

words.ex: He twitched the rope to pull the box closer.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地一拉绳子，把箱子拉近了些。
words.en: To make a sudden, small movement with a part of your body, especially because you are nervous or in pain.

words.tr: adj. 排字上的；印刷上的
words.ex: The typo was a typographical error.
words.ex_cn: 这个拼写错误是一个排版错误。
words.en: Relating to the arrangement, appearance, or style of printed matter.

words.tr: n. 印刷术；排印；印刷样式
words.ex: He loves good typography in books.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢书中的好排版。
words.en: The art or process of setting and arranging types and printing from them.

words.tr: adj. 暴虐的；压制的；残暴的
words.ex: The tyrannical king punished people for small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 这个暴虐的国王因为小错误惩罚人民。
words.en: Using power in a cruel and unfair way over people in a country or group.

words.ex: He tries to tyrannize his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图欺压他的弟弟。
words.en: To rule or govern someone or something in a cruel and oppressive way.

words.ex: The doctor used ultrasound to check the baby.
words.ex_cn: 医生用超声波检查了婴儿。
words.en: Ultrasound is sound which is very high and cannot be heard by humans, used in medical examinations to produce images of the inside of the body.

words.tr: adj. 不在乎的；不害臊的；不难为情的
words.ex: He was unabashed about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的错误毫不在意。
words.en: If you describe someone as unabashed, you mean that they are not ashamed, embarrassed, or shy about something, especially something that might make other people feel uncomfortable.

words.tr: adj. 不衰退的；不减弱的
words.ex: The storm continued unabated throughout the night.
words.ex_cn: 风暴整夜未减。
words.en: If something continues unabated, it continues without any reduction in intensity or strength.

words.tr: adj. 无法解释的；不能理解的；无责任的
words.ex: The manager made unaccountable decisions.
words.ex_cn: 这位经理做出了无法解释的决定。
words.en: If someone or something is unaccountable, there is no way of explaining why they behave in a particular way, and it is often strange or surprising.

words.ex: He remained unaffected by the noise.
words.ex_cn: 他没有受到噪音的影响。
words.en: If someone or something is unaffected by an event or occurrence, they are not changed by it in any way.

words.tr: adv. 出其不意地；突然地；不知不觉地
words.ex: He caught the thief unawares.
words.ex_cn: 他出其不意地抓住了小偷。
words.en: If something happens unawares, it happens without someone realizing it or expecting it.

words.tr: adj. 不恰当的；不得体的；无吸引力的
words.ex: It is unbecoming to shout at teachers.
words.ex_cn: 对老师大喊大叫是不合适的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or remarks as unbecoming, you mean that they are shocking and unsuitable for that person.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

words.tr: adj. 不拘礼仪的；随意的；无礼的；唐突的
words.ex: He left the meeting in an unceremonious way.
words.ex_cn: 他以一种不拘礼节的方式离开了会议。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as unceremonious, you mean it is done in a sudden, rude, or informal way without any regard for formalities or politeness.

words.tr: adj. 不让步的；不妥协的；强硬的
words.ex: He is uncompromising about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他在诚实方面毫不妥协。
words.en: If you describe someone as uncompromising, you mean that they are determined not to change their opinions or aims in any way.

words.tr: v. 学习成绩低于智力测验得分；未展现实力；未发挥水平
words.ex: He underachieves because he doesn't try hard.
words.ex_cn: 他没有努力，所以表现不佳。
words.en: To perform less well or achieve less success than expected or is possible.

words.ex: The deer hid in the underbrush.
words.ex_cn: 鹿藏在矮树丛里。
words.en: Underbrush refers to the dense growth of shrubs and other plants beneath the trees in a forest.

words.tr:
v. 少要价钱；少算价钱；填充不足
n. 低的索价；填不够量的火药；充电不足
words.ex: The mechanic undercharged me for the repair work.
words.ex_cn: 修理工给我的修理工作索价低于常价。
words.en: To charge someone less than the correct or usual amount for something.

words.ex: The new policy undercut the company's profits.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策削弱了公司的利润。
words.en: To undercut means to sell something at a lower price than a competitor, or to weaken something or someone.

words.tr:
adj. 半生不熟的；煮得嫩的
v. 使煮得嫩；使做得不够；不尽全力做；“underdo”的过去分词
words.ex: The steak is underdone.
words.ex_cn: 这块牛排还没熟。
words.en: If food is underdone, it has not been cooked for long enough and is not ready to eat.

words.ex: The deer walked through the thick undergrowth.
words.ex_cn: 鹿穿过了茂密的矮树丛。
words.en: Undergrowth refers to the dense growth of shrubs and other plants beneath the trees in a forest.

words.tr:
adj. 秘密的；阴险的；下投的
adv. 低手地；秘密地
words.ex: He made an underhand deal to hide the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他秘密地做了一笔交易来掩盖真相。
words.en: If an action is underhand, it is done secretly and sometimes dishonestly in order to achieve something.

words.tr: v. 构成…的基础（或起因）
words.ex: Poor diet underlies many health problems.
words.ex_cn: 不良饮食是许多健康问题的根源。
words.en: If something underlies a situation or activity, it is the cause or basis of it.

words.ex: The manager yelled at his underling for making a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 经理因为下属犯了错误而对他大喊大叫。
words.en: An underling is a person who is lower in rank or position than someone else, especially in a work environment.

words.tr: n. （铁路或公路下的）地下通道
words.ex: The dog ran under the underpass.
words.ex_cn: 狗从立交桥下跑过去了。
words.en: An underpass is a road or path that goes under another road or a railway.

words.tr: adj. 弱势的；下层社会的；贫困的
words.ex: The school helps underprivileged children learn to read.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校帮助弱势儿童学习阅读。
words.en: People who are underprivileged lack the advantages that other people have, such as enough money or a good standard of living.

words.tr: v. 以低于市价售出；抛售
words.ex: The store undersells other shops by lowering prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店通过降价来以低于市价售出商品。
words.en: To sell something at a lower price than competitors or to undervalue something.

words.ex: The underside of the table is dirty.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的下侧很脏。
words.en: The underside of something is the part of it which normally faces towards the ground or is not normally seen.

words.tr:
n. 候补演员
v. 练习当候补演员
words.ex: He is the understudy for the main actor.
words.ex_cn: 他是主角的替补演员。
words.en: An understudy is an actor who learns the part of another actor in a play so that they can take their place if necessary.

words.tr:
adv. 在水下；
adj. 水下的；
words.ex: The divers swam underwater to explore the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 潜水员在水下游泳以探索珊瑚礁。
words.en: Located, occurring, or used beneath the surface of the water.

words.tr: adj. 无尊严的；不成体统的；不体面的；不庄重的
words.ex: He felt undignified wearing pajamas to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得穿睡衣去开会很失体面。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as undignified, you mean they are foolish or embarrassing.

words.ex: He achieved an undreamt-of success in his first year.
words.ex_cn: 他在第一年就取得了前所未有的成功。
words.en: Something that is undreamt-of is something that has not been imagined or thought possible.

words.ex: He faced undue pressure from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他受到了来自老板的过度压力。
words.en: If you describe something bad as undue, you mean that it is greater or more extreme than you think is reasonable or appropriate.

words.tr:
v. 使波动；使起伏
adj. 波动的；起伏的
words.ex: The hills undulate gently in the distance.
words.ex_cn: 远处的山丘轻轻起伏。
words.en: To move or cause to move in a smooth, wavelike motion.

words.ex: He was unduly harsh on his son.
